## 4. pages vs chunks vs facts vs takes vs "entities"; the schema-pack system

- **page** = one markdown file = one row. Two-layer body split at a `<!-- timeline -->` sentinel by `splitBody()` (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/markdown.ts:367`): everything above → `pages.compiled_truth` (always-current synthesis), everything below → `pages.timeline` (append-only evidence log). YAML frontmatter → `pages.frontmatter JSONB`. `page_kind ∈ {markdown, code, image}` is orthogonal to `type`.
- **chunk** = retrieval unit derived from `compiled_truth` after the chunker strips fences. Re-chunked when `content_hash` changes. Code chunks carry tree-sitter symbol metadata; image chunks carry `modality='image'` + a 1024-d Voyage vector.
- **take** = an epistemic claim with an explicit *holder*. Canonical form is a markdown fence (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/takes-fence.ts`): `## Takes` between `<!--- gbrain:takes:begin -->` / `:end -->`, columns `| # | claim | kind | who | weight | since | source |`. Append-only `row_num` so cross-page refs `slug#N` and `synthesis_evidence` never break; supersession is `~~strikethrough~~` + a new row. Holder semantics are strict: *"Did this person SAY or CLEARLY IMPLY this? YES → holder = people/slug; NO, it's your analysis of them → holder = brain."*
- **fact** = hot, single-user, per-turn conversational memory. Fence in `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/facts-fence.ts`: `<!--- gbrain:facts:begin -->` with 10 data columns `| # | claim | kind | confidence | visibility | notability | valid_from | valid_until | source | context |`. Strikethrough + `context: superseded by #N` vs `context: forgotten: <reason>` are distinguished semantically; `forgotten` maps to `valid_until = today` so `expired_at` re-derives on rebuild.
- **The bridge is one-way** (`docs/takes-vs-facts.md`): `hot facts → [dream consolidate] → cold takes`, stamping `consolidated_at` + `consolidated_into`.

**There is no `entities` table.** This is the single most important correction to the docs. `docs/GBRAIN_RECOMMENDED_SCHEMA.md:82` describes an aspirational "Entity registry — canonical ID, all aliases, all external IDs … in one table," but the implementation makes **`pages` the entity registry**: an entity is a page under `people/` or `companies/` with `type='person'|'company'`. `facts.entity_slug` and `takes.holder` are plain TEXT slug references with **no foreign key**. Grepping `CREATE TABLE … entit` across `schema.sql`, `migrate.ts`, and `pglite-schema.ts` returns zero hits.

**Schema packs** (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/schema-pack/`) are how custom page types are defined — YAML/JSON manifests, `api_version: gbrain-schema-pack-v1`, validated with zod in `manifest-v1.ts`. Key mechanics:

The comment spells out why: *"This prevents adversary-profile (entity primitive) from surfacing in `whoknows expert` just because it shares a primitive with person."*

Extends chain: warn at depth >4, hard reject at >8. Cache is keyed by pack *name* with a 1000ms stat-TTL gate and reverse-extends-graph invalidation cascade.

## 5. Graph model

**Storage.** Wikilinks are extracted by the pure functions in `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/link-extraction.ts` and persisted as `links` rows. Provenance is the design center — `link_source` is an **open kebab-case tag, not a closed allowlist** (v114/#1941), with reconciliation-managed built-ins: `markdown`, `frontmatter`, `mentions`, `wikilink-resolved`, plus user-facing `manual`. The op layer (`operations.ts`) forbids callers passing the four managed built-ins even though the DB CHECK admits them, because *"a CLI-forged 'frontmatter' row with NULL origin would be a phantom edge reconciliation never cleans."* Reconciliation on `put_page` filters by `(link_source='frontmatter' AND origin_page_id = written_page)` so it never touches other pages' edges.

**Resolution.** `[[source:slug]]` → `resolution_type='qualified'`; bare `[[slug]]` → local-first fallback, `resolution_type='unqualified'`. Aliases short-circuit at read time via `engine.resolveSlugWithAlias` (`postgres-engine.ts:5679`) querying `slug_aliases` ordered by `array_position(sources, source_id)`. Opt-in global-basename resolution (`link_resolution.global_basename`, issue #972) stamps `link_type='wikilink_basename'` + `link_source='wikilink-resolved'`. Staleness is watermarked: `LINK_EXTRACTOR_VERSION_TS = '2026-08-01T00:00:00Z'` — a page is stale when `links_extracted_at IS NULL OR links_extracted_at < LINK_EXTRACTOR_VERSION_TS OR updated_at > links_extracted_at`.

**Yes, real recursive-CTE traversal.** Three distinct queries:

`traverseGraph(slug, depth=5, opts)` (`postgres-engine.ts:3244`, mirrored at `pglite-engine.ts:3091`) — array-based cycle prevention, source-scope filters at seed/step/aggregation, optional per-iteration frontier cap:
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE graph AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.slug, p.title, p.type, 0 as depth, ARRAY[p.id] as visited
  FROM pages p WHERE p.slug = $1 <seedScope>
  UNION ALL
  SELECT p2.id, p2.slug, p2.title, p2.type, g.depth + 1, g.visited || p2.id
  FROM graph g
  JOIN links l ON l.from_page_id = g.id
  JOIN pages p2 ON p2.id = l.to_page_id
  WHERE g.depth < $2 AND NOT (p2.id = ANY(g.visited)) <stepScope>
)
SELECT DISTINCT g.slug, g.title, g.type, g.depth,
  coalesce((SELECT jsonb_agg(DISTINCT jsonb_build_object('to_slug', p3.slug, 'link_type', l2.link_type))
            FROM links l2 JOIN pages p3 ON p3.id = l2.to_page_id
            WHERE l2.from_page_id = g.id <aggScope>), '[]'::jsonb) as links
FROM graph g ORDER BY g.depth, g.slug
```

`traversePaths(slug, {depth, linkType, direction: 'in'|'out'|'both'})` — returns edges (from_slug, to_slug, link_type, context, depth) rather than nodes; the `'both'` branch scopes both endpoint joins.

`relationalFanout(seeds[], opts)` (`postgres-engine.ts:3477`) — the retrieval-integrated one, injecting edge-derived answers into RRF fusion. Depth clamped `[1,3]`, limit clamped `[1,200]`, `mentions` edges excluded unless `includeMentions`. Notably it enforces **strict within-source traversal** even when several sources are in read scope, via `AND p2.source_id = w.seed_source`, and carries a full path array:
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE walk AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.slug, p.source_id, 0::int AS depth,
         ARRAY[p.id] AS visited, ARRAY[p.slug] AS path,
         p.source_id AS seed_source, NULL::text AS last_link_type
  FROM pages p WHERE p.slug = ANY($seeds::text[]) <seedScope> AND p.deleted_at IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT p2.id, p2.slug, p2.source_id, w.depth + 1, w.visited || p2.id, w.path || p2.slug,
         w.seed_source, l.link_type
  FROM walk w <recurStep>
  WHERE w.depth < $depth AND NOT (p2.id = ANY(w.visited))
    AND p2.source_id = w.seed_source AND p2.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND l.link_source IS DISTINCT FROM 'mentions' <typeFilter>
)
SELECT n.source_id, n.slug, MIN(n.depth) AS hop,
       COUNT(DISTINCT n.last_link_type) AS edge_count,
       array_agg(DISTINCT n.last_link_type) FILTER (WHERE n.last_link_type IS NOT NULL) AS via_link_types,
       (array_agg(array_to_string(n.path, chr(9)) ORDER BY n.depth ASC, array_length(n.path,1) ASC))[1] AS path_str,
       (SELECT cc.id FROM content_chunks cc WHERE cc.page_id = n.id ORDER BY cc.chunk_index ASC LIMIT 1) AS canonical_chunk_id
FROM walk n WHERE n.depth > 0
GROUP BY n.source_id, n.slug, n.id
ORDER BY hop ASC, edge_count DESC, n.source_id ASC, n.slug ASC LIMIT $limit
```

Ranking hook: `getBacklinkCounts` excludes `link_source='mentions'` using NULL-safe `IS DISTINCT FROM`, because auto-linked mentions are *"graph-completeness signal, NOT human-intent signal"* and counting them would globally shift search ranking on the first `--by-mention` run.

Separately, code has its own graph: `code_edges_chunk` ∪ `code_edges_symbol` with `getCalleesOf` / `code-callers` traversal and a `code_traversal_cache`.

## 6. Identity, dedup, and merge

There is **no entity-merge primitive** — no `merge_pages` op, no `gbrain merge` command (grep for `merge_pages|mergePages` returns nothing in `operations.ts` or `src/commands/`). Identity is instead handled by four cooperating layers, all slug-centric:

**(a) `resolveEntitySlug(engine, source_id, raw)`** — `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/entities/resolve.ts`. The canonicalization chain at fact-extraction time, with an explicitly documented failure mode:
1. Exact slug match (if `raw` contains `/` or matches a `pages.slug` row).
2. **Bare-name prefix expansion** — for single-token names, `slug LIKE 'people/<token>-%'` then `'companies/<token>-%'`, resolving *only* when exactly one candidate matches. Rationale: *"Bare first names like 'Alice' score too low on pg_trgm (short strings have terrible trigram overlap), so without this step they fall through to slugify('Alice') → 'alice', which spawns a phantom `people/alice.md` stub."* Collisions deliberately fall through rather than guess by connection count.
3. **pg_trgm fuzzy match** against `pages.slug` + `pages.title`, source-scoped, case-insensitive — multi-token input only. Bare names skip this arm because *"a shared first name is not specific enough to choose one person by trigram score or popularity."*
4. Deterministic slugify fallback. Bug #3447 fix: path-shaped input is slugified **per segment**, since naive slugify would corrupt `people/alice-example` → `people-alice-example`, a slug no page can ever have, causing infinite re-minting.

A variant returns a tagged resolution source (`exact_page` | `fuzzy_match` | `fallback_slugify`) for trajectory routing.

**(b) `page_aliases`** — free-text name → canonical slug, for *search*. `alias_norm` is `normalizeAlias()` output (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/search/alias-normalize.ts`). Populated from frontmatter `aliases:` at import, backfilled by `gbrain reindex --aliases` (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/commands/reindex-aliases.ts`) via `engine.setPageAliases` (replace-set semantics = idempotent). The unique key `(source_id, alias_norm, slug)` deliberately allows a *second* page to claim the same alias — collisions are reported and resolved at query time rather than blocked at write. This is where `"[REDACTED_EMAIL]"` would live if declared in `people/john-smith.md`'s frontmatter, but **there is no automatic email/phone/external-ID identity index** — nothing parses emails into an identifier table.

**(c) `slug_aliases`** — slug → slug *redirect*, for wikilinks. Populated by the `page_to_alias` unify-types handler (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/schema-pack/page-to-alias.ts`), which converted a 5.5K-page `concept-redirect` cluster in a production brain. Deliberately does **not** rewrite body text: *"the alias_table IS the resolver — engine.resolveSlugWithAlias short-circuits wikilinks like [[old-concept-name]] to the canonical at read time. Rewriting body-text would destroy historical spelling/context."* Crash-safe via "soft-delete LAST" ordering + `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on the unique constraint.

**(d) Content-level dedup**, not identity: `importFromFile` detects duplicates by `content_hash` OR external `frontmatter.id` (granola UUID etc.) and warns when *"content_hash matches but identity differs"* (`import-file.ts:651`). Facts dedup via `idx_facts_ontology_dedup` on `value_hash`; takes dedup at consolidation via HNSW similarity over `takes.embedding`; contradictions surfaced (not merged) by `gbrain eval suspected-contradictions` with a persistent `eval_contradictions_cache` keyed on `(chunk_a_hash, chunk_b_hash, model_id, prompt_version, truncation_policy)`.

**Bottom line on merge:** the doc's claim that "identity resolution becomes a database operation (merge entity IDs)" is not implemented. The shipped model is: one page per entity, aliases as indirection tables, and slug canonicalization at write time — with an explicit design bias toward *refusing to guess* (ambiguous bare names fall through to a guarded holding path rather than merge into the wrong entity).</result>

# gbrain storage layer & data model — technical report

## 1. Substrate: git-backed markdown is canonical; Postgres is a derived cache

This is stated as a hard architectural contract in `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/docs/architecture/system-of-record.md:1`:

> **The GitHub repo (markdown + frontmatter) is the system of record. The Postgres/PGLite database is a derived cache. We do not back up the database — we rebuild it from the repo.**

**Sync direction is FS → DB, with one narrow DB → FS write-back.**

- **FS → DB (primary):** `gbrain sync` runs `git diff --name-status -M LAST..HEAD` against the source's checkout (`sources.local_path` / `config.sync.repo_path`), parses it into a `SyncManifest {added, modified, deleted, renamed}` (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/sync.ts:20`), filters via `isSyncable()`, maps paths→slugs via `pathToSlug()`, and imports each file through `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/import-file.ts`. Sync watermark is `sources.last_commit` + `sources.last_sync_at`; forced full re-walks trigger when `sources.chunker_version != CURRENT_CHUNKER_VERSION`.
- **DB → FS (narrow):** `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/write-through.ts` renders a DB row back to markdown via `serializePageToMarkdown` and atomically (`.tmp` + `rename`) writes it into the repo. This fires only for the `put_page` op and `gbrain brainstorm/lsd --save`. Its own header states the invariant: *"The file is rendered FROM the DB row, so the two sinks cannot diverge."* Optionally git-commits via `commitWriteThroughFile` on repos hardened by `gbrain sources harden`.

**Conflict resolution is content-hash idempotence, not merge.** `importFromFile` computes a `content_hash` over parsed content (excluding timestamp-bearing frontmatter, `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/import-file.ts:544`) and short-circuits at `:635`:

```ts
if (existing?.content_hash === hash && !opts.forceRechunk) { … }
```

There is no three-way merge — the file wins, unconditionally. Post-write there's a read-back verifier that raises a *"Silent desync — DB index has a stale row"* error if `readBack.content_hash !== expectedHash` (`:1026`). Cross-machine concurrency is delegated to git ("Multi-machine sync is git").

**Three-category table taxonomy** (system-of-record.md:41): *FS-canonical* (takes, facts, links, timeline_entries, tags, `pages.emotional_weight`, synthesis_evidence — each with a named markdown encoding and a reconciler), *derived-from-FS* (`pages`, `content_chunks`, `page_versions`), and *DB-only by design* (raw_data, subagent_*, oauth_*, mcp_request_log, minion_*, eval_*, dream_verdicts, cycle locks, some `config` keys). A CI gate `scripts/check-system-of-record.sh` fails PRs that add direct writes to derived tables outside the reconciler layer.

DR is literally `DELETE FROM facts; DELETE FROM takes; DELETE FROM links; DELETE FROM timeline_entries;` then `gbrain sync && gbrain extract all`, pinned by `test/e2e/system-of-record-invariant.test.ts`.

**Binary blobs never go in the DB.** `files.storage_path` references a path in the brain repo; `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/storage.ts` defines a separate pluggable `StorageBackend` (`local` / `s3` / `supabase`) for binary object storage with `upload/download/delete/exists/list/getUrl`.

## 2. The actual DB schema

Canonical Postgres DDL: `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/schema.sql` (1442 lines) → codegen'd into `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/schema-embedded.ts` (`// AUTO-GENERATED — do not edit. Run: bun run build:schema`). PGLite mirror: `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/pglite-schema.ts` (1124 lines, explicit `DRIFT WARNING` comment). Everything else arrives via `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/migrate.ts` — **125 numbered migrations**, ledgered as the `config` table row `key='version'` (not a `schema_migrations` table): `runMigrations` reads `await engine.getConfig('version')` (`migrate.ts:5947`).

~60 tables total. The load-bearing ones:

### `pages` — the core content table
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pages (
  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  source_id     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default' REFERENCES sources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  slug          TEXT NOT NULL,
  type          TEXT NOT NULL,
  page_kind     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'markdown' CHECK (page_kind IN ('markdown','code','image')),
  title         TEXT NOT NULL,
  compiled_truth TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  timeline      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  frontmatter   JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  content_hash  TEXT,
  emotional_weight REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.0,
  created_at, updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  deleted_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,                    -- soft delete, 72h purge window
  effective_date TIMESTAMPTZ, effective_date_source TEXT, import_filename TEXT,
  salience_touched_at TIMESTAMPTZ, last_retrieved_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  links_extracted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,               -- extraction freshness watermark
  contextual_retrieval_mode TEXT, corpus_generation TEXT,
  generation    BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  CONSTRAINT pages_source_slug_key UNIQUE (source_id, slug)
);
```
Plus (migration v58, `migrate.ts:2720`) `source_path TEXT` — import-time repo-relative path, so sync's delete/rename path can map file→row; and (v81) `source_kind`, `source_uri`, `ingested_via`, `ingested_at`. Also `search_vector tsvector` added by `ALTER TABLE` at the bottom of the schema.

Indexes: `idx_pages_type`, `idx_pages_frontmatter` (GIN on JSONB), `idx_pages_trgm` (GIN `title gin_trgm_ops`), `idx_pages_source_id`, `idx_pages_search` (GIN on tsvector), `pages_deleted_at_purge_idx` (partial), `pages_coalesce_date_idx` (expression index on `COALESCE(effective_date, updated_at)`), `pages_last_retrieved_at_idx`, `pages_links_extracted_at_idx (source_id, links_extracted_at)`, `pages_source_path_idx` (partial).

Two generation-clock mechanisms for cache invalidation:
- Row-level `bump_page_generation_trg` (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE) — on INSERT sets `MAX(generation)+1`; on UPDATE bumps only when one of a 10-column allow-list `IS DISTINCT FROM` (compiled_truth, timeline, frontmatter, deleted_at, contextual_retrieval_mode, title, type, page_kind, corpus_generation, content_hash).
- Statement-level `bump_page_generation_clock_trg` (AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE FOR EACH STATEMENT) → `PERFORM nextval('page_generation_clock_seq')`. Comment: *"nextval() takes a microsecond LWLock, not a transaction-length row lock."* `page_generation_clock` table is retained for name compat; Layer-1 reads `last_value`.

### `content_chunks` — chunk grain + embeddings
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS content_chunks (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  page_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  chunk_index INTEGER NOT NULL,
  chunk_text  TEXT NOT NULL,
  chunk_source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'compiled_truth',
  embedding   vector(1536),                      -- rewritten to configured dims at init
  model       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'text-embedding-3-large',
  token_count INTEGER, embedded_at TIMESTAMPTZ, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  language TEXT, symbol_name TEXT, symbol_type TEXT, start_line INTEGER, end_line INTEGER,
  parent_symbol_path TEXT[], doc_comment TEXT, symbol_name_qualified TEXT,
  search_vector TSVECTOR,
  modality TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'text',
  embedding_image      vector(1024),             -- Voyage multimodal
  embedding_multimodal vector(1024)              -- unified cross-modal column
);
```
The literal `vector(1536)` / `'text-embedding-3-large'` are template placeholders — `getPostgresSchema(dims, model)` (`postgres-engine.ts:101`) does `.replace(/vector\(1536\)/g, ...)`; PGLite uses `__EMBEDDING_DIMS__` / `__EMBEDDING_MODEL__` tokens. Default is **`zeroentropyai:zembed-1` @ 1280 dims** (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/ai/defaults.ts:20`), not OpenAI.

`content_chunks` has **no `updated_at`** — chunks are re-INSERTed on page change, never UPDATEd.

### `links` — the graph edge table
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  from_page_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  to_page_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  link_type    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  context      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  link_source  TEXT CHECK (link_source IS NULL OR (link_source ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$' AND char_length(link_source) <= 64)),
  link_kind    TEXT CHECK (link_kind IS NULL OR link_kind IN ('plain','typed_ner')),
  origin_page_id INTEGER REFERENCES pages(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  origin_field   TEXT,
  resolution_type TEXT CHECK (resolution_type IS NULL OR resolution_type IN ('qualified','unqualified')),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT links_from_to_type_source_origin_unique
    UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (from_page_id, to_page_id, link_type, link_source, origin_page_id)
);
```
`CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW page_links AS SELECT id, from_page_id, to_page_id FROM links;` — deliberately narrow projection so the alias can't block `ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN`.

## 3. Engines: PGLite vs Postgres — what actually differs

Interface: `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/engine.ts` (2285 lines — far larger than the doc's 37-method sketch in ENGINES.md). Discriminator: `readonly kind: 'postgres' | 'pglite'`. Factory with dynamic imports in `engine-factory.ts`.

**Same:** both are real Postgres. Same SQL for FTS, vector, trigram, recursive CTEs. `PGLiteEngine` = Postgres 17.5 in WASM via `@electric-sql/pglite` with `extensions: { vector, pg_trgm }` (`pglite-engine.ts:307`).

**Vector indexing (both engines):**
- **HNSW only. No ivfflat anywhere in the codebase.** `CREATE INDEX idx_chunks_embedding ON content_chunks USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);`
- Dimension-gated index emission — `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/vector-index.ts:19`: `PGVECTOR_HNSW_VECTOR_MAX_DIMS = 2000`, `PGVECTOR_HNSW_HALFVEC_MAX_DIMS = 4000`. Above the cap the DDL degrades to a comment: *"idx_chunks_embedding skipped: pgvector HNSW vector indexes support at most 2000 dimensions; exact vector scans remain available."*
- `halfvec` support: `facts.embedding` and `query_cache.embedding` are emitted as `halfvec(N)` with `halfvec_cosine_ops` when configured (`migrate.ts:2291`, `:2891`).
- `hnswEfSearchFor(candidateLimit)` clamps `hnsw.ef_search` into `[40, 1000]` — shared by both engines because *"An HNSW index scan returns at most `hnsw.ef_search` rows (default 40) no matter what the query's LIMIT asks for."*
- Partial HNSW for images: `WHERE embedding_image IS NOT NULL`; partial HNSW for takes: `WHERE active AND embedding IS NOT NULL`.

**FTS (both engines, identical SQL):** two tsvector columns.
- `pages.search_vector` — trigger `update_page_search_vector()`, `setweight(to_tsvector('english', title),'A') || setweight(…timeline…,'C') || setweight(…aggregated timeline_entries text…,'C')`. Note `compiled_truth` is **deliberately excluded** (`pglite-schema.ts:1025`): *"#2704: compiled_truth (unbounded whole-page body) deliberately NOT indexed — overflows Postgres's 1MB tsvector cap on large pages."*
- `content_chunks.search_vector` — trigger `update_chunk_search_vector()`, weight A on `doc_comment` + `symbol_name_qualified`, weight B on `chunk_text`. Fires `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF chunk_text, doc_comment, symbol_name_qualified` only.
- Query side is `websearch_to_tsquery` + `ts_rank` (chunk grain) / `ts_rank_cd` (page grain), e.g. `postgres-engine.ts:1791`, `pglite-engine.ts:1689`. The config name is **not** hardcoded 'english': `getFtsLanguage()` (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/fts-language.ts`) reads `GBRAIN_FTS_LANGUAGE`, validated against `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/` because *"Postgres tsvector functions don't accept parameterized config names."* Migration v123 rewrites both trigger functions with the configured language.

**Real differences:**

| | PostgresEngine | PGLiteEngine |
|---|---|---|
| Driver | `postgres` (porsager) tagged templates | `db.query(sql, params)` positional |
| Schema source | `SCHEMA_SQL` (schema-embedded.ts) | `PGLITE_SCHEMA_SQL_TEMPLATE` |
| DDL lock | `SELECT pg_advisory_lock(42)` on the DDL connection | file lock via `pglite-lock.ts` (`acquireLock(dataDir)`); single-writer |
| Pooling | `ConnectionManager` dual-pool (pooler + direct), `withReservedConnection`, reconnect supervisor | none |
| RLS | `DO $$ … IF has_bypass THEN ALTER TABLE … ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` per table; opt-in `GBRAIN_RLS_SCOPE_BINDING=1` sets `app.scopes` via `set_config(…, true)` | absent |
| Index lifecycle | `dropZombieIndexes` (sweeps `pg_index.indisvalid=false`), `dropAndRebuild` (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` + atomic `ALTER INDEX … RENAME` swap), `monitorBuild` | all no-ops (`if (engine.kind !== 'postgres') return`) |
| Schema verify | `verifySchema()` self-heals missing columns (PgBouncer txn-mode silently dropping DDL) | n/a |
| `SET STORAGE EXTERNAL` on `minion_attachments.content` | applied (migration v7) | omitted |
| CJK search | – | `pglite-engine.ts:1845` bigram-frequency fallback when `websearch_to_tsquery('english')` degrades |
| Snapshot restore | – | `GBRAIN_PGLITE_SNAPSHOT` fast-restore for in-memory engines |

**The JSONB double-encode trap** (`docs/ENGINES.md:224`) is the sharpest real divergence: `postgres.js` `.unsafe(sql, params)` binds a JS string as text, so a bare `$N::jsonb` cast wraps already-JSON text into a jsonb *scalar string*. PGLite's `db.query` parses text→jsonb natively **and hides the bug**. Sanctioned forms: `sql.json(obj)`, `executeRawJsonb`, or `$N::text::jsonb`. Two CI guards (`scripts/check-jsonb-pattern.sh`, `scripts/check-jsonb-params.mjs`).

## 4. pages vs chunks vs facts vs takes vs "entities"; the schema-pack system

- **page** = one markdown file = one row. Two-layer body split at a `<!-- timeline -->` sentinel by `splitBody()` (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/markdown.ts:367`): everything above → `pages.compiled_truth` (always-current synthesis), everything below → `pages.timeline` (append-only evidence log). YAML frontmatter → `pages.frontmatter JSONB`. `page_kind ∈ {markdown, code, image}` is orthogonal to `type`.
- **chunk** = retrieval unit derived from `compiled_truth` after the chunker strips fences. Re-chunked when `content_hash` changes. Code chunks carry tree-sitter symbol metadata; image chunks carry `modality='image'` + a 1024-d Voyage vector.
- **take** = an epistemic claim with an explicit *holder*. Canonical form is a markdown fence (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/takes-fence.ts`): `## Takes` between `<!--- gbrain:takes:begin -->` / `:end -->`, columns `| # | claim | kind | who | weight | since | source |`. Append-only `row_num` so cross-page refs `slug#N` and `synthesis_evidence` never break; supersession is `~~strikethrough~~` + a new row. Holder semantics are strict: *"Did this person SAY or CLEARLY IMPLY this? YES → holder = people/slug; NO, it's your analysis of them → holder = brain."*
- **fact** = hot, single-user, per-turn conversational memory. Fence in `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/facts-fence.ts`: `<!--- gbrain:facts:begin -->` with 10 data columns `| # | claim | kind | confidence | visibility | notability | valid_from | valid_until | source | context |`. Strikethrough + `context: superseded by #N` vs `context: forgotten: <reason>` are distinguished semantically; `forgotten` maps to `valid_until = today` so `expired_at` re-derives on rebuild.
- **The bridge is one-way** (`docs/takes-vs-facts.md`): `hot facts → [dream consolidate] → cold takes`, stamping `consolidated_at` + `consolidated_into`.

**There is no `entities` table.** This is the single most important correction to the docs. `docs/GBRAIN_RECOMMENDED_SCHEMA.md:82` describes an aspirational "Entity registry — canonical ID, all aliases, all external IDs … in one table," but the implementation makes **`pages` the entity registry**: an entity is a page under `people/` or `companies/` with `type='person'|'company'`. `facts.entity_slug` and `takes.holder` are plain TEXT slug references with **no foreign key**. Grepping `CREATE TABLE … entit` across `schema.sql`, `migrate.ts`, and `pglite-schema.ts` returns zero hits.

**Schema packs** (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/schema-pack/`) are how custom page types are defined — YAML/JSON manifests, `api_version: gbrain-schema-pack-v1`, validated with zod in `manifest-v1.ts`. Key mechanics:

- **Five closed primitives**: `PACK_PRIMITIVES = ['entity','media','temporal','annotation','concept']`. Packs cannot add primitives, only types extending one.
- A `page_types[]` entry carries `name`, `primitive`, `path_prefixes[]` (drives `inferType` from file path — *first match wins, manifest order is priority*), `aliases[]`, `extractable` (`boolean | ExtractableSpec` with `prompt_template`/`fixture_corpus`/`eval_dimensions`/`benchmark_min_recall`; `verifier_path` is parsed but **refused at runtime**), `expert_routing: boolean`, and `subtypes[]` with `when: {path_pattern | frontmatter_field + frontmatter_value}`.
- Crucially, `primitive` and `aliases` are **orthogonal**: primitive drives defaults (link verbs, enrichment rubric); aliases drive **query closure** (directed declarations, symmetric per declaration, transitive cap depth 4). The comment spells out why: *"This prevents adversary-profile (entity primitive) from surfacing in `whoknows expert` just because it shares a primitive with person."*
- Pack identity = `<pack-name>@<version>+<manifest-sha8>`; folded into the search cache key so cross-pack contamination is structurally impossible.
- **7-tier resolution chain** (`schema-pack/registry.ts:24`): per-call `schema_pack` opt (CLI only — rejected when `ctx.remote === true`) → `GBRAIN_SCHEMA_PACK` env → DB config `schema_pack.source.<id>` → DB config `schema_pack` → `gbrain.yml schema:` → `~/.gbrain/config.json` → default `gbrain-base`. Extends chain: warn at depth >4, hard reject at >8. Cache is keyed by pack *name* with a 1000ms stat-TTL gate and reverse-extends-graph invalidation cascade.
- Bundled packs in `schema-pack/base/`: `gbrain-base` (24 types, codegen'd to reproduce pre-v0.38 hardcoded behavior), `gbrain-base-v2` (15-type MECE collapse — response to a production brain that accreted **94 distinct `pages.type` values**), `gbrain-recommended`, `gbrain-creator`, `gbrain-engineer`, `gbrain-investor`, `gbrain-everything`.
- `PageType` in `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/types.ts:28` is just `string` — the exhaustive union was deliberately opened in v0.38; `ALL_PAGE_TYPES` is now only a seed list.
- Pack-driven data migration: `mapping_rules` feed a `unify-types` Minion handler with three primitives — `retype` (change `pages.type`, stamp `frontmatter.legacy_type`), `page_to_link` (convert edge-shaped pages to `links` rows), `page_to_alias` (convert redirect-shaped pages to `slug_aliases` rows + soft-delete), plus a catch-all `from_type: '*unknown*'` → `note`.

## 5. Graph model

**Storage.** Wikilinks are extracted by the pure functions in `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/link-extraction.ts` and persisted as `links` rows. Provenance is the design center — `link_source` is an **open kebab-case tag, not a closed allowlist** (v114/#1941), with reconciliation-managed built-ins: `markdown`, `frontmatter`, `mentions`, `wikilink-resolved`, plus user-facing `manual`. The op layer (`operations.ts`) forbids callers passing the four managed built-ins even though the DB CHECK admits them, because *"a CLI-forged 'frontmatter' row with NULL origin would be a phantom edge reconciliation never cleans."* Reconciliation on `put_page` filters by `(link_source='frontmatter' AND origin_page_id = written_page)` so it never touches other pages' edges.

**Resolution.** `[[source:slug]]` → `resolution_type='qualified'`; bare `[[slug]]` → local-first fallback, `resolution_type='unqualified'`. Aliases short-circuit at read time via `engine.resolveSlugWithAlias` (`postgres-engine.ts:5679`) querying `slug_aliases` ordered by `array_position(sources, source_id)`. Opt-in global-basename resolution (`link_resolution.global_basename`, issue #972) stamps `link_type='wikilink_basename'` + `link_source='wikilink-resolved'`. Staleness is watermarked: `LINK_EXTRACTOR_VERSION_TS = '2026-08-01T00:00:00Z'` — a page is stale when `links_extracted_at IS NULL OR links_extracted_at < LINK_EXTRACTOR_VERSION_TS OR updated_at > links_extracted_at`.

**Yes, real recursive-CTE traversal.** Three distinct queries:

`traverseGraph(slug, depth=5, opts)` (`postgres-engine.ts:3244`, mirrored at `pglite-engine.ts:3091`) — array-based cycle prevention, source-scope filters at seed/step/aggregation, optional per-iteration frontier cap:
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE graph AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.slug, p.title, p.type, 0 as depth, ARRAY[p.id] as visited
  FROM pages p WHERE p.slug = $1 <seedScope>
  UNION ALL
  SELECT p2.id, p2.slug, p2.title, p2.type, g.depth + 1, g.visited || p2.id
  FROM graph g
  JOIN links l ON l.from_page_id = g.id
  JOIN pages p2 ON p2.id = l.to_page_id
  WHERE g.depth < $2 AND NOT (p2.id = ANY(g.visited)) <stepScope>
)
SELECT DISTINCT g.slug, g.title, g.type, g.depth,
  coalesce((SELECT jsonb_agg(DISTINCT jsonb_build_object('to_slug', p3.slug, 'link_type', l2.link_type))
            FROM links l2 JOIN pages p3 ON p3.id = l2.to_page_id
            WHERE l2.from_page_id = g.id <aggScope>), '[]'::jsonb) as links
FROM graph g ORDER BY g.depth, g.slug
```

`traversePaths(slug, {depth, linkType, direction: 'in'|'out'|'both'})` — returns edges (from_slug, to_slug, link_type, context, depth) rather than nodes; the `'both'` branch scopes both endpoint joins.

`relationalFanout(seeds[], opts)` (`postgres-engine.ts:3477`) — the retrieval-integrated one, injecting edge-derived answers into RRF fusion. Depth clamped `[1,3]`, limit clamped `[1,200]`, `mentions` edges excluded unless `includeMentions`. Notably it enforces **strict within-source traversal** even when several sources are in read scope, via `AND p2.source_id = w.seed_source`, and carries a full path array:
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE walk AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.slug, p.source_id, 0::int AS depth,
         ARRAY[p.id] AS visited, ARRAY[p.slug] AS path,
         p.source_id AS seed_source, NULL::text AS last_link_type
  FROM pages p WHERE p.slug = ANY($seeds::text[]) <seedScope> AND p.deleted_at IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT p2.id, p2.slug, p2.source_id, w.depth + 1, w.visited || p2.id, w.path || p2.slug,
         w.seed_source, l.link_type
  FROM walk w <recurStep>
  WHERE w.depth < $depth AND NOT (p2.id = ANY(w.visited))
    AND p2.source_id = w.seed_source AND p2.deleted_at IS NULL
    AND l.link_source IS DISTINCT FROM 'mentions' <typeFilter>
)
SELECT n.source_id, n.slug, MIN(n.depth) AS hop,
       COUNT(DISTINCT n.last_link_type) AS edge_count,
       array_agg(DISTINCT n.last_link_type) FILTER (WHERE n.last_link_type IS NOT NULL) AS via_link_types,
       (array_agg(array_to_string(n.path, chr(9)) ORDER BY n.depth ASC, array_length(n.path,1) ASC))[1] AS path_str,
       (SELECT cc.id FROM content_chunks cc WHERE cc.page_id = n.id ORDER BY cc.chunk_index ASC LIMIT 1) AS canonical_chunk_id
FROM walk n WHERE n.depth > 0
GROUP BY n.source_id, n.slug, n.id
ORDER BY hop ASC, edge_count DESC, n.source_id ASC, n.slug ASC LIMIT $limit
```

Ranking hook: `getBacklinkCounts` excludes `link_source='mentions'` using NULL-safe `IS DISTINCT FROM`, because auto-linked mentions are *"graph-completeness signal, NOT human-intent signal"* and counting them would globally shift search ranking on the first `--by-mention` run.

Separately, code has its own graph: `code_edges_chunk` ∪ `code_edges_symbol` with `getCalleesOf` / `code-callers` traversal and a `code_traversal_cache`.

## 6. Identity, dedup, and merge

There is **no entity-merge primitive** — no `merge_pages` op, no `gbrain merge` command (grep for `merge_pages|mergePages` returns nothing in `operations.ts` or `src/commands/`). Identity is instead handled by four cooperating layers, all slug-centric:

**(a) `resolveEntitySlug(engine, source_id, raw)`** — `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/entities/resolve.ts`. The canonicalization chain at fact-extraction time, with an explicitly documented failure mode:
1. Exact slug match (if `raw` contains `/` or matches a `pages.slug` row).
2. **Bare-name prefix expansion** — for single-token names, `slug LIKE 'people/<token>-%'` then `'companies/<token>-%'`, resolving *only* when exactly one candidate matches. Rationale: *"Bare first names like 'Alice' score too low on pg_trgm (short strings have terrible trigram overlap), so without this step they fall through to slugify('Alice') → 'alice', which spawns a phantom `people/alice.md` stub."* Collisions deliberately fall through rather than guess by connection count.
3. **pg_trgm fuzzy match** against `pages.slug` + `pages.title`, source-scoped, case-insensitive — multi-token input only. Bare names skip this arm because *"a shared first name is not specific enough to choose one person by trigram score or popularity."*
4. Deterministic slugify fallback. Bug #3447 fix: path-shaped input is slugified **per segment**, since naive slugify would corrupt `people/alice-example` → `people-alice-example`, a slug no page can ever have, causing infinite re-minting.

A variant returns a tagged resolution source (`exact_page` | `fuzzy_match` | `fallback_slugify`) for trajectory routing.

**(b) `page_aliases`** — free-text name → canonical slug, for *search*. `alias_norm` is `normalizeAlias()` output (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/search/alias-normalize.ts`). Populated from frontmatter `aliases:` at import, backfilled by `gbrain reindex --aliases` (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/commands/reindex-aliases.ts`) via `engine.setPageAliases` (replace-set semantics = idempotent). The unique key `(source_id, alias_norm, slug)` deliberately allows a *second* page to claim the same alias — collisions are reported and resolved at query time rather than blocked at write. This is where `"[REDACTED_EMAIL]"` would live if declared in `people/john-smith.md`'s frontmatter, but **there is no automatic email/phone/external-ID identity index** — nothing parses emails into an identifier table.

**(c) `slug_aliases`** — slug → slug *redirect*, for wikilinks. Populated by the `page_to_alias` unify-types handler (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/schema-pack/page-to-alias.ts`), which converted a 5.5K-page `concept-redirect` cluster in a production brain. Deliberately does **not** rewrite body text: *"the alias_table IS the resolver — engine.resolveSlugWithAlias short-circuits wikilinks like [[old-concept-name]] to the canonical at read time. Rewriting body-text would destroy historical spelling/context."* Crash-safe via "soft-delete LAST" ordering + `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on the unique constraint.

**(d) Content-level dedup**, not identity: `importFromFile` detects duplicates by `content_hash` OR external `frontmatter.id` (granola UUID etc.) and warns when *"content_hash matches but identity differs"* (`import-file.ts:651`). Facts dedup via `idx_facts_ontology_dedup` on `value_hash`; takes dedup at consolidation via HNSW similarity over `takes.embedding`; contradictions surfaced (not merged) by `gbrain eval suspected-contradictions` with a persistent `eval_contradictions_cache` keyed on `(chunk_a_hash, chunk_b_hash, model_id, prompt_version, truncation_policy)`.

**Bottom line on merge:** the doc's claim that "identity resolution becomes a database operation (merge entity IDs)" is not implemented. The shipped model is: one page per entity, aliases as indirection tables, and slug canonicalization at write time — with an explicit design bias toward *refusing to guess* (ambiguous bare names fall through to a guarded holding path rather than merge into the wrong entity).</result>

## 3. The markdown sync algorithm

**Change detection is `git diff` + SHA-256 content hash. `mtime` is used nowhere** — `grep -n "mtime" src/commands/sync.ts src/commands/import.ts` returns nothing.

### The bookmark
`sources.last_commit` (or the legacy `sync.repo_path`-anchored config key). `readSyncAnchor`/`writeSyncAnchor` at `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/commands/sync.ts:1239` / `:1314`. Advancing `last_commit` also stamps `last_sync_at` and `newest_content_at` in one UPDATE (sync.ts:1336).

### Dispatch ladder in `performSyncInner` (sync.ts:1819)
1. Resolve repo → re-clone if a managed clone is `missing`/`no-git`/`not-a-dir`; **refuse loudly** on `url-drift`/`corrupted`; **never delete** an unowned working tree (`isOwnedClone`, #1881).
2. `discoverGitRoot` + realpath; `--src-subpath` scope must satisfy `isWithinRoot(syncScopeRoot, gitContextRoot)` (path-traversal + symlink-escape guard).
3. `git pull` (SSRF-hardened flags via `pullRepo` from `git-remote.ts`; skipped on detached HEAD or `--no-pull`).
4. **Anchor reachability**: `git cat-file -t <lastCommit>` fails → **full sync**. A *present-but-non-ancestor* anchor (force-push/squash/`master`→`main`) is **still diffed directly** — `git diff A..B` is an endpoint-tree comparison, no merge-base needed (#1970). It only logs the rewrite.
5. `!lastCommit` → full sync. `--include-gitignored` → full sync (git diff can't report untracked-ignored files).
6. **Chunker-version gate**: `sources.chunker_version !== CHUNKER_VERSION` (currently `4`) forces a full re-walk *even at identical HEAD*.
7. `lastCommit === headCommit` and no version mismatch and no detached-working-tree changes → `up_to_date` (bumps `last_sync_at` as a heartbeat so `doctor` doesn't false-alarm on a quiet vault). Exception (#3068): if `pullFailed`, returns **`partial`**, not `up_to_date`, and freezes the anchor.

### The delta
`computeSyncDelta(gitContextRoot, lastCommit, pin)` at `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/sync-delta.ts` — the **single source of truth** shared with the cost estimator (issue #2139: previously the estimator priced the whole tree while the executor diffed, producing a 400× overestimate that wedged the cron).

```
execFileSync('git', ['-c','core.quotepath=false','-C',repoPath, 'diff','--name-status','-M', `${from}..${to}`],
  { timeout: 30_000, maxBuffer: 100 * 1024 * 1024 })
```

`-M` enables rename detection. `core.quotepath=false` so CJK paths arrive as UTF-8. 100 MiB buffer because Node's 1 MiB default ENOBUFS-crashes a 100K-file diff silently. Returns `{status:'unavailable', reason:'anchor_missing'|'diff_failed'}` → caller falls back to full reconcile. Detached HEAD merges in `git diff --name-status -M HEAD` **plus** `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` (untracked). Attached HEADs deliberately do *not* import dirty/untracked files.

### Resumable incremental sync (#1794)
Two `op_checkpoint` rows keyed by `syncFingerprint(sourceId, lastCommit)`: a **pinned target** and a **completed-paths list**. The diff runs `lastCommit..pin`, not `lastCommit..HEAD` — so a killed-and-resumed run keeps a stable, deterministic manifest even as HEAD races forward. On resume, if the stored pin is no longer an ancestor of HEAD (rewrite), the checkpoint is discarded. Cadence: flush after the **first** file, then every `SYNC_CHECKPOINT_EVERY_DEFAULT = 1000` files **or** `SYNC_CHECKPOINT_SECONDS_DEFAULT = 10` seconds. `SYNC_MAX_CHECKPOINT_FAILURES_DEFAULT = 3` consecutive failed flushes sets `checkpointDead` (a flag, not a throw — a throw would be swallowed by the per-file catch). A `registerCleanup('sync-checkpoint', …)` one-shot no-retry flush handles external SIGTERM. **D4 invariant: `last_commit` is NEVER advanced on partial.** `SYNC_YIELD_EVERY_DEFAULT = 64` — a `setTimeout(0)` (not `setImmediate`, which starves Bun's timers phase) every 64 files so the lock-refresh heartbeat can fire.

### Deletes
Batched at `DELETE_BATCH_SIZE = 500` (`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/engine-constants.ts:25`). Per batch: one `resolveSlugsByPaths` SELECT + one `deletePages` DELETE, both scoped to `sourceId`. Round-trips for 73K deletes: **146,000 → 292** (~5 hours → ~2 minutes). On batch failure it decomposes to per-slug `deletePage`; unrecoverable ones go to `failedFiles`. `pagesAffected` receives only slugs the DELETE actually `RETURNING`-ed (no phantoms). Legacy no-`sourceId` path falls back to the per-path loop.

Two important non-deletes:
- A file that became **un-syncable** by modification is deleted — **except** when `unsyncableReason(path)` is `'metafile'` (#1433: `log.md`, `schema.md`, `index.md`, `README.md`, `RESOLVER.md` — `SYNC_SKIP_FILES` at sync.ts:343) or `'pruned-dir'` (#2404: a page under a pruned dir can only exist via a deliberate `put_page`).
- `manifest.deleted` entries that fail `isSyncable` are filtered out upstream — `rm log.md` does **not** remove the page.

### Renames
`filtered.renamed` → `engine.updateSlug(oldSlug, newSlug)`. **#3056**: the cheap rename is *observed*, not assumed — `renameApplied = (await updateSlug(...)) > 0`, because a zero-row UPDATE doesn't throw and a thrown collision used to be swallowed, leaving the old row live alongside a newly-created destination row. On `!renameApplied`, the destination is re-imported and then a reconcile fires with two rails: (1) delete only if the destination **demonstrably materialized** (`imported`, or errorless `skipped` **at** `newSlug` — identity-dedup can skip against the *old* row, in which case deleting it would destroy the only copy); (2) locate the stale row **positively** by `source_path = from`, never by the `oldSlug` guess. A failed reconcile records a `<rename:…>` **sentinel** in `failedFiles` that the chronic-skip valve can never auto-skip, so a transient outage can't become a permanent duplicate.

### Full-sync reconcile + mass-delete valve
`planReconcileDeletes` (sync.ts:4018) is pure and exported. `normalizeReconcilePath` collapses `\` → `/` (#2828: on Windows every page looked stale and the reconcile wiped the source). Thresholds:

```ts
export const MASS_RECONCILE_RATIO = 0.5;
export const MASS_RECONCILE_MIN_PAGES = 20;
```

If stale > 50% of reconcilable pages on a source with > 20 of them, it's treated as a suspected path-comparison bug and refuses. Escape hatch: `GBRAIN_ALLOW_MASS_RECONCILE=1`. `listEverCommittedPaths` (`git log --all --no-renames --diff-filter=A --name-only`, 512 MiB buffer) distinguishes "was committed and later deleted" (real delete) from "never committed" (DB-only write-through → **preserve**) (#2426).

### Deferred embedding
`const noEmbed = opts.noEmbed || totalChanges > 100` — any sync touching >100 files imports text and defers embeddings.

## 4. Chunking strategy

Two live chunkers plus a dead one.

### Prose / markdown — `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/chunkers/recursive.ts`

```ts
export const MARKDOWN_CHUNKER_VERSION = 3;

const DELIMITERS: string[][] = [
  ['\n\n'],                          // L0: paragraphs
  ['\n'],                            // L1: lines
  ['. ', '! ', '? ', '.\n', '!\n', '?\n', ...CJK_SENTENCE_DELIMITERS], // L2: sentences
  ['; ', ': ', ', ', ...CJK_CLAUSE_DELIMITERS],                         // L3: clauses
  [],                                // L4: words + CJK char-slice fallback
];

export function chunkText(text: string, opts?: ChunkOptions): TextChunk[] {
  const chunkSize    = opts?.chunkSize    || 300;   // target WORDS per chunk
  const chunkOverlap = opts?.chunkOverlap || 50;    // overlap WORDS
  const maxChars     = opts?.maxChars     || 6000;  // hard char cap
```

Pipeline: `stripFactsFence(stripTakesFence(text), { keepVisibility: ['world'] })` → `recursiveSplit` → `greedyMerge` → `applyOverlap` → `capByChars`. Private facts and takes are stripped **before** chunking (Codex P0 privacy fix — they live only in the `facts`/`takes` tables where per-token MCP allowlists apply).

`capByChars` is a dual-budget sliding window — chars **and** estimated embedding tokens:

```ts
const window = est <= DEFAULT_MAX_CHUNK_TOKENS
  ? maxChars
  : Math.max(1, Math.min(maxChars, Math.floor((text.length * DEFAULT_MAX_CHUNK_TOKENS) / est)));
```

Window is derived from the text's *own measured density*, re-checked per slice (local density can exceed the average). Overlap is `min(500, window/10)`. Every boundary goes through `safeSplitIndex` (astral-pair safe, since the density-derived window has arbitrary parity). `DENSITY_PROBE_CHARS = 2000`.

### Code — `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/chunkers/code.ts` (1341 L)

```ts
export const CHUNKER_VERSION = 4;
const largeThreshold = opts.largeChunkThresholdTokens ?? 1000;   // line 591
const chunkTarget    = opts.chunkSizeTokens          ?? 300;     // line 592
const cap            = opts.maxChunkTokens ?? DEFAULT_MAX_CHUNK_TOKENS; // 851
// fallback to prose chunker when tree-sitter can't split:
chunkSize:    opts.fallbackChunkSizeWords ?? 300,
chunkOverlap: opts.fallbackOverlapWords   ?? 50,
const DEFAULT_CHUNKER_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
```

Tree-sitter WASM, **30 language grammars** embedded via Bun `with { type: 'file' }` (bash, c, c#, cpp, css, dart, elixir, elm, go, html, java, javascript, json, kotlin, lua, ocaml, php, python, ruby, rust, scala, solidity, sql, swift, toml, tsx, typescript, vue, yaml, zig). Chunks carry a structured header `[Lang] path:N-M symbol` plus qualified name + `parent_symbol_path` + `doc_comment`.

`capOversizedChunks` is the safety net for AST nodes with no splittable body (giant object literals, template literals, minified one-liners). It **strips the header, budgets for the re-added header** via `estimateEmbedTokensCeiling` (an upper bound — the plain cl100k figure under-counts ~2.5× on mixed-script joins; a measured 2000 cap was emitting 2011-token chunks), then falls back to word/line splitting and finally hard character splitting.

### The shared token budget — `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/chunkers/token-estimate.ts:20`

```ts
export const DEFAULT_MAX_CHUNK_TOKENS = 2000;
```

> "2000 keeps a margin under the smallest common strict embedder contexts (nomic-embed-text 2048 — #3037; llama-server -ub 2048 — #2826)."

Real tokenization via `@dqbd/tiktoken` `cl100k_base` (same encoder text-embedding-3-large uses), lazy-init, falling back to the `len/4` heuristic on load failure. The old heuristic was "2-3× off for code."

### Fenced-code extraction in prose

`extractFencedChunks` (`import-file.ts:136`) walks marked's lexer, maps fence tags through `FENCE_TAG_TO_PSEUDO_PATH` (import-file.ts:62-93, ~40 tags), and routes each fence through the **code** chunker, persisting as `chunk_source: 'fenced_code'` on the parent markdown page. Guards:
- Fast path: `if (!/(^|[\r\n])[ \t]{0,3}(```|~~~)/.test(markdown)) return out;` — because marked's lexer allocates ~110 MB of transient heap on a 2 MB table-heavy page to produce zero fences, and during bulk import that stacks into an OOM the try/catch cannot rescue (process death, not a throw).
- `MAX_FENCES_PER_PAGE = Number.parseInt(process.env.GBRAIN_MAX_FENCES_PER_PAGE || '100', 10)` — fence-bomb DOS defense.

### Chunk sources
`chunk_source ∈ { 'compiled_truth', 'timeline', 'fenced_code' }`. Timeline is chunked separately from compiled_truth.

### Contextual retrieval wrapper (v0.40.3.0, Anthropic's methodology)
`effectiveCRMode ∈ {'none','title','per_chunk_synopsis'}`. The **inline import path caps at `title`** — `per_chunk_synopsis` is too expensive and is deferred to a Minion backfill behind a cost prompt. Stored `chunk_text` stays canonical; only the embedding *input* is wrapped. `chunk_source === 'fenced_code'` bypasses wrapping (D20-T4). `token_count = Math.ceil(wrappedTexts[i].length / 4)` — the wrapped length, so cost reporting matches what was actually sent.

### Dead code
`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/chunkers/semantic.ts` (340 L: sentence embeddings → adjacent cosine → Savitzky-Golay 5-window 3rd-order → local minima) and `chunkers/llm.ts` (`CANDIDATE_SIZE = 128` words, `WINDOW_SIZE = 5`, `MAX_RETRIES = 3`) have **zero importers** anywhere in `src/` or `test/`. Ported from a Ruby implementation, never wired.

### No per-content-type chunker for transcripts
Transcripts/meetings/conversations chunk as **prose** through `chunkText`. Their special handling is at the *facts extraction* layer, not the chunking layer (see §5).

## 5. Transcript / diarization handling

### There is no diarization module
`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/diarize/` contains exactly one file — `payload-fitter.ts` (268 L) — and it is **not diarization at all**. **(1) Frontmatter graph edges** — `/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/link-extraction.ts:892`:

## 6. Dedup at ingest time

**Five distinct layers**, each solving a different duplicate class.

### L1 — Daemon LRU (unwired path)
`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/ingestion/dedup.ts`:
```ts
const DEFAULT_TTL_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 24 hours
const DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES = 5000;
```
Insertion-ordered `Map` keyed `${source_kind}:${content_hash}`; `mark()` does delete-then-set for LRU touch; eviction pops `entries.keys().next().value`. `prune()` short-circuits on the first non-expired entry (insertion order guarantees the rest are fresh). ~96 bytes/entry → ~480 KB worst case. **In-memory only, deliberately not surviving daemon restart** — cross-restart at-least-once is the Minion queue's `idempotency_key`'s job. Bypassed entirely for `mode: 'migration'` sources, which must own permanent slug-keyed idempotency via `op_checkpoint`.

### L2 — Minion queue idempotency key
`ingest:webhook:${clientId}:${contentHash}` (serve-http.ts:2353) and `webhook:sync:${source.id}:${Math.floor(Date.now()/30_000)}` (30s bucket).

### L3 — `content_hash` short-circuit (the workhorse)
`import-file.ts:635`: `if (existing?.content_hash === hash && !opts.forceRechunk) return { status: 'skipped', chunks: 0, parsedPage };`

The hash is over `{title, type, compiled_truth, timeline, frontmatter, tags.sort()}` — **with ephemeral keys stripped** (import-file.ts:603-613):
```ts
const HASH_EPHEMERAL_FRONTMATTER_KEYS = [
  'captured_at', 'ingested_at', QUARANTINE_KEY, CONTENT_FLAG_KEY, EMBED_SKIP_KEY,
];
```
Two bug classes fixed here: (a) `gbrain capture` stamps `captured_at`/`ingested_at` per call, so every capture of identical content used to produce a fresh hash → re-chunk + re-embed → wasted spend, and defeated the daemon's 24h LRU (which consumes the same hash); (b) the content-sanity gate stamps markers with a fresh `assessed_at` on **every** import, so every re-sync of a flagged page saw a changed hash and re-embedded forever. Note it strips only those keys, not all frontmatter — stripping all would mean adding a tag wouldn't change the hash, and tag reconciliation would silently no-op.

### L4 — Cross-slug identity dedup (#1309)
`import-file.ts:661-699`. Catches overlapping ingest roots: `gbrain import /vault/Subdir/` then `gbrain import /vault/` indexes the same file as `vault/subdir/note` and `vault/note`. `engine.findDuplicatePage(sourceId, {hash, frontmatterId})` (`postgres-engine.ts:1074`):
```sql
SELECT id, slug FROM pages
WHERE source_id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL
  AND (content_hash = $hash OR (frontmatter->>'id' = $fmId AND $fmId::text IS NOT NULL))
ORDER BY id LIMIT 1
```
Three-way posture:
- **SKIP** only when `frontmatter.id` matches (a true external duplicate — Granola UUID, ULID). Returns the *existing* dup's slug.
- **WARN-ALWAYS, index both** when `content_hash` matches but identity differs (templates, daily logs that legitimately share text).
- **FAIL CLOSED** on lookup error — throws `[import] dedup pre-check failed … Re-run import after DB recovery`, because an unverifiable uniqueness check must not silently allow a duplicate.

`deleted_at IS NULL` excludes tombstones so a soft-deleted page can't block re-import. Engines without `findDuplicatePage` fall through via `engine.findDuplicatePage?.`.

### L5 — Source-level dedup
- `inbox-folder`: binary files hash `${absPath}|${size}|${mtimeMs}` rather than bytes (O(1) instead of O(filesize)) — repeat drops of the *same* file dedup, same-named different files don't.
- `gstack-learnings`: seeds a `seenLines` set with `computeContentHash(JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(line)))` — **canonical JSON**, so whitespace reformatting doesn't look new. Seeded at `start()` so a fresh install doesn't replay thousands of historical lines.
- `x-to-brain` recipe: instructs the agent's collector to track seen tweet IDs in `data/state.json` and diff for deletions.
- `email-to-brain` recipe: `if msg.id in state.knownMessageIds: continue`.

### Related gates (not dedup, but ingest-time rejection)
`/tmp/gbrain_research/gbrain/src/core/content-sanity.ts`: `DEFAULT_BYTES_WARN = 50_000`, `DEFAULT_BYTES_BLOCK = 500_000`, `DEFAULT_MAX_MARKUP_RATIO = 0.85`. Dispositions: junk pattern/operator literal → **quarantine** (default; page lands hidden with zero chunks) or **reject** (throw `ContentSanityBlockError`) when `content_sanity.junk_disposition = 'reject'`; `markup_heavy` → **flag** (stays searchable + embedded, agent warned); `oversized` → flag + `embed_skip` marker (page lands, zero chunks, `tx.deleteChunks` purges old ones). Kill switch: `GBRAIN_NO_SANITY=1` (assesses + audits with a bypass flag, loud stderr per offending ingest). Hard size cap upstream: `MAX_FILE_SIZE = 5_000_000` bytes, checked via `Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf-8')` on the *network* path too — otherwise an authenticated MCP caller could spend the owner's embedding budget at will.

### Post-write verification
`verifyPageReadable` (import-file.ts:998) re-reads the page after commit and asserts `content_hash` matches; on failure it writes an `ingest_log` row (`source_type: 'write-verify-guard'`) then throws. "A write is not 'done' until it is readable back" — catches the silent-desync class where the file/commit lands but the DB index never picks it up.

## 1. ChatGPT memory (consumer/business) — **GA, architecture replaced June 2026**

**What changed:** Memory launched April 2024 as *saved memories*. April 2025 added *reference chat history* via "dreaming v1". On **June 4, 2026** OpenAI shipped **Dreaming V3**, a background synthesis system that is now the primary memory substrate, not a supplement.

Quoting the announcement: *"Over the last year, dreaming supplemented saved memories… However, it historically was never sufficient as a standalone memory system. Today, we are launching a significantly more capable and compute-efficient memory architecture built on top of dreaming."*

| Dimension | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Substrate** | Opaque managed service. A continuously-updated *synthesis* over chats, files, and connected apps — explicitly **not** an enumerable list. Help center: *"ChatGPT's memory is based on a continually updated synthesis of context from your past chats, which may be broader than what can be shown as individual items in a summary."* Legacy saved memories were a separate "notepad" stored apart from chat history |
| **Write path** | **Platform auto-extraction in a background process** — the defining change. No model tool call, no user cue needed. Legacy saved memories used model-decided writes triggered by cues ("remember I'm traveling to Singapore in July") |
| **Read path** | Auto-injected. Per-response provenance via the **book icon** ("memories in sources") showing custom instructions / past chats / files / memories, with per-memory "why this was used" explanations |
| **Granularity** | Synthesized prose summary + non-surfaced latent state. Legacy: atomic facts |
| **Scoping** | Per-user. **Project-only memory** isolates to a single project — set at project creation only, existing projects stay on "default", and it is **irreversible** once a project is shared. Enterprise/Edu: chats stay contained in projects even under "default" memory. Business workspace merge migrates memories irreversibly; personal workspace is permanently deleted |
| **Consolidation** | **Automatic supersede/rewrite** — the headline capability. *"revise its memory from 'You're going to Singapore in July' to 'You went to Singapore in July 2026'"*. Explicitly fixes contradictions ("I'm training for a marathon" vs "I sprained my ankle") |
| **Versioning/audit/deletion** | Weak, and this is the notable regression. Memory summary page is editable (type corrections, highlight text to correct, three-dot → *Delete and turn off memory*). But: *"To fully delete something ChatGPT may know about you, you'll need to delete every source where it appears, including past chats, archived chats, files, the memory summary, and disconnect any connected apps."* Deleting memories does **not** delete past chats, and re-enabling memory **re-derives** memories from remaining history. Deleted saved-memory logs retained **up to 30 days** for safety/debugging. No rollback, no write-attribution audit trail |
| **Limits & pricing** | No published item/size caps. Dreaming compute cost cut **~5x**, enabling Free-tier rollout and *"increase memory capacity for Plus and Pro users"*. Rollout: **Plus and Pro in the US first (June 4, 2026)**, then additional countries + Free and Go |
| **Security** | *"Sensitive information may appear in memory if you share it with ChatGPT."* Mitigations: Temporary Chat (uses no existing memories, creates none), workspace-level off switch. Injection surface is real: connected apps (Gmail/Calendar/Drive) now feed the extractor, so attacker-controlled email content can influence persistent memory |

**Admin/business controls:** Workspace owners toggle memory org-wide; **turning it off deletes existing saved memories for members**. Memories are per-account and non-transferable between users. Workspace *deactivation* preserves memories; workspace *deletion* permanently destroys them. Business/Enterprise data is not trained on by default.

**EU/GDPR:** Memory improvements are fully rolled out to Plus/Pro in the **EEA, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein**, but launched **off by default** there (data-minimization/legal-basis posture) versus on-by-default in the US. Note the timing collision: EU AI Act chatbot transparency obligations take effect **August 2, 2026** — today.

**Related:** **ChatGPT Pulse** (still **preview**, Plus/Pro, mobile) does proactive overnight research seeded from memory; the memory settings page now shows a **"Pulse memory suggestions"** toggle.

## 3. Conversations API — **YES, `/v1/conversations` exists. GA.**

Exact endpoints from the OpenAPI spec:

```
POST   /v1/conversations
GET    /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}
POST   /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}          (update metadata)
DELETE /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}
POST   /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/items    (create items)
GET    /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/items    (list items)
GET    /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/items/{item_id}
DELETE /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/items/{item_id}
```

**Objects:** `conversation` — `{ id, object: "conversation", created_at (unixtime), metadata }`. Deletion returns `object: "conversation.deleted"`. Items are `message` / `function_call` / tool outputs etc., with `id`, `type`, `status` (`in_progress` | `completed` | `incomplete`), `role` (enum includes `unknown, user, assistant, system, critic, discriminator, developer, tool`), and assistant-only `phase` (`commentary` | `final_answer`).

**Exact limits:**
- `items` on create: **`maxItems: 20`** — *"You may add up to 20 items at a time."* Same cap on create-items.
- `metadata`: **16 key-value pairs**, keys **≤64 chars**, values **≤512 chars**.
- List items: `limit` between **1 and 100, default 20**; `order` (`asc`/`desc`); `after` cursor; `include` (same enum as Responses).

**Relation to `previous_response_id`:** mutually exclusive. `ConversationParam`: *"Items from this conversation are prepended to `input_items` for this response request. Input items and output items from this response are automatically added to this conversation after this response completes."* Pass either a conversation ID string or an object.

**Retention:** Conversation objects and their items are **not subject to the 30-day TTL** — they persist indefinitely until deleted. This is the durable-state answer.

**GDPR gotcha, quoted from the spec:** `DELETE /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}` — *"Delete a conversation. **Items in the conversation will not be deleted.**"* You must delete items individually. This is a real erasure-cascade trap.

**9 dimensions:** opaque managed KV/list store; explicit app-API writes (plus automatic append from Responses); server-side auto-prepend read path; item-level granularity; per-conversation scoping with app-defined user mapping via `metadata`; append-only (no merge/supersede); deletion is per-object with the caveat above and no versioning/audit; no published storage pricing.

```
POST /v1/vector_stores/{vector_store_id}/file_batches/{batch_id}/cancel
GET  /v1/vector_stores/{vector_store_id}/file_batches/{batch_id}/files
POST /v1/vector_stores/{vector_store_id}/search
```

**`chunking_strategy`:** `auto` (default) or `static`. `StaticChunkingStrategy` requires both `max_chunk_size_tokens` (**default 800**, min **100**, max **4096**) and `chunk_overlap_tokens` (**default 400**, *"must not exceed half of `max_chunk_size_tokens`"*).

**`expires_after`:** `{ anchor: "last_active_at", days: 1–365 }`. Only anchor supported is `last_active_at`.

**`attributes`:** max **16 keys**; keys ≤64 chars; values are string ≤512 chars, number, or boolean. (The retrieval guide states *"at most 16 keys, with a limit of 256 characters each"* — **this conflicts with the OpenAPI spec's 64/512**; treat 16 keys as reliable, char limits as ambiguous.)

**Filtering:** `ComparisonFilter` (`eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, nin`) and `CompoundFilter` (`and`, `or`).

**Search params:** `query` (string or array), `rewrite_query` (bool, **default false**), `max_num_results` (**default 10, min 1, max 50**), `filters`, `ranking_options` with `score_threshold` (0–1, default 0) and `ranker`. **Ranker version discrepancy:** spec enum is `none | auto | default-2024-11-15` (default `auto`); the retrieval guide text says `auto` or `default-2024-08-21`. **NEW: `ranking_options.hybrid_search`** with `embedding_weight` (`rrf_embedding_weight`) and `text_weight` (`rrf_text_weight`) tuning reciprocal rank fusion between semantic and sparse keyword matches — at least one must be > 0.

**`file_search` tool:** requires `type: "file_search"` and `vector_store_ids`; optional `max_num_results` (1–50), `ranking_options`, `filters`.

**Limits:** max file size **512 MB**; **5,000,000 tokens per file**; `file_ids` on vector store create **`maxItems: 500`**; **300 requests/minute** shared across `/files` and `/file_batches` per vector store; ~25 supported file types. Per-project total storage cap of 100 GB is widely reported but I could not confirm it in current primary docs — treat as unverified.

**Pricing (primary doc, exact):** `Up to 1 GB (across all stores) | Free` · `Beyond 1 GB | $0.10/GB/day`. Billed on parsed+chunked+embedded size regardless of access frequency. Search/retrieval token costs are separate.

**9 dimensions:** vector index substrate; explicit app-API writes only (no model-initiated writes); retrieved-on-demand via tool call; document/chunk granularity; scoped per vector store (app maps to user/org); no consolidation — append-only, dedup is your problem; deletion is explicit per-file/store with `expires_after` TTL as the only automation, no versioning; injection risk is standard RAG (retrieved chunks enter context verbatim).

### 5a. Session memory (conversation history) — GA

`Session` protocol — four methods, exact signatures:
```python
async get_items(limit: int | None = None) -> list[TResponseInputItem]
async add_items(items: list[TResponseInputItem]) -> None
async pop_item() -> TResponseInputItem | None
async clear_session() -> None
```
Custom implementations inherit `SessionABC`.

**Python implementations (expanded well beyond May 2026):** `SQLiteSession`, `AsyncSQLiteSession` (aiosqlite), `RedisSession`, `SQLAlchemySession`, **`MongoDBSession`**, **`DaprSession`** (30+ backends), `AdvancedSQLiteSession` (conversation branching + usage analytics), `EncryptedSession` (wrapper, transparent encryption + TTL), `OpenAIConversationsSession`, **`OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession`**.

Signatures:
```python
SQLiteSession(session_id, db_path=":memory:", sessions_table="agent_sessions",
              messages_table="agent_messages", session_settings=None)
OpenAIConversationsSession(*, conversation_id=None, openai_client=None, session_settings=None)
EncryptedSession(session_id, underlying_session, encryption_key, ttl=600)
RedisSession.from_url(session_id, url="redis://...")
MongoDBSession.from_uri(session_id, uri="mongodb://...", database="agents")
```

### 5b. Sandbox agent memory — **BETA, and this is the real first-party long-term memory**

Explicit banner: *"Sandbox agents are in beta. Expect details of the API, defaults, and supported capabilities to change before general availability."*

| Dimension | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Substrate** | **Files in the sandbox workspace.** Default dir `memories/`: `memory_summary.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `raw_memories.md`, `phase_two_selection.json`, `raw_memories/<rollout-id>.md`, `rollout_summaries/<rollout-id>_<slug>.md`, `skills/`. Sessions at `sessions/<rollout-id>.jsonl` |
| **Write path** | **Automated post-run extraction, not a tool call.** Two phases: (1) conversation extraction — a memory-generating model summarizes one accumulated conversation file; (2) layout consolidation — a consolidation agent reads raw memories and writes `MEMORY.md` + `memory_summary.md`. The agent *can* also update `memories/MEMORY.md` live if `Filesystem()` is enabled |
| **Read path** | **Progressive disclosure.** `memory_summary.md` auto-injected into the developer prompt at run start; the agent then greps `MEMORY.md` as a keyword index and opens specific rollout summaries only when needed. Requires `Shell()`; live update requires `Filesystem()` |
| **Granularity** | Rollout summaries + distilled tips/preferences |
| **Scoping** | By `MemoryLayoutConfig`, **not** by agent name. Same layout + same memory conversation ID ⇒ shared memory. Conversation ID priority: explicit `conversation_id` → `session.session_id` → `RunConfig.group_id` → auto-generated per-run ID |
| **Consolidation** | Real merge + **forgetting**. `max_raw_memories_for_consolidation` **default 256**; beyond it, *"Phase 2 keeps only memories from the newest conversations and removes older ones."* Long conversations truncated with beginning and end preserved |
| **Versioning/deletion** | Plain files — full git-style inspectability, but no built-in audit or rollback |
| **Config** | `Memory()`, `Memory(generate=None)` read-only, `Memory(read=None)` generate-only; `MemoryGenerateConfig(max_raw_memories_for_consolidation=..., extra_prompt=...)`; `MemoryLayoutConfig(memories_dir=..., sessions_dir=...)` |
| **Security** | Architectural mitigation: harness/compute separation is explicitly positioned against prompt injection and exfiltration; sandbox providers supported are Cloudflare, Daytona, E2B, Modal, Runloop, Vercel. **But the memory docs carry no explicit injection warning** — and consolidation models read untrusted conversation content and write durable instructions the agent auto-loads. That is a persistent-injection surface |

## 6. Codex / AGENTS.md as memory

- `AGENTS.md` remains the **static, manually-maintained** instruction layer, with a **32 KiB ceiling and silent truncation past the cap** — a real monorepo footgun.
- Codex CLI reads `memory_summary.md` whole at session start (token-truncated to budget) then greps `MEMORY.md` — i.e. **the same two-file progressive-disclosure pattern as the Agents SDK sandbox**, which is the clearest signal of OpenAI's converging house style for agent memory.

| | Write decider | Read | Consolidation | Durable? | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ChatGPT Dreaming | Platform (background) | Auto-inject | **Rewrite/supersede** | Yes | Subscription |
| Responses `previous_response_id` | App (`store`) | Server reconstruct | Append + **compaction** | 30d | Prior tokens **re-billed**; cache −75% |
| Conversations API | App + auto-append | Server prepend | Append-only | **Indefinite** | Not published |

| SDK Sessions | SDK auto | Auto-inject | None (unless compaction session) | Your DB | Your infra |

| Skills API | App upload | Agent loads | **Versioned** | Yes | Not published |

**Bottom line:** There is **no `/v1/memories` endpoint** — I verified this directly against the OpenAPI spec. OpenAI has no standalone developer memory service. The closest first-party long-term memory is the **beta sandbox `MEMORY.md` system**, which is file-based, model-extracted, and self-consolidating. For durable state, Conversations API is the answer, but its `DELETE` semantics leave items orphaned. Only Skills offers versioning. Only ChatGPT Dreaming offers supersede-on-write, and it trades away the auditability the old saved-memories list had.

## 1. ChatGPT memory (consumer/business) — **GA, architecture replaced June 2026**

**What changed:** Memory launched April 2024 as *saved memories*. April 2025 added *reference chat history* via "dreaming v1". On **June 4, 2026** OpenAI shipped **Dreaming V3**, a background synthesis system that is now the primary memory substrate, not a supplement.

Quoting the announcement: *"Over the last year, dreaming supplemented saved memories… However, it historically was never sufficient as a standalone memory system. Today, we are launching a significantly more capable and compute-efficient memory architecture built on top of dreaming."*

| Dimension | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Substrate** | Opaque managed service. A continuously-updated *synthesis* over chats, files, and connected apps — explicitly **not** an enumerable list. Help center: *"ChatGPT's memory is based on a continually updated synthesis of context from your past chats, which may be broader than what can be shown as individual items in a summary."* Legacy saved memories were a separate "notepad" stored apart from chat history |
| **Write path** | **Platform auto-extraction in a background process** — the defining change. No model tool call, no user cue needed. Legacy saved memories used model-decided writes triggered by cues ("remember I'm traveling to Singapore in July") |
| **Read path** | Auto-injected. Per-response provenance via the **book icon** ("memories in sources") showing custom instructions / past chats / files / memories, with per-memory "why this was used" explanations |
| **Granularity** | Synthesized prose summary + non-surfaced latent state. Legacy: atomic facts |
| **Scoping** | Per-user. **Project-only memory** isolates to a single project — set at project creation only, existing projects stay on "default", and it is **irreversible** once a project is shared. Enterprise/Edu: chats stay contained in projects even under "default" memory. Business workspace merge migrates memories irreversibly; personal workspace is permanently deleted |
| **Consolidation** | **Automatic supersede/rewrite** — the headline capability. *"revise its memory from 'You're going to Singapore in July' to 'You went to Singapore in July 2026'"*. Explicitly fixes contradictions ("I'm training for a marathon" vs "I sprained my ankle") |
| **Versioning/audit/deletion** | Weak, and this is the notable regression. Memory summary page is editable (type corrections, highlight text to correct, three-dot → *Delete and turn off memory*). But: *"To fully delete something ChatGPT may know about you, you'll need to delete every source where it appears, including past chats, archived chats, files, the memory summary, and disconnect any connected apps."* Deleting memories does **not** delete past chats, and re-enabling memory **re-derives** memories from remaining history. Deleted saved-memory logs retained **up to 30 days** for safety/debugging. No rollback, no write-attribution audit trail |
| **Limits & pricing** | No published item/size caps. Dreaming compute cost cut **~5x**, enabling Free-tier rollout and *"increase memory capacity for Plus and Pro users"*. Rollout: **Plus and Pro in the US first (June 4, 2026)**, then additional countries + Free and Go |
| **Security** | *"Sensitive information may appear in memory if you share it with ChatGPT."* Mitigations: Temporary Chat (uses no existing memories, creates none), workspace-level off switch. Injection surface is real: connected apps (Gmail/Calendar/Drive) now feed the extractor, so attacker-controlled email content can influence persistent memory |

**Admin/business controls:** Workspace owners toggle memory org-wide; **turning it off deletes existing saved memories for members**. Memories are per-account and non-transferable between users. Workspace *deactivation* preserves memories; workspace *deletion* permanently destroys them. Business/Enterprise data is not trained on by default.

**EU/GDPR:** Memory improvements are fully rolled out to Plus/Pro in the **EEA, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein**, but launched **off by default** there (data-minimization/legal-basis posture) versus on-by-default in the US. Note the timing collision: EU AI Act chatbot transparency obligations take effect **August 2, 2026** — today.

**Related:** **ChatGPT Pulse** (still **preview**, Plus/Pro, mobile) does proactive overnight research seeded from memory; the memory settings page now shows a **"Pulse memory suggestions"** toggle.

| Dimension | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Substrate** | Opaque managed store of `response` objects, chainable by ID |
| **Write path** | Explicit app API. `store` (boolean, **default `true`**) |
| **Read path** | Server-side reconstruction via `previous_response_id` (string, e.g. `resp_123`) — cannot be combined with `conversation` |
