## B. Microsoft

### B1. Foundry Agent Service **Memory (public preview)** — the big new thing

`api-version=2025-11-15-preview`. Base: `https://{account}.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/{project}`. SDKs: `azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0` (Py), `Azure.AI.Projects` + `Azure.AI.Projects.Memory` (C#), `@azure/ai-projects@2` (TS), `com.azure:azure-ai-agents` (Java). Python surface is under **`project_client.beta.memory_stores`**.

**Endpoints:**
```
POST   /memory_stores                                    (create)
POST   /memory_stores/{name}                             (update)
GET    /memory_stores                                    (list)
DELETE /memory_stores/{name}
POST   /memory_stores/{name}:update_memories             → returns update_id
GET    /memory_stores/{name}/updates/{update_id}
POST   /memory_stores/{name}:search_memories
POST   /memory_stores/{name}:delete_scope
POST   /memory_stores/{name}/items                       (create item)
GET    /memory_stores/{name}/items/{id}
GET    /memory_stores/{name}/items:list?scope=...
POST   /memory_stores/{name}/items/{id}                  (update item)
DELETE /memory_stores/{name}/items/{id}
```

**Store definition** (`MemoryStoreDefaultDefinition` / `MemoryStoreDefaultOptions`, REST `"kind": "default"`):
`chat_model`, `embedding_model`, and `options.{ chat_summary_enabled, user_profile_enabled, procedural_memory_enabled, default_ttl_seconds, user_profile_details }`.

- `default_ttl_seconds: 0` = **no expiration**. TTL applies to *all* memories including remember-commands; consolidation **resets** last-updated time. TTL only applies to stores created after TTL support shipped.
- `user_profile_details` is a natural-language steering string, used both to prioritize *and* to exclude (`"Avoid irrelevant or sensitive data, such as age, financials, precise location, and credentials"`).

**Three memory types**, all enabled by default: **user profile**, **chat summary**, **procedural** (reusable how-to routines). Item `kind` values include `user_profile`.

**Tool form:** `{"type": "memory_search_preview", "memory_store_name": "...", "scope": "...", "update_delay": N}`. `update_delay` = seconds of inactivity before extraction; **default 300**. Set `update_delay: 0` to force immediate processing. Note the agents API uses `api-version=v1` while the memory store API uses `2025-11-15-preview` — **two different api-versions in the same app**.

**Scope:** set `scope` to `"{{$userId}}"` and the service resolves from the **`x-memory-user-id`** header, falling back to the Entra token as **`{tid}_{oid}`**. ⚠️ Automatic scope resolution works **only** with the memory search tool — low-level APIs require explicit `scope` in every request.

**Retrieval pattern MS recommends:** call `search_memories` with `scope` but **without** `items` → returns *static* user-profile memories (inject at conversation start); with `items` → *contextual* memories per turn. `options.max_memories` caps results.

**Remember/forget:** the tool emits a `memory_command_call` output item with `{"action": "remember"|"forget", "content": ...}`. Direct commands **do not** override TTL.

**Quotas:** 100 scopes per store · **10,000 memories per scope** · 1,000 search req/min · 1,000 update req/min.

**Regions (19):** Australia East, Brazil South, Canada East, East US 2, France Central, Italy North, Japan East, Korea Central, North Central US, Norway East, South Africa North, South India, Sweden Central, Switzerland North, UAE North, UK South, West US, West US 2, West US 3.

**Pricing:** no separate memory SKU — *"You're billed for usage of the underlying chat and embedding models you configure."*

**Limitations:** requires compatible AOAI chat + embedding deployments (e.g. `gpt-5.2`, `text-embedding-3-small`); **VNet integration is NOT supported for memory stores**; some store options are create-time-only.

**Security:** explicit prompt-injection + **memory-corruption** warnings; recommends Azure AI Content Safety jailbreak/prompt-injection detection on data entering *and leaving* memory. Best practices call out per-user `scope`, tamper-evident deletion audit trails, and *"Allow customers to define, isolate, inspect, and delete their own memory footprint."*

**9 dims (delta only):** substrate = managed store keyed by `scope`; write = LLM auto-extract on debounce + explicit item CRUD + remember/forget commands; read = auto via tool OR explicit `search_memories`; granularity = memory item (profile fact / summary / procedure); consolidation = LLM merge + conflict resolution, "can vary by memory type and might change during the preview"; deletion = item DELETE, `:delete_scope` (the GDPR DSR path), store DELETE — **materially better GDPR story than AgentCore** because of `delete_scope` + real TTL on the extracted records.

## C. Second tier

**Mistral — real, and it's conversation state, not extracted memory.** The Agents API `conversations` endpoints (beta) are: `GET /v1/conversations`, `POST /v1/conversations` (create+append), `GET|POST|DELETE /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}`, `GET /v1/conversations/{id}/history` (all entries), `GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages` (messages only), `POST /v1/conversations/{id}/restart` (fork from an entry), plus `#stream` variants of create/append/restart. Key params: `agent_id` **xor** `model`, `inputs` (string or message list), **`store`** (boolean, **default `true`** — *"You can opt out from the automatic storing with `store=False`; this will make the new history not being stored on Mistral's cloud"*), `completion_args`, `guardrails`, and `handoff_execution` (`"server"` default, or `"client"`). Access control: *"The public Conversations API can read and modify only conversations owned by the API key creator"* — i.e. **API-key-scoped, not end-user-scoped; you must build tenant isolation yourself.** There is **no server-side fact extraction/consolidation** — it's a durable transcript with branching (`restart`), the analogue of OpenAI's Conversations, not of AgentCore Memory. Consumer-side, **Le Chat "Memories"** exists and is now documented under the **Vibe** product as *"a legacy Chat feature… with no public deprecation date"* — explicit save (`"Remember that I prefer concise answers"`) plus opportunistic automatic capture, with a Memories tab for view/edit/delete-one/delete-all and conversational deletion (`"Forget that I mentioned my location"`), *"Memories only stores information you've explicitly included in your prompts,"* stored for the subscription duration, **not API-accessible**, and — importantly — **on Free/Pro/Student plans prompts with Memories may be used for model training (opt-out available); Team/Enterprise are opted out by default.** No pricing line item, no TTL, no documented quota.

**Cohere — no memory primitive. Confirmed negative.** Chat v2 is deliberately **stateless**: the v1 `conversation_id` parameter (which had Cohere manage history server-side) **is not supported in v2**; you pass an ordered `messages` array of `User`/`Assistant`/`Tool`/`System` roles and a `documents` field (list of objects with a `data` object or string, plus optional `id` used for citations) for grounding. That's RAG, not memory — there is no write path, no extraction, no scoping, no deletion endpoint, no retention, no memory pricing, because nothing is stored. The docs page titled "Short-Term Memory Handling for Agents" is a **client-side cookbook** using LangChain `SystemMessage`/`HumanMessage`/`AIMessage` and `intermediate_steps` to hand-build `chat_history` — not a Cohere API. Cohere's **North** platform (GA) markets a memory capability that *"allows agents to leverage information from a previous session to answer questions in a subsequent session"* (benchmarked at 54% with Command A+ vs 39% with Command A Reasoning), but this is a product feature of the closed workspace, **with no public memory API, parameters, quotas, or pricing** — unverified as a developer primitive.

**xAI / SpaceXAI — conversation state yes, memory service no.** ⚠️ First: **xAI no longer exists as an independent entity.** SpaceX absorbed xAI in an all-stock deal on **2026-02-02**; the merged company rebranded to **SpaceXAI** on **2026-07-06**; `docs.x.ai` now renders as "SpaceXAI Docs." Grok keeps its name. On the API: the **Responses API is now the preferred interface** (Chat Completions is labeled legacy), with **`store`** (boolean, **default `true`**) controlling server-side storage and **`previous_response_id`** to continue a conversation without resending history — including encrypted reasoning content. **Retention is exactly 30 days**: *"Responses stored for 30 days"*, and *"If you want to continue a conversation after 30 days, you should store your responses history and the encrypted thinking content locally, and pass them in a new request body."* There is **no documented deletion endpoint** for stored responses and no extraction/consolidation layer — substrate is a raw transcript keyed by response ID, scoped to the API key. Consumer-side, **Grok does have a cross-chat memory feature** that *"remembers your preferences and past conversations,"* alongside custom instructions, with user data controls under **Profile → Settings → Data Controls** (delete/download data, `grok.com/files`, `x.ai/privacy-portal`) and *"Deleted chats and files are removed from systems within standard retention windows unless we are required to retain them longer for legal, compliance, or safety purposes."* No GA date, no memory-specific quotas or pricing, **not API-accessible**. Note also: *"a limited number of authorized xAI personnel may review your conversations."* (Grok-app memory details are medium confidence — `x.ai/grok` returns 403 to fetchers; sourced from search snippets of that page.)

**Meta Llama API — dead.** The Llama API public preview **shut down 2026-07-06** (~4 weeks ago); requests return a sunset response with redirect guidance. It never had server-side stateful conversations — it was an OpenAI-compatible stateless chat-completions endpoint. Meta directs developers to download weights or use third-party hosts (Bedrock, Together, Groq). Secondary reporting says Meta pivoted to a proprietary "Muse Spark" line served from `api.meta.ai` via a "Meta Model API" — **I could not verify this against a Meta primary source; treat as unconfirmed.** Net: **no first-party Meta memory or conversation-state primitive exists today.**

**Mem0 / Zep / Letta — third-party, not provider-native.** Worth one caveat: Mem0 is the closest thing to a blessed third party — Microsoft ships **first-party connectors** for it in both Semantic Kernel (`Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Memory.Mem0Provider`) and Microsoft Agent Framework (`agent_framework.mem0.Mem0Provider` / `Mem0ContextProvider`), so "Microsoft supports Mem0" is true at the SDK layer while the *service* remains Mem0's.

## A. AWS Bedrock AgentCore Memory — the only true first-party *managed extraction* memory service at GA

**Status: GA since 2025-10-13** (whole AgentCore). Memory is GA; individual sub-features shipped incrementally.

### Control plane vs data plane (they are two different services)

| | Service | API version | Endpoint | Ops |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Control | `bedrock-agentcore-control` | `2023-06-05` | `bedrock-agentcore-control.<region>.amazonaws.com` | `CreateMemory` (`POST /memories/create`), `UpdateMemory`, `GetMemory`, `DeleteMemory`, `ListMemories` |
| Data | `bedrock-agentcore` | `2024-02-28` | (regional data-plane host) | `CreateEvent` (`POST /memories/{memoryId}/events`), `ListEvents`, `GetEvent`, `DeleteEvent`, `ListSessions`, `ListActors`, `RetrieveMemoryRecords` (`POST /memories/{memoryId}/retrieve`), `ListMemoryRecords`, `GetMemoryRecord`, `DeleteMemoryRecord`, `BatchCreateMemoryRecords`, `BatchUpdateMemoryRecords`, `BatchDeleteMemoryRecords`, `StartMemoryExtractionJob`, `ListMemoryExtractionJobs` |

PrivateLink: `com.amazonaws.region.bedrock-agentcore-control` (Mar 2026).

### `CreateMemory` request — exact fields

```
POST /memories/create
{ "clientToken", "description" (1–4096), "encryptionKeyArn", "eventExpiryDuration",
  "indexedKeys": [{ "key", "type" }],            // 1–10 items
  "memoryExecutionRoleArn", "memoryStrategies": [ MemoryStrategyInput ],
  "name" (pattern [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,47}),
  "streamDeliveryResources": { "resources": [...] }, "tags" }
```
Returns **HTTP 202** (async; poll `status`).

`eventExpiryDuration` — **conflicting AWS docs**: `API_CreateMemory` says `Valid Range: Minimum value of 3. Maximum value of 365`; the quotas page says `Minimum EventExpirationDuration days in a CreateEvent operation | 7`. Assume **7–365 days** in practice. **Required: Yes.**

### `MemoryStrategyInput` — UNION, exactly one of:

`semanticMemoryStrategy` · `summaryMemoryStrategy` · `userPreferenceMemoryStrategy` · **`episodicMemoryStrategy`** · `customMemoryStrategy`

Resolved strategy object exposes: `configuration.{ extraction, consolidation, reflection, selfManagedConfiguration, type }`, `namespaces[]`, **`namespaceTemplates[]`**, `memoryRecordSchema.metadataSchema[]`, `strategyId`, `status`, `type`.

| Strategy | Steps | Output | Default namespace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Semantic | Extraction, Consolidation | JSON facts. Processes **only `USER` and `ASSISTANT`** role messages | `/strategy/{memoryStrategyId}/actors/{actorId}/` |
| User preference | Extraction, Consolidation | JSON `{context, preference, categories}` | (actor-scoped) |
| Summary | **Consolidation only** | XML `<topic>` chunks; multiple chunks per session | `/strategy/{memoryStrategyId}/actor/{actorId}/session/{sessionId}/` (`sessionId` **required**) |
| **Episodic** (Dec 2025) | Extraction, Consolidation, **Reflection** | XML: situation, intent, assessment, justification, episode-level reflection | you choose; strategy / actor / session level |

Note the doc inconsistency: semantic says `/actors/` (plural), episodic + the organization page say `/actor/` (singular). Namespace variables: `{memoryStrategyId}`, `{actorId}`, `{sessionId}`. **Always use a trailing slash** — AWS explicitly warns `/actors/Alice/` not `/actors/Alice` to prevent prefix collisions in multi-tenant apps.

Episodic records are indexed on **"intent"**; reflections on **"use case"**. Episodes only materialize once AgentCore *detects a completed episode* — higher latency than other strategies.

### Prompt overrides — YES, overridable

Built-in-with-overrides lets you replace the **instructions** (not the output schema) and choose the Bedrock `modelId`. The field is **`appendToPrompt`** (max **30 KB**) — and note the doc's own warning: *"The content of `appendToPrompt` **replaces** the default instructions in the system prompt."* (i.e. the name lies).

Overridable steps: Semantic = Extraction+Consolidation · Summary = Consolidation · User preference = Extraction+Consolidation · Episodic = Extraction+Consolidation+Reflection.

Hard rules: don't modify schemas in prompts; **don't rename consolidation operations (`AddMemory`, `UpdateMemory`)** or the pipeline fails.

**Which model does extraction?** For pure built-ins AWS does not disclose the model and does not bill you for it. For built-in-with-overrides and self-managed, **it runs in *your* account** via `memoryExecutionRoleArn`, consumes *your* Bedrock quotas, and is billed separately to you.

### Self-managed strategies (`customMemoryStrategy.configuration.selfManagedConfiguration`)

```json
{"customMemoryStrategy": {"name": "...", "configuration": {"selfManagedConfiguration": {
  "triggerConditions": [
    {"messageBasedTrigger": {"messageCount": 6}},
    {"tokenBasedTrigger": {"tokenCount": 1000}},
    {"timeBasedTrigger": {"idleSessionTimeout": 30}}],
  "historicalContextWindowSize": 2,
  "invocationConfiguration": {"payloadDeliveryBucketName": "...", "topicArn": "arn:aws:sns:..."}}}}}
```
Flow: trigger → SNS notification `{jobId, s3PayloadLocation, memoryId, strategyId}` → S3 payload `{requestId, accountId, memoryId, actorId, sessionId, strategyId, startingTimestamp, endingTimestamp, currentContext[], historicalContext[]}` → your pipeline → `BatchCreateMemoryRecords`. Use **FIFO SNS topics** if session ordering matters.

### `CreateEvent` — exact fields

`actorId` (req, 1–255) · `sessionId` (opt, 1–100) · `eventTimestamp` (**required**) · `branch: {name, rootEventId}` · `payload[]` (req, 0–**100** items) · `clientToken` · `metadata` (0–**15** entries, `stringValue` only, **not encrypted with your CMK**) · **`extractionMode: "SKIP"`** ← store in short-term but exclude from long-term extraction.

### `RetrieveMemoryRecords`

```
POST /memories/{memoryId}/retrieve
{ "maxResults": 1–100 (default 20), "namespace" | "namespacePath", "nextToken",
  "searchCriteria": { "memoryStrategyId", "searchQuery", "topK", "metadataFilters": [{left, operator, right}] } }
```
`namespace` = prefix match. `namespacePath` = hierarchical (all records under a parent). Response: `memoryRecordSummaries[].{content, createdAt, memoryRecordId, memoryStrategyId, metadata, namespaces[], score}`.

### Metadata filtering (Apr 2026)

- `indexedKeys` types: `STRING`, `STRINGLIST`, `NUMBER`. **Cannot be removed once declared. No backfill.**
- `metadataSchema[]`: `key`, `type`, `definition` (required), `llmExtractionInstruction` (built-in `LATEST_VALUE` or custom NL), `validation.{stringValidation.allowedValues | stringListValidation.{allowedValues,maxItems} | numberValidation.{minValue,maxValue}}`
- `extractionType`: `LLM_INFERRED` (default) or **`STRICTLY_CONSISTENT`** — value copied verbatim from event, LLM never consulted, **and it partitions extraction/consolidation** so records from different value groups never merge. Ideal for compliance isolation.
- Operators: `EQUALS_TO`, `CONTAINS`, `EXISTS`, `NOT_EXISTS`, `GREATER_THAN(_OR_EQUALS)`, `LESS_THAN(_OR_EQUALS)`, `BEFORE`, `AFTER`. Max **5 filters**, `AND` only. Pre-filter before KNN.
- Free system fields (no indexed-key budget): `x-amz-agentcore-memory-recordType`, `x-amz-agentcore-memory-createdAt`, `x-amz-agentcore-memory-updatedAt`.
- `ListEvents` metadata filters support only `EXISTS`, `NOT_EXISTS`, `EQUALS_TO` and only `stringValue`.

Adjacent: Runtime/Browser/Code Interpreter all **$0.0895/vCPU-hour + $0.00945/GB-hour**. Gateway $0.005/1,000 invocations, Search API $0.025/1,000, tool indexing $0.02/100 tools/month. Identity **$0.010 per 1,000 tokens/API keys** for non-AWS resources, **free** via Runtime or Gateway.

### Regions

GA (Oct 2025): us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, ap-northeast-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1. Added: São Paulo + Canada Central (Apr 2026), GovCloud US-West (May 2026), Bangkok + Malaysia + Milan + Spain (Jun 2026).

### Runtime / Identity / tools (context relevant)

Runtime: session isolation via microVMs; **idle session timeout 15 min** (`idleRuntimeSessionTimeout` in `LifecycleConfiguration`), **max session duration 8 h** (`maxLifetime`), request timeout 15 min, payload 100 MB, session storage 1 GB, 5,000 active sessions/account (us-east-1/us-west-2; 2,500 elsewhere). Code Interpreter 2vCPU/8GB, 10 GB disk; Browser 1vCPU/4GB.

### Framework integration

- **Strands**: `AgentCoreMemorySessionManager(AgentCoreMemoryConfig(memory_id, session_id, actor_id, batch_size=N), region_name=...)` from `bedrock_agentcore.memory.integrations.strands`. **Gotcha:** with `batch_size > 1` you MUST use a `with` block or `close()` or buffered messages are lost.
- **LangGraph**: `AgentCoreMemorySaver` (checkpointer) and `AgentCoreMemoryStore` from `langgraph_checkpoint_aws`; requires `thread_id` + `actor_id` in runtime config.
- CLI: `agentcore add memory --name X --strategies SEMANTIC,SUMMARIZATION,USER_PREFERENCE`

### 9 dimensions

1. **Substrate** — AWS-managed; events (short-term, TTL'd) + vector-indexed memory records (long-term). KMS CMK via `encryptionKeyArn`. VPC-deployable (Sep 2025).
2. **Write path** — App calls `CreateEvent`; **service-side LLM decides what becomes a record** (extraction→consolidation, async background). Escape hatches: `extractionMode: "SKIP"`, `appendToPrompt` overrides, self-managed pipelines, direct `BatchCreateMemoryRecords`.
3. **Read path** — **Explicit pull only.** Nothing is auto-injected into your prompt. `RetrieveMemoryRecords` (semantic + metadata pre-filter), `ListMemoryRecords`, `GetMemoryRecord`; `ListEvents`/`GetEvent`/`ListSessions` for raw.
4. **Granularity** — event (turn-batch, ≤100 messages), fact, preference, summary chunk, episode, reflection.
5. **Scoping** — `actorId` × `sessionId` × `branch` for short-term; hierarchical `namespaces` for long-term, enforceable via IAM condition keys `bedrock-agentcore:namespace` / `bedrock-agentcore:namespacePath`, plus resource-based policies.
6. **Consolidation/dedup** — built-in `AddMemory`/`UpdateMemory` consolidation ops per strategy; `STRICTLY_CONSISTENT` metadata partitions consolidation groups; episodic reflection consolidates *across* episodes.
7. **Versioning/audit/deletion** — `DeleteEvent`, `DeleteMemoryRecord`, `BatchDeleteMemoryRecords`, `DeleteMemory`; CloudTrail + one-click observability (Mar 2026). ⚠️ **GDPR gap: `eventExpiryDuration` TTL applies to short-term events only. Extracted long-term memory records have no documented automatic expiry** — you must delete them yourself, and there is no per-actor "erase everything" call (you enumerate by namespace).
8. **Limits & pricing** — above.
9. **Security posture** — Cross-actor reflection warning: *"Because reflections can span multiple actors within the same memory resource, consider the privacy implications of cross-actor analysis"*; recommends Bedrock Guardrails. Event metadata is **not** CMK-encrypted. Explicit anti-pattern: *"Don't rely on metadata alone for tenant isolation… security-through-convention model that breaks on any missed filter. Use namespaces for the who, and metadata for the what."* ISO + CSA STAR certified (Feb 2026).

## B. Microsoft

### B1. Foundry Agent Service **Memory (public preview)** — the big new thing

`api-version=2025-11-15-preview`. Base: `https://{account}.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/{project}`. SDKs: `azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0` (Py), `Azure.AI.Projects` + `Azure.AI.Projects.Memory` (C#), `@azure/ai-projects@2` (TS), `com.azure:azure-ai-agents` (Java). Python surface is under **`project_client.beta.memory_stores`**.

**Endpoints:**
```
POST   /memory_stores                                    (create)
POST   /memory_stores/{name}                             (update)
GET    /memory_stores                                    (list)
DELETE /memory_stores/{name}
POST   /memory_stores/{name}:update_memories             → returns update_id
GET    /memory_stores/{name}/updates/{update_id}
POST   /memory_stores/{name}:search_memories
POST   /memory_stores/{name}:delete_scope
POST   /memory_stores/{name}/items                       (create item)
GET    /memory_stores/{name}/items/{id}
GET    /memory_stores/{name}/items:list?scope=...
POST   /memory_stores/{name}/items/{id}                  (update item)
DELETE /memory_stores/{name}/items/{id}
```

**Store definition** (`MemoryStoreDefaultDefinition` / `MemoryStoreDefaultOptions`, REST `"kind": "default"`):
`chat_model`, `embedding_model`, and `options.{ chat_summary_enabled, user_profile_enabled, procedural_memory_enabled, default_ttl_seconds, user_profile_details }`.

- `default_ttl_seconds: 0` = **no expiration**. TTL applies to *all* memories including remember-commands; consolidation **resets** last-updated time. TTL only applies to stores created after TTL support shipped.
- `user_profile_details` is a natural-language steering string, used both to prioritize *and* to exclude (`"Avoid irrelevant or sensitive data, such as age, financials, precise location, and credentials"`).

**Three memory types**, all enabled by default: **user profile**, **chat summary**, **procedural** (reusable how-to routines). Item `kind` values include `user_profile`.

**Tool form:** `{"type": "memory_search_preview", "memory_store_name": "...", "scope": "...", "update_delay": N}`. `update_delay` = seconds of inactivity before extraction; **default 300**. Set `update_delay: 0` to force immediate processing. Note the agents API uses `api-version=v1` while the memory store API uses `2025-11-15-preview` — **two different api-versions in the same app**.

**Scope:** set `scope` to `"{{$userId}}"` and the service resolves from the **`x-memory-user-id`** header, falling back to the Entra token as **`{tid}_{oid}`**. ⚠️ Automatic scope resolution works **only** with the memory search tool — low-level APIs require explicit `scope` in every request.

**Retrieval pattern MS recommends:** call `search_memories` with `scope` but **without** `items` → returns *static* user-profile memories (inject at conversation start); with `items` → *contextual* memories per turn. `options.max_memories` caps results.

**Remember/forget:** the tool emits a `memory_command_call` output item with `{"action": "remember"|"forget", "content": ...}`. Direct commands **do not** override TTL.

**Quotas:** 100 scopes per store · **10,000 memories per scope** · 1,000 search req/min · 1,000 update req/min.

**Regions (19):** Australia East, Brazil South, Canada East, East US 2, France Central, Italy North, Japan East, Korea Central, North Central US, Norway East, South Africa North, South India, Sweden Central, Switzerland North, UAE North, UK South, West US, West US 2, West US 3.

**Pricing:** no separate memory SKU — *"You're billed for usage of the underlying chat and embedding models you configure."*

**Limitations:** requires compatible AOAI chat + embedding deployments (e.g. `gpt-5.2`, `text-embedding-3-small`); **VNet integration is NOT supported for memory stores**; some store options are create-time-only.

**Security:** explicit prompt-injection + **memory-corruption** warnings; recommends Azure AI Content Safety jailbreak/prompt-injection detection on data entering *and leaving* memory. Best practices call out per-user `scope`, tamper-evident deletion audit trails, and *"Allow customers to define, isolate, inspect, and delete their own memory footprint."*

**9 dims (delta only):** substrate = managed store keyed by `scope`; write = LLM auto-extract on debounce + explicit item CRUD + remember/forget commands; read = auto via tool OR explicit `search_memories`; granularity = memory item (profile fact / summary / procedure); consolidation = LLM merge + conflict resolution, "can vary by memory type and might change during the preview"; deletion = item DELETE, `:delete_scope` (the GDPR DSR path), store DELETE — **materially better GDPR story than AgentCore** because of `delete_scope` + real TTL on the extracted records.

### B2. Foundry threads/state (non-memory)

- **Threads → Conversations, Runs → Responses.** Conversations store *items* (messages, tool calls, tool outputs), not just messages. `openai.conversations.create()`, `conversations.items.create()`, obtained via `project.get_openai_client()`. Agent creation/versioning stays on the project client (`PromptAgentDefinition`, `create_version`).
- **BYO thread storage in your own Cosmos DB**: database **`enterprise_memory`**, containers `thread-message-store`, `system-thread-message-store`, `agent-entity-store`, plus `agent-definitions-v1` and `run-state-v1` when using the Responses API. Requires **≥3000 RU/s total**, **1000 RU/s per container**; provisioned or serverless.
- File search / vector stores remain the separate grounding path; MS explicitly tells you to use **Foundry IQ knowledge bases** for curated org content and **file search** for user docs — *not* memory.

### B3. Semantic Kernel → Microsoft Agent Framework

- **SK memory is legacy on two axes.** (a) `Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Memory.IMemoryStore` / `ISemanticTextMemory` → **Vector Store abstractions** (`VectorStore` in `Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData.Abstractions`; `{Provider}MemoryStore` → `{Provider}VectorStore`). Only Vector Stores support custom schemas, multiple vectors/record, choice of index + distance function, and **metadata pre-filtering**. (b) SK agents themselves → **Microsoft Agent Framework** (RC Feb 2026, **1.0 production-ready ~Apr 2026**), the "direct successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen." SK v1.x supported *"for at least one year after Microsoft Agent Framework leaves Preview."*
- **SK's agent memory page still carries: *"The Semantic Kernel Agent Memory functionality is experimental."*** C# only; Python/Java say "Coming Soon." API: `agentThread.AIContextProviders.Add(provider)` with `Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Memory.Mem0Provider` (options `ApplicationId`, `AgentId`, `ThreadId`, `UserId`, `ScopeToPerOperationThreadId`, `ContextPrompt`) and `WhiteboardProvider` (options `MaxWhiteboardMessages`, `ContextPrompt`, `WhiteboardEmptyPrompt`, `MaintenancePromptTemplate` with `{{$maxWhiteboardMessages}}`, `{{$inputMessages}}`, `{{$currentWhiteboard}}`).
- **Agent Framework is the current API**: namespace **`Microsoft.Agents.AI`**, base class **`AIContextProvider`** returning `AIContext`, hooks `ProvideAIContextAsync` / `StoreAIContextAsync` / `InvokingCoreAsync` / `InvokedCoreAsync`, plus `ProviderSessionState<T>` and `StateKey`. **`AgentThread` is replaced by `AgentSession`** (`CreateSessionAsync()`, `RunAsync(input, session)`, `SerializeSession`/`DeserializeSessionAsync`; Python `create_session()`, `get_session(service_session_id=...)`, `to_dict()`/`from_dict()`; Go `agent.Session` + `agent.ContextProvider`). Providers: `InMemoryChatHistoryProvider` (default), **`ChatHistoryMemoryProvider`** (stores chat history in a vector store, retrieves by similarity), **`agent_framework.mem0.Mem0Provider`** / `Mem0ContextProvider`.
- ⚠️ Security note straight from the docs: *"OpenAI Responses and Conversations IDs are scoped to the backing API key or project by default; if a hosted agent uses the same key or project for multiple end users, store those IDs server-side and verify the authenticated user or tenant before resuming."*

### B4. Microsoft 365 Copilot memory & personalization

**Status: the Learn doc says PREVIEW** — *"Copilot personalization and memory are in preview and subject to change"* (Frontier program). (Some 2025 blog coverage called it GA; the current admin doc says preview. Trust the doc.) Available to Copilot Chat users **with and without** an M365 Copilot license.

- **Substrate: the user's Exchange mailbox, hidden folder.** Item class **`IPM.Contact`**, folder **`CopilotMemory`**. Inherits Customer Lockbox + encryption at rest.
- **Admin control: "Enhanced personalization", ON by default.** Graph resource type **`enhancedPersonalizationSetting`**. Turning it off greys out the user-level Custom instructions / Saved memories / Chat history toggles.
- Three components: **saved memories**, **inferred details from chat history**, **custom instructions**.
- **Retention — the sharp edges:** *"Retention policies and retention labels configured in Purview by organization admins **don't apply** to Copilot memory… There are no admin controls to enforce retention rules specifically for Copilot memory."* Saved memories persist until the user deletes them; **deleting a chat does not delete memories generated from it**. If a user deletes all chats containing a fact, chat-history details are purged **within 7 days**. If the control is turned off, chat-history details are deleted after **30 days**. Turning controls off **stops application but does not remove** custom instructions or saved memories.
- **DSR path:** eDiscovery/Content Search + Microsoft Graph Explorer; search item class `IPM.Contact`. **Custom instructions are NOT discoverable** (user must self-export via Settings > Personalization).
- **No audit logging:** *"Memory and personalization actions don't generate audit log entries in Purview."*
- **Admins cannot restrict what goes into memory.** Temporary chats *are* discoverable in Purview.
- Jan 2026: voice chats in the M365 Copilot app can now reference memory.

### B5. GitHub Copilot — convention, not a memory service

No server-side memory primitive. The "memory" is file conventions read from the repo: **`AGENTS.md`** (root or nested, supported by coding agent since **2025-08-28**), **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`**, **`.github/instructions/**.instructions.md`** (since 2025-07-23), and it also reads **`CLAUDE.md`** and **`GEMINI.md`**. **`excludeAgent`** frontmatter property (2025-11-12) scopes an instructions file away from e.g. `code-review`. Substrate = git; write path = humans/PRs; read path = auto-injected by prompt assembly; versioning = git history; deletion = git; security = **the file is fully attacker-controllable in a fork/PR context** — treat as untrusted instruction injection.

## C. Second tier

**Mistral — real, and it's conversation state, not extracted memory.** The Agents API `conversations` endpoints (beta) are: `GET /v1/conversations`, `POST /v1/conversations` (create+append), `GET|POST|DELETE /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}`, `GET /v1/conversations/{id}/history` (all entries), `GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages` (messages only), `POST /v1/conversations/{id}/restart` (fork from an entry), plus `#stream` variants of create/append/restart. Key params: `agent_id` **xor** `model`, `inputs` (string or message list), **`store`** (boolean, **default `true`** — *"You can opt out from the automatic storing with `store=False`; this will make the new history not being stored on Mistral's cloud"*), `completion_args`, `guardrails`, and `handoff_execution` (`"server"` default, or `"client"`). Access control: *"The public Conversations API can read and modify only conversations owned by the API key creator"* — i.e. **API-key-scoped, not end-user-scoped; you must build tenant isolation yourself.** There is **no server-side fact extraction/consolidation** — it's a durable transcript with branching (`restart`), the analogue of OpenAI's Conversations, not of AgentCore Memory. Consumer-side, **Le Chat "Memories"** exists and is now documented under the **Vibe** product as *"a legacy Chat feature… with no public deprecation date"* — explicit save (`"Remember that I prefer concise answers"`) plus opportunistic automatic capture, with a Memories tab for view/edit/delete-one/delete-all and conversational deletion (`"Forget that I mentioned my location"`), *"Memories only stores information you've explicitly included in your prompts,"* stored for the subscription duration, **not API-accessible**, and — importantly — **on Free/Pro/Student plans prompts with Memories may be used for model training (opt-out available); Team/Enterprise are opted out by default.** No pricing line item, no TTL, no documented quota.

**Cohere — no memory primitive. Confirmed negative.** Chat v2 is deliberately **stateless**: the v1 `conversation_id` parameter (which had Cohere manage history server-side) **is not supported in v2**; you pass an ordered `messages` array of `User`/`Assistant`/`Tool`/`System` roles and a `documents` field (list of objects with a `data` object or string, plus optional `id` used for citations) for grounding. That's RAG, not memory — there is no write path, no extraction, no scoping, no deletion endpoint, no retention, no memory pricing, because nothing is stored. The docs page titled "Short-Term Memory Handling for Agents" is a **client-side cookbook** using LangChain `SystemMessage`/`HumanMessage`/`AIMessage` and `intermediate_steps` to hand-build `chat_history` — not a Cohere API. Cohere's **North** platform (GA) markets a memory capability that *"allows agents to leverage information from a previous session to answer questions in a subsequent session"* (benchmarked at 54% with Command A+ vs 39% with Command A Reasoning), but this is a product feature of the closed workspace, **with no public memory API, parameters, quotas, or pricing** — unverified as a developer primitive.

**xAI / SpaceXAI — conversation state yes, memory service no.** ⚠️ First: **xAI no longer exists as an independent entity.** SpaceX absorbed xAI in an all-stock deal on **2026-02-02**; the merged company rebranded to **SpaceXAI** on **2026-07-06**; `docs.x.ai` now renders as "SpaceXAI Docs." Grok keeps its name. On the API: the **Responses API is now the preferred interface** (Chat Completions is labeled legacy), with **`store`** (boolean, **default `true`**) controlling server-side storage and **`previous_response_id`** to continue a conversation without resending history — including encrypted reasoning content. **Retention is exactly 30 days**: *"Responses stored for 30 days"*, and *"If you want to continue a conversation after 30 days, you should store your responses history and the encrypted thinking content locally, and pass them in a new request body."* There is **no documented deletion endpoint** for stored responses and no extraction/consolidation layer — substrate is a raw transcript keyed by response ID, scoped to the API key. Consumer-side, **Grok does have a cross-chat memory feature** that *"remembers your preferences and past conversations,"* alongside custom instructions, with user data controls under **Profile → Settings → Data Controls** (delete/download data, `grok.com/files`, `x.ai/privacy-portal`) and *"Deleted chats and files are removed from systems within standard retention windows unless we are required to retain them longer for legal, compliance, or safety purposes."* No GA date, no memory-specific quotas or pricing, **not API-accessible**. Note also: *"a limited number of authorized xAI personnel may review your conversations."* (Grok-app memory details are medium confidence — `x.ai/grok` returns 403 to fetchers; sourced from search snippets of that page.)

**Meta Llama API — dead.** The Llama API public preview **shut down 2026-07-06** (~4 weeks ago); requests return a sunset response with redirect guidance. It never had server-side stateful conversations — it was an OpenAI-compatible stateless chat-completions endpoint. Meta directs developers to download weights or use third-party hosts (Bedrock, Together, Groq). Secondary reporting says Meta pivoted to a proprietary "Muse Spark" line served from `api.meta.ai` via a "Meta Model API" — **I could not verify this against a Meta primary source; treat as unconfirmed.** Net: **no first-party Meta memory or conversation-state primitive exists today.**

**Mem0 / Zep / Letta — third-party, not provider-native.** Worth one caveat: Mem0 is the closest thing to a blessed third party — Microsoft ships **first-party connectors** for it in both Semantic Kernel (`Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Memory.Mem0Provider`) and Microsoft Agent Framework (`agent_framework.mem0.Mem0Provider` / `Mem0ContextProvider`), so "Microsoft supports Mem0" is true at the SDK layer while the *service* remains Mem0's.

## Cross-cutting: the two real services compared

| | AgentCore Memory | Foundry Memory |
|---|---|---|
| Status | **GA** (Oct 2025) | **Public preview** |
| Strategies | 5 named, composable, prompt-overridable, self-managed escape hatch | 3 fixed booleans + a NL steering string |
| Read path | explicit `RetrieveMemoryRecords` | tool auto-injection **or** explicit `search_memories` |
| Scoping | `actorId`/`sessionId`/namespaces + IAM condition keys + RBP | flat `scope` string (auto-resolved from `x-memory-user-id`/Entra) |
| Filtering | rich metadata pre-filter, 10 indexed keys, 9 operators | none documented |
| Deletion | per-record/per-event/per-memory; **no per-actor purge, no LTM TTL** | **`:delete_scope`** + `default_ttl_seconds` |
| Pricing | explicit per-event/per-record/per-retrieval | folded into model deployment cost |
| Scale ceiling | 150 memories/region, 6 strategies each; no record cap | 100 scopes/store, 10k memories/scope |
| Biggest weakness | no built-in expiry for extracted records (GDPR) | preview, no VNet, no metadata filtering, small scope ceiling |

## ⚠️ Lead finding: the thing you're researching has been deprecated by its own authors

The MemGPT memory architecture (core memory blocks in Postgres + archival passages + recall memory + self-editing tools) is **no longer Letta's product**. As of 2026 it is the "legacy Letta server," in maintenance mode.

**[VERIFIED]** `github.com/letta-ai/letta/AGENTS.md` opens with the literal heading "## This repository is deprecated":
> "This repository contains the **legacy Letta server**: the self-hosted API server (`letta/letta` image) that powers the Letta V1 API and V1 SDKs... It is in maintenance mode and is no longer where active development happens."
> — https://github.com/letta-ai/letta/blob/main/AGENTS.md

**[VERIFIED]** The README note: "This repository contains the legacy Letta server (the API server behind the Letta V1 API and SDKs). Active development has moved to the [Letta Agent repo](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta-code)" — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta/main/README.md

**[VERIFIED]** The replacement architecture is **MemFS** — a **git-backed markdown filesystem**, not a database. From `letta.com/blog/our-next-phase` (MAR 2026): *"Memory moves from specialized memory tools that edit memory in a database to generalized computer use tools like bash that operate over memory projected into git-backed files."* The post lists a **mid-April 2026 sunset** for: legacy server memory tools (explicitly naming `core_memory_replace`), Letta Filesystem, Templates, server-side MCP, and Tool Rules. — https://www.letta.com/blog/our-next-phase

I'll document **both** architectures, because the legacy one is the fully-specified, reimplementable design and the new one is where their current thinking is.

---

# PART A — The legacy MemGPT/Letta architecture (v0.16.8, still the best-specified reference)

All source citations below are pinned to tag `0.16.8` (last release, 2026-05-14).

## 1. The memory hierarchy — actual data structures

| Tier | In context? | Storage | Table |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core memory** (memory blocks) | Always, verbatim | Postgres row per block | `block`, joined via `blocks_agents` |
| **Message buffer** (FIFO) | Yes, until evicted | Postgres | `messages` |
| **Recall memory** | No — searched via tool | Same `messages` table; "recall" = the searchable superset of all messages ever | `messages` |
| **Archival memory** | No — searched via tool | Passages with embeddings | `archival_passages` (+ `source_passages` for files) |

**Key subtlety [VERIFIED]:** recall memory is *not a separate store*. It is the same message table; `conversation_search` queries it with filters. Archival memory is genuinely separate (`letta/orm/passage.py`).

`ContextWindowOverview` in `letta/schemas/memory.py` enumerates exactly what occupies context: `system_prompt`, `core_memory`, `memory_filesystem`, `tool_usage_rules`, `directories`, `summary_memory`, `functions_definitions`, `messages`, plus `external_memory_summary` (a metadata line telling the agent *how many* archival/recall items exist without listing them).
— https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta/0.16.8/letta/schemas/memory.py

## 2. Memory blocks — full field list and prompt rendering

**[VERIFIED]** From `letta/schemas/block.py`:

```
value: str                      # the content
limit: int = 100_000            # CORE_MEMORY_BLOCK_CHAR_LIMIT
label: Optional[str]            # 'human', 'persona', ...
description: Optional[str]      # tells the agent what the block is FOR
read_only: bool = False         # agent cannot edit via memory tools
metadata: Optional[dict] = {}
hidden: Optional[bool]
tags: Optional[List[str]] = []
project_id, template_name, is_template, template_id, base_template_id,
deployment_id, entity_id, preserve_on_migration
created_by_id, last_updated_by_id
```
— https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta/0.16.8/letta/schemas/block.py

**Character limits [VERIFIED]** (`letta/constants.py`):
- `CORE_MEMORY_BLOCK_CHAR_LIMIT = 100000`
- `CORE_MEMORY_PERSONA_CHAR_LIMIT = 20000`, `CORE_MEMORY_HUMAN_CHAR_LIMIT = 20000`
- `DEFAULT_CORE_MEMORY_SOURCE_CHAR_LIMIT = 50000` (file blocks)

**Prompt rendering [VERIFIED]** — `Memory._render_memory_blocks_standard()` emits exactly:

```xml
<memory_blocks>
The following memory blocks are currently engaged in your core memory unit:

<human>
<description>
{description}
</description>
<metadata>
- read_only=true          ← only if read_only
- chars_current={len(value)}
- chars_limit={limit}
</metadata>
<value>
{value}
</value>
</human>

</memory_blocks>
```

There is a second renderer, `_render_memory_blocks_line_numbered()`, which prefixes each line with `1→ `, `2→ ` and injects a `<warning>` block containing `CORE_MEMORY_LINE_NUMBER_WARNING`. This is the design that lets the agent do precise `str_replace`-style edits — it's a direct lift of Anthropic's text-editor tool pattern (the source even cites `anthropic-quickstarts/computer-use-demo/.../edit.py`).

**Overflow behavior [VERIFIED, and it's blunt]:** the limit is *advisory to the model* (surfaced as `chars_limit` in the metadata) and *enforced as an exception* at the persistence layer — `block_manager.py` documents `Raises: ValueError if any new value exceeds its block's limit`. There is **no auto-truncation and no auto-summarization of blocks**. An overflowing edit simply fails and the error goes back to the model as a tool error. This is a real design decision worth copying or rejecting deliberately.

**Versioning [VERIFIED]:** `block_history` table snapshots `(description, label, value, limit, metadata_, actor_type, actor_id, sequence_number)` per block for undo/redo, with a unique index on `(block_id, sequence_number)`.
— https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta/0.16.8/letta/orm/block_history.py

## 3. Self-editing memory tools — exact signatures

**[VERIFIED]** From `letta/functions/function_sets/base.py` and `letta/constants.py`. There are **four generations** of the memory toolset, which tells you a lot about what didn't work:

```python
BASE_TOOLS            = ["send_message", "conversation_search",
                         "archival_memory_insert", "archival_memory_search"]
BASE_MEMORY_TOOLS     = ["core_memory_append", "core_memory_replace",
                         "memory", "memory_apply_patch"]          # v1
BASE_MEMORY_TOOLS_V2  = ["memory_replace", "memory_insert"]        # v2
BASE_MEMORY_TOOLS_V3  = ["memory"]                                 # v3 - omni-tool
BASE_SLEEPTIME_TOOLS  = ["memory_replace", "memory_insert",
                         "memory_rethink", "memory_finish_edits"]
BASE_SLEEPTIME_CHAT_TOOLS   = ["send_message", "conversation_search",
                               "archival_memory_search"]
BASE_VOICE_SLEEPTIME_TOOLS  = ["store_memories", "rethink_user_memory",
                               "finish_rethinking_memory"]
LETTA_PARALLEL_SAFE_TOOLS = {"conversation_search", "archival_memory_search",
                             "run_code", "web_search", "fetch_webpage",
                             "grep_files", "semantic_search_files"}
```

Note `DEPRECATED_LETTA_TOOLS = ["archival_memory_insert", "archival_memory_search"]` — even archival was on the way out.

Signatures:

```python
core_memory_append(agent_state, label: str, content: str) -> str
    # naive: current + "\n" + content

core_memory_replace(agent_state, label: str, old_content: str, new_content: str) -> str
    # raises ValueError if old_content not in current
    # uses str.replace() — replaces ALL occurrences (a latent bug vs memory_replace)

memory_replace(agent_state, label: str, old_string: str, new_string: str) -> str
    # REQUIRES old_string to occur EXACTLY ONCE; if >1 it raises listing the line numbers
    # rejects args containing "\nLine \d+: " or the line-number warning banner

memory_insert(agent_state, label: str, new_string: str, insert_line: int = -1) -> str
    # 0 = beginning, -1 = end; validates range

memory_rethink(agent_state, label: str, new_memory: str) -> str
    # full rewrite; creates the block if missing

memory_finish_edits(agent_state) -> None
    # explicit "I'm done" signal that terminates the sleep-time edit loop

memory_apply_patch(agent_state, label: str, patch: str) -> str
    # unified-diff patches; multi-block mode via "*** Add/Update/Delete Block: <label>"
    # and "*** Move to: <new_label>"

memory(agent_state, command, path, file_text, description, old_string, new_string,
       insert_line, insert_text, old_path, new_path)
    # v3 omni-tool. commands: create | str_replace | insert | delete | rename
    # NOTE: paths, e.g. "/memories/user_preferences" — the filesystem metaphor
    # already leaking into the block model before the MemFS pivot
```

**How the agent decides to call them [VERIFIED]:** purely via the system prompt + block `description` fields. There is no classifier, no router, no trigger heuristic. The `sleeptime_v2` prompt is the clearest statement of policy:

> "Use your precise tools to make narrow edits, as well as broad tools to make larger comprehensive edits... you can use your `rethink` tool to reorganize the entire memory block at a single time."
> "When writing to memory blocks, make sure to be precise when referencing dates and times (for example, do not write 'today' or 'recently', instead write specific dates and times, because 'today' and 'recently' are relative, and the memory is persisted indefinitely)."
> "Not every observation warrants a memory edit, be selective in your memory editing, but also aim to have high recall."

— https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta/0.16.8/letta/prompts/system_prompts/sleeptime_v2.py

That temporal-absolutization rule is the single most portable idea in the whole codebase for a team knowledge brain.

## 4. Sleep-time compute / sleep-time agents

**Yes — a genuinely separate agent that shares memory blocks.** [VERIFIED]

Mechanism (`letta/groups/sleeptime_multi_agent_v4.py`):

1. Agent created with `enable_sleeptime=True` ("If set to True, memory management will move to a background agent thread" — `schemas/agent.py`). This creates a `Group` with `manager_type=sleeptime`, `manager_agent_id` = the primary agent, and `agent_ids` = the sleep-time participants.
2. After **every** foreground `step()`/`stream()`, `run_sleeptime_agents()` fires.
3. Gating: if `group.sleeptime_agent_frequency` is set, a `turns_counter` is bumped and the sleep-time agents only run when `turns_counter % sleeptime_agent_frequency == 0`. If frequency is `None`, they run **every turn**. Default is `None` (`schemas/group.py`).
4. It records `last_processed_message_id` so the next run picks up exactly the unprocessed slice.
5. It builds a transcript from `prior_messages + response_messages`, stringified, and dispatches it as a **background asyncio task** (`safe_create_task`) with its own `Run` record — fully async, off the user's latency path.
6. The injected prompt is verbatim:

```
<\system-reminder>
You are a sleeptime agent - a background agent that asynchronously processes
conversations after they occur.

IMPORTANT: You are NOT the primary agent. You are reviewing a conversation that
already happened between a primary agent and its user:
- Messages labeled "assistant" are from the primary agent (not you)
- Messages labeled "user" are from the primary agent's user

Your primary role is memory management. Review the conversation and use your
memory tools to update any relevant memory blocks with information worth
preserving. Check your memory_persona block for any additional instructions or
policies.
<\/system-reminder>

Messages:
{messages_text}
```

**Block sharing is the whole trick:** blocks live in their own table and attach many-to-many via `blocks_agents` (unique on `(agent_id, block_label)` and `(agent_id, block_id)`). The sleep-time agent is attached to the *same block rows*. When it calls `memory_rethink`, the primary agent's next turn renders the new value. No message passing, no sync protocol — shared mutable state in a table.
— https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta/0.16.8/letta/orm/blocks_agents.py

**"Learned context"** [VERIFIED] is the term from the research, not a hardcoded block label. From the blog: *"Given some original context (e.g. the conversation history, a set of files) the sleep-time agent will reflect on the original context to iteratively derive a learned context."* Shipped in Letta 0.7.0, 2025-04-21. — https://www.letta.com/blog/sleep-time-compute/

**Benchmark numbers [VERIFIED]** (arXiv:2504.13171, Lin, Snell, Wang, Packer, Wooders, Stoica, Gonzalez; 2025-04-17):
- **~5× reduction** in test-time compute for equal accuracy on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME
- **up to +13%** accuracy on Stateful GSM-Symbolic; **up to +18%** on Stateful AIME
- **~2.5× lower cost per query** when sleep-time compute is amortized across related queries (Multi-Query GSM-Symbolic)
- Effectiveness correlates with **query predictability**
— https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13171 · code: https://github.com/letta-ai/sleep-time-compute

**Trustworthiness caveat:** these are *math-reasoning* benchmarks (GSM-Symbolic, AIME) with a synthetic stateful split, not memory benchmarks. The "sleep-time compute helps" result is about precomputing reasoning over a fixed context, which is a different claim from "background agents produce better long-term memory." Letta has not, as far as I can verify, published a controlled ablation of sleep-time agents on a memory benchmark.

## 5. Context overflow — eviction and recursive summarization

**MemGPT paper policy [VERIFIED]** (arXiv:2310.08560v2, Packer, Wooders, Lin, Fang, Patil, Stoica, Gonzalez):
- **Warning at 70%** of context window → a system message tells the agent to save anything important
- **Flush at 100%**
- **Evict 50%** of the context window
- New recursive summary = f(existing recursive summary, evicted messages)
— https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2310.08560

**Implementation [VERIFIED]** (`letta/services/summarizer/`):
- `SUMMARIZATION_TRIGGER_MULTIPLIER = 0.9` — fires when step usage > `context_window * 0.9` (comment: *"using instead of 1.0 to avoid 'too many tokens in prompt' fallbacks"*)
- Two modes: `STATIC_MESSAGE_BUFFER` and `PARTIAL_EVICT_MESSAGE_BUFFER`
- `partial_evict_summarizer_percentage = 0.30`
- `DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE_BUFFER_LENGTH = 30`, `DEFAULT_MIN_MESSAGE_BUFFER_LENGTH = 15`
- Partial-evict docstring: *"Evict a partial amount of messages, and replace message[1] with a recursive summary"* — the summary is spliced in at index 1, right after the system message.
- Also `EphemeralSummaryAgent` (writes summaries to a *block* instead of into the message list, so it can be async).
— https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta/0.16.8/letta/services/summarizer/summarizer.py

## 6. Agent File (.af)

**[VERIFIED]** https://github.com/letta-ai/agent-file (1,192 stars, last pushed 2026-03-24 — effectively frozen).

Serialized: model config (context window limit, model name, embedding model), **full message history with an `in_context` boolean per message**, system prompt, memory blocks, tool rules, tool-exec environment variables, and tools *including source code + JSON schemas*.

**Explicitly NOT serialized:** *"We currently do not support Passages (the units of Archival Memory in Letta/MemGPT)"* — so **.af does not carry archival memory**. Secrets are nulled on export.

Portability claim: *"other frameworks could also load in .af files if they convert the state into their own representations."* In practice adoption outside Letta appears negligible, and the format has not been updated since the MemFS pivot.

## 7. Retrieval — how archival search actually works

**Two backends [VERIFIED]:**

**(a) Native / pgvector.** `archival_passages` table with `embedding = Vector(4096)` under Postgres (`CommonVector` blob under SQLite). Embeddings are **zero-padded to `MAX_EMBEDDING_DIM = 4096`** so heterogeneous embedding models share one column — with the comment *"do NOT change or else DBs will need to be reset."* `DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_DIM = 1024`, `DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_CHUNK_SIZE = 300`, `EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE = 200`.

**(b) Turbopuffer** (`letta/helpers/tpuf_client.py`, ~2,150 lines — the serious path). Namespace per archive: `_get_archive_namespace_name(archive_id)`. Schema declares `{"text": {"type": "string", "full_text_search": True}}`.

Search modes: `"vector"` (ANN), `"fts"` (BM25), `"hybrid"`, `"timestamp"`. Hybrid issues a `multi_query` of an ANN query and a BM25 query, then fuses:

```
k = 60   # "standard RRF constant from Cormack et al. (2009)"
score = vector_weight/(k + vector_rank) + fts_weight/(k + fts_rank)
# defaults: vector_weight = 0.5, fts_weight = 0.5
```

Ranks are 1-indexed; missing-from-a-list contributes 0. **No cross-encoder reranker.** Fallback: if no query text is given, `search_mode` silently degrades to `"timestamp"` (most-recent-first).

**Result count — there's an inconsistency worth knowing [VERIFIED]:** the `archival_memory_search` tool docstring advertises `top_k` "(default: 10)", `TurbopufferClient.query_passages` defaults `top_k: int = 10`, but `AgentManager.search_archival_memory` does `limit = top_k if top_k is not None else RETRIEVAL_QUERY_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` where that constant is **5**. So the agent-facing default is 5, not the 10 the model is told.

**Timestamp filtering [VERIFIED]:** `start_datetime` / `end_datetime`, ISO 8601, accepting date-only (`2024-01-15` → 00:00:00) or datetime; naive datetimes are localized to the *agent's* configured timezone (`agent_state.timezone`). End dates snap to `23:59:59.999999`.

**Tags [VERIFIED]:** dual storage — a JSON column on the passage for fast read *and* a `passage_tags` junction table for efficient filtering. `tag_match_mode` ∈ `{"any","all"}`.

**Returned shape [VERIFIED]:**
```json
{"id": "...", "timestamp": "<ISO, agent tz>", "content": "...", "tags": [...],
 "relevance": {"rrf_score": ..., "vector_rank": ..., "fts_rank": ...}}
```
The agent literally sees the fusion ranks. That's a nice affordance for calibration.

**`conversation_search` (recall)** [VERIFIED] is *also* hybrid ("hybrid search (text + semantic similarity)") with `roles` filter, `limit` (default 5), and `start_date`/`end_date`.

## 8. Multi-agent shared memory

**[VERIFIED]** Two independent sharing mechanisms:

- **Blocks:** create a block, pass `block_ids=[...]` at agent creation or `attach()` later. `blocks_agents` junction. Updates are immediately visible to every attached agent — no propagation delay, no eventual consistency. **Last-write-wins**, and the docs warn that setting `value` replaces the entire block, so concurrent writers can silently clobber each other.
- **Archives:** `Archive` is a first-class entity ("a collection of archival passages that can be shared between agents") joined via `archives_agents`, with its own `vector_db_provider` and `embedding_config`. Endpoints: `agents.archives.attach/detach`.

For a team knowledge brain this is the most directly reusable piece: a shared block = a live team fact sheet; a shared archive = a team corpus.

## 9. Forgetting — essentially absent

**[VERIFIED]** There is **no TTL, no decay, no scoring, no automatic eviction** anywhere in archival memory. Passages have `is_deleted: bool` (soft delete) and can be deleted via SDK (`client.agents.passages.delete`), but:
- the v1 docs state archival memory is **agent-immutable**: *"Agents cannot easily modify or delete archival memories"* — there is no `archival_memory_delete` tool in `LETTA_TOOL_SET`
- the sleep-time system prompt says memory "is persisted indefinitely"

Forgetting exists only in **core memory**, and only as a side effect of the agent choosing to overwrite: `core_memory_replace(..., new_content="")` or `memory_rethink`. Practical upshot: **archival is append-only forever in practice.** If you copy this design, you inherit an unbounded, monotonically-degrading corpus.

The newer MemFS design does address this — see Part B.

## 10. Evaluation

### MemGPT paper (arXiv:2310.08560, v1 2023-10-12, v2 2024-02-12)

**Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR)** — built from the Multi-Session Chat (MSC) dataset via LLM self-instruct; 5 prior sessions, session 6 contains a single QA pair. **[VERIFIED]**

| Model | Accuracy | ROUGE-L |
|---|---|---|
| GPT-3.5 Turbo | 38.7% | 0.394 |
| **MemGPT + GPT-3.5** | **66.9%** | **0.629** |
| GPT-4 | 32.1% | 0.296 |
| **MemGPT + GPT-4** | **92.5%** | **0.814** |
| GPT-4 Turbo | 35.3% | 0.359 |
| **MemGPT + GPT-4 Turbo** | **93.4%** | **0.827** |

**Conversation opener (CSIM)** — SIM-1 / SIM-3 / SIM-H: Human 0.800/0.800/1.000; GPT-3.5 0.830/0.812/0.817; GPT-4 0.868/0.843/0.773; GPT-4 Turbo 0.857/0.828/0.767.

**Nested key-value retrieval:** paper reports only qualitatively — *"MemGPT is the only approach that is able to consistently complete the nested KV task beyond 2 nesting levels,"* with GPT-3.5 at 0% at 1 nesting level. Per-level numbers are in Figure 7, not tabulated.

**Document QA:** Figure 5 only, no table. Paper concedes MemGPT is *"significantly degraded... using GPT-3.5"* and best with GPT-4.

**Trustworthiness assessment:** DMR is the headline and it's the weakest link — the baselines are *deliberately handicapped* (GPT-4 with no retrieval scoring 32.1% is a strawman, and it scores *lower* than GPT-3.5, which is a red flag for prompt sensitivity rather than capability). The 92.5%-vs-32.1% delta is mostly "has retrieval vs. doesn't," not "MemGPT's architecture vs. alternatives." No comparison against a plain RAG baseline on DMR.

# PART B — What replaced it: MemFS / context repositories (2026)

This is what they'd build today, and it's arguably more relevant to a team knowledge brain.

## Structure [VERIFIED]

Memory is a **git repository of Markdown files with YAML frontmatter**:

```
$MEMORY_DIR/
├── system/          ← ALWAYS fully loaded into the system prompt
│   ├── persona.md
│   └── human.md
├── reference/       ← tree + description visible; contents loaded on demand
│   └── project-notes.md
└── skills/
    └── my-skill/SKILL.md
```

```markdown
---
description: "Who I am, what I value, and how I approach working with people."
---
I am a Letta agent. I remember durable preferences and improve with use.
```

- `system/` ≈ the old core-memory blocks (the legacy renderer even strips a `system/` prefix so `system/human` renders as `<human>`)
- Everything else = **progressive disclosure**: the *filetree and descriptions* are always in the system prompt; contents are fetched on demand. This is the single biggest architectural idea — it replaces embedding-based archival retrieval with *description-driven navigation*.
- `[[path]]` wiki-links cross-reference files; the agent is instructed to maintain them for discoverability

— https://docs.letta.com/concepts/memfs · https://www.letta.com/blog/context-repositories (2026-02-12)

## Retrieval: they removed the vector store

**[VERIFIED, and this is striking]:** *"MemFS does not include a semantic or vector index by default. Agents find memory in its Markdown files with normal file-search and read tools."* Keyword/semantic/hybrid search is an **optional mod** (`@letta-ai/memfs-search`, requiring QMD indexed over `$MEMORY_DIR`). They shipped `grep` as the default retrieval strategy for memory. Their own blog says RAG "is hard to do much better than just `grep`."

```json
{"command": "str_replace|insert|delete|rename|update_description|create",

```

Every memory edit is a **git commit with a mandatory human-readable reason**. That is free provenance and free undo. It's the best idea in the new design.

## Contradictions and forgetting — now explicitly handled

**[VERIFIED]** from the reflection subagent prompt (`src/agent/subagents/builtin/reflection.md`) — the most concrete policy statement Letta has ever published:

> **"Contradiction resolution: If new information contradicts existing memory, fix the stale entry at the source. Do not append the new version alongside the old."**

> "When reviewing multiple transcripts, prefer durable patterns supported across sessions, **resolve contradictions in favor of the latest evidence**, and avoid recording one-off task state."

> **"Archiving retired context:** Use the single non-system root file `ARCHIVE.md` when content should no longer be load-bearing but may still be useful as historical context — shrink or remove the active source, then append a concise dated entry to `ARCHIVE.md`. **Delete (don't archive)** content the user asked to forget, sensitive or wrong content, or junk with no future-reference value."

> "**Temporal references?** Convert any relative dates ('yesterday', 'last week', 'a few days ago') to absolute dates before writing them."

> "**Identity preservation:** Persona and behavioral files are load-bearing. Edit them surgically... Never rewrite them wholesale or silently overwrite established identity."

Its extraction priority order is: **(1) mistakes and corrections → (2) preferences and patterns → (3) new durable facts → (4) contradictions → (5) reusable procedures**, each passed through filters: durable-or-ephemeral, already-captured, generalizable, temporal-normalized, memory-or-skill. And: *"The raw conversation is already searchable — don't re-record it."*

So: **real forgetting (delete), real archival demotion (ARCHIVE.md), and destructive contradiction resolution** — all of which the legacy architecture lacked.

# What I'd actually take for a team knowledge brain

1. **The block schema** — `(label, description, value, limit, read_only)` with `chars_current`/`chars_limit` rendered into the prompt is a genuinely good, cheap design. The `description` field doing double duty as routing instructions is the underrated part.
2. **Two-tier loading** — always-in-context vs. tree+description-visible-contents-on-demand. This is more robust than embedding search and is where Letta ended up after three years.
3. **Exactly-once `old_string` matching** in `memory_replace` (vs. `core_memory_replace`'s `str.replace()` which silently replaces all occurrences). Copy the strict one.
4. **Mandatory `reason` on every write, persisted as an audit entry.** Free provenance.
5. **The absolute-dates rule.** "Do not write 'today' or 'recently'... the memory is persisted indefinitely."
6. **Destructive contradiction resolution + `ARCHIVE.md` demotion + genuine delete.** The legacy append-only archival design is the thing to *not* copy.
7. **Hybrid = BM25 + ANN fused with RRF, k=60, equal weights, no reranker**, returning fusion ranks to the model. Simple, and it's what they actually run in production against Turbopuffer.
8. **Background reflection triggered on compaction events** (not on a timer) — you get memory consolidation exactly when context is being lost, which is the moment it matters. Their default is `compaction-event`, not step-count, and that's the better default.

Things to be skeptical of: every published memory benchmark number in this space (LOCOMO is contested by all three of mem0/Zep/Letta, and Letta themselves concluded a plain filesystem beats purpose-built memory on it); the sleep-time compute numbers, which come from math benchmarks not memory ones; and the durability of any API in `letta-ai/letta`, which is in declared maintenance mode.</result>

# "Hermes Agent" — what it is, and how it manages memory

## 1. What "Hermes Agent" is

**Verdict: unambiguous. Confidence: high (verified against first-party docs, the GitHub repo, and the vendor's own domain).**

**Hermes Agent** is an open-source, self-hosted, self-improving AI agent from **Nous Research**, MIT-licensed, first released **25 Feb 2026**. Official site `hermes-agent.nousresearch.com`, repo `github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent`. Tagline: *"The Agent That Grows With You."* Latest release **v0.19.1 (v2026.7.30)**, 30 Jul 2026. GitHub shows ~224k stars; OpenRouter's app page ranks it **#1 daily globally**, ~29.9T tokens, ~400 models used, active since March 2026.

It runs as a CLI/TUI, a messaging gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp/Signal/Matrix/email/SMS), or a cron worker. It is **model-agnostic** — any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, vLLM, Bedrock, Vertex, etc.).

**Disambiguation — the other candidates I checked and ruled out:**
- **Nous Research's Hermes *model* family** (Hermes 4-14B/70B/405B, Hermes-4.3-36B; latest HF update Jan 2026, no Hermes 5) is a *separate* thing. The models ship no agent harness or memory mechanism; Hermes Agent does not require them.
- **`HERMES` (arXiv 2511.18760)** — "Towards Efficient and Verifiable Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs." Has a "memory module for proof continuity." Real, unrelated, almost certainly not what was meant.
- **No YC company, no separate framework, no AI-lab codename** named "Hermes Agent" surfaced. Sites like `hermes-agent.org`, `hermes-ai.net`, `hermesagents.net` are third-party SEO mirrors of the Nous project, not distinct products.
- One caution: several SEO articles claim Hermes' core memory *is* "holographic memory (SQLite + FTS5)." **That is wrong.** "Holographic" is one *optional* plugin provider (see §3).

## 2. How Hermes Agent manages memory

Six distinct layers, all local-first by default (`~/.hermes/`, per-profile, no telemetry).

**(a) Curated prompt memory — the core.** Two files in `~/.hermes/memories/`:

| File | Content | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `MEMORY.md` | agent's notes on world/env/projects | **2,200 chars** (~800 tok) |
| `USER.md` | notes on you: identity, prefs, style | **1,375 chars** (~500 tok) |

Read path: **auto-injected, not tool-fetched** — read off disk at session start and pasted into the system prompt as a **frozen snapshot** (entries delimited by `§`, with a usage-percentage header). Deliberate: freezing preserves the provider prefix cache. Mid-session writes hit disk immediately but **don't appear in the prompt until the next session**.

Write path: **model-decided**, via a `memory` tool with exactly three actions — `add`, `replace` (substring match on `old_text`), `remove`. **There is no `read` action.** At the cap the tool errors and forces the model to consolidate/remove within the same turn. Duplicates are auto-rejected; every entry is scanned for prompt-injection and invisible Unicode.

**(b) The nudge / background-review loop.** A counter `_turns_since_memory` on the agent instance; when it reaches `nudge_interval` the agent calls `_spawn_background_review` on a fork and reconsiders what to persist. `nudge_interval` is a real key (confirmed in issue #8506 where a user sets `nudge_interval: 3`); the widely-reported default is **10**, but note it is **not** in `config_defaults.py`'s `DEFAULT_CONFIG` — so it appears to be an undocumented code-level fallback. **Medium confidence on the value 10.**

**(c) Human-in-the-loop gate.** `memory.write_approval: true` stages writes for `/memory pending` → `/memory approve|reject <id>`. Same for skills (`/skills pending|diff|approve`), staged under `~/.hermes/pending/skills/`. `hermes journey` (aka `learning`, `memory-graph`) is a timeline UI to list/edit/delete accumulated memories and skills.

**(d) Episodic recall.** A `session_search` tool over `~/.hermes/state.db` — **SQLite + FTS5**. Unlimited capacity, ~20ms, zero standing token cost, returns real messages. This is the "did we discuss X last week" path.

**(e) Procedural memory = Skills.** `~/.hermes/skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md` (+ `references/`, `scripts/`, `templates/`), following the **agentskills.io** standard. Written autonomously by the agent via `skill_manage` (`create`/`patch`/`edit`/`write_file`/`delete`) after complex tasks. Three-tier progressive disclosure: `skills_list()` (~3k tok summaries) → `skill_view(name)` → `skill_view(name, path)`. A background **Curator** (`curator.interval_hours: 168`, `stale_after_days: 30`, `archive_after_days: 90`, `consolidate: false`) ages unused skills `active → stale → archived` and optionally LLM-merges duplicates.

**(f) Working-memory / context management.** A pluggable `context.engine` (default `ContextCompressor`). Defaults: `compression.threshold: 0.50` of the main model's context, `target_ratio: 0.20` tail budget, `protect_last_n: 20`, `protect_first_n: 3`; summary budget `min(context_length × 0.05, 12,000)`. Four phases: prune tool results >200 chars → find tail boundary (aligned so tool_call/tool_result pairs never split) → structured LLM summary of the middle (Goal / Constraints / Progress / Decisions / Files / Next Steps) → reassemble. A second 85% "gateway hygiene" pass runs before message handling. Plus Anthropic-style prompt caching (`prompt_caching.cache_ttl: "5m"|"1h"`, `system_and_3` strategy, ≤4 `cache_control` breakpoints, claimed ~75% input-cost reduction).

**Scoping:** per **profile**. "Each profile has its own memory store, session database, and skills directory. They are completely isolated." Multi-user gateway deployments isolate by allowlist + DM pairing, not by memory partition.

# "Hermes Agent" — what it is, and how it manages memory

## 1. What "Hermes Agent" is

**Verdict: unambiguous. Confidence: high (verified against first-party docs, the GitHub repo, and the vendor's own domain).**

**Hermes Agent** is an open-source, self-hosted, self-improving AI agent from **Nous Research**, MIT-licensed, first released **25 Feb 2026**. Official site `hermes-agent.nousresearch.com`, repo `github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent`. Tagline: *"The Agent That Grows With You."* Latest release **v0.19.1 (v2026.7.30)**, 30 Jul 2026. GitHub shows ~224k stars; OpenRouter's app page ranks it **#1 daily globally**, ~29.9T tokens, ~400 models used, active since March 2026.

It runs as a CLI/TUI, a messaging gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp/Signal/Matrix/email/SMS), or a cron worker. It is **model-agnostic** — any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, vLLM, Bedrock, Vertex, etc.).

**Disambiguation — the other candidates I checked and ruled out:**
- **Nous Research's Hermes *model* family** (Hermes 4-14B/70B/405B, Hermes-4.3-36B; latest HF update Jan 2026, no Hermes 5) is a *separate* thing. The models ship no agent harness or memory mechanism; Hermes Agent does not require them.
- **`HERMES` (arXiv 2511.18760)** — "Towards Efficient and Verifiable Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs." Has a "memory module for proof continuity." Real, unrelated, almost certainly not what was meant.
- **No YC company, no separate framework, no AI-lab codename** named "Hermes Agent" surfaced. Sites like `hermes-agent.org`, `hermes-ai.net`, `hermesagents.net` are third-party SEO mirrors of the Nous project, not distinct products.
- One caution: several SEO articles claim Hermes' core memory *is* "holographic memory (SQLite + FTS5)." **That is wrong.** "Holographic" is one *optional* plugin provider (see §3).

## 2. How Hermes Agent manages memory

Six distinct layers, all local-first by default (`~/.hermes/`, per-profile, no telemetry).

**(a) Curated prompt memory — the core.** Two files in `~/.hermes/memories/`:

| File | Content | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `MEMORY.md` | agent's notes on world/env/projects | **2,200 chars** (~800 tok) |
| `USER.md` | notes on you: identity, prefs, style | **1,375 chars** (~500 tok) |

Read path: **auto-injected, not tool-fetched** — read off disk at session start and pasted into the system prompt as a **frozen snapshot** (entries delimited by `§`, with a usage-percentage header). Deliberate: freezing preserves the provider prefix cache. Mid-session writes hit disk immediately but **don't appear in the prompt until the next session**.

Write path: **model-decided**, via a `memory` tool with exactly three actions — `add`, `replace` (substring match on `old_text`), `remove`. **There is no `read` action.** At the cap the tool errors and forces the model to consolidate/remove within the same turn. Duplicates are auto-rejected; every entry is scanned for prompt-injection and invisible Unicode.

**(b) The nudge / background-review loop.** A counter `_turns_since_memory` on the agent instance; when it reaches `nudge_interval` the agent calls `_spawn_background_review` on a fork and reconsiders what to persist. `nudge_interval` is a real key (confirmed in issue #8506 where a user sets `nudge_interval: 3`); the widely-reported default is **10**, but note it is **not** in `config_defaults.py`'s `DEFAULT_CONFIG` — so it appears to be an undocumented code-level fallback. **Medium confidence on the value 10.**

**(c) Human-in-the-loop gate.** `memory.write_approval: true` stages writes for `/memory pending` → `/memory approve|reject <id>`. Same for skills (`/skills pending|diff|approve`), staged under `~/.hermes/pending/skills/`. `hermes journey` (aka `learning`, `memory-graph`) is a timeline UI to list/edit/delete accumulated memories and skills.

**(d) Episodic recall.** A `session_search` tool over `~/.hermes/state.db` — **SQLite + FTS5**. Unlimited capacity, ~20ms, zero standing token cost, returns real messages. This is the "did we discuss X last week" path.

**(e) Procedural memory = Skills.** `~/.hermes/skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md` (+ `references/`, `scripts/`, `templates/`), following the **agentskills.io** standard. Written autonomously by the agent via `skill_manage` (`create`/`patch`/`edit`/`write_file`/`delete`) after complex tasks. Three-tier progressive disclosure: `skills_list()` (~3k tok summaries) → `skill_view(name)` → `skill_view(name, path)`. A background **Curator** (`curator.interval_hours: 168`, `stale_after_days: 30`, `archive_after_days: 90`, `consolidate: false`) ages unused skills `active → stale → archived` and optionally LLM-merges duplicates.

**(f) Working-memory / context management.** A pluggable `context.engine` (default `ContextCompressor`). Defaults: `compression.threshold: 0.50` of the main model's context, `target_ratio: 0.20` tail budget, `protect_last_n: 20`, `protect_first_n: 3`; summary budget `min(context_length × 0.05, 12,000)`. Four phases: prune tool results >200 chars → find tail boundary (aligned so tool_call/tool_result pairs never split) → structured LLM summary of the middle (Goal / Constraints / Progress / Decisions / Files / Next Steps) → reassemble. A second 85% "gateway hygiene" pass runs before message handling. Plus Anthropic-style prompt caching (`prompt_caching.cache_ttl: "5m"|"1h"`, `system_and_3` strategy, ≤4 `cache_control` breakpoints, claimed ~75% input-cost reduction).

**Scoping:** per **profile**. "Each profile has its own memory store, session database, and skills directory. They are completely isolated." Multi-user gateway deployments isolate by allowlist + DM pairing, not by memory partition.

## 3. "Options you can use by providers" — two different things, and one is almost certainly what was meant

Hermes uses the word "providers" for **two separate concepts**, which is very likely the source of the question.

### 3a. Memory Providers (this is the one) — VERIFIED

`~/.hermes/config.yaml` → `memory.provider: <id>`. Confirmed in `config_defaults.py`: the memory block contains `"provider": ""`. CLI: `hermes memory setup | status | off`.

**Nine built-in provider IDs** (docs prose still says "8" in places — stale; the enum and table both list 9):
