### NEW in 2026 (b) — Managed Agents **memory stores** (server-side memory, this is the big one)

This is a genuinely new *server-side* memory product distinct from the client-side `memory_20250818` tool, and it's the most directly relevant prior art for a MongoDB-backed knowledge layer.

- Public beta **April 23, 2026** under `managed-agents-2026-04-01`; memory-store endpoints later moved to their own beta header **`agent-memory-2026-07-22`** (July 2, 2026). Sending both headers on a memory-store request returns **400**. [VERIFIED from source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/api and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory]
- Model: a **memory store** (`memstore_...`) is a workspace-scoped collection of path-addressed text documents. Attached to a session via `resources: [{type: "memory_store", memory_store_id, access: "read_write"|"read_only", instructions}]` — **attach-at-creation only**, max **8 stores per session**, `instructions` capped at 4,096 chars. [VERIFIED from source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory]
- It's **mounted as a real directory** in the session sandbox at `/mnt/memory/<slugified-store-name>/`, exposed via `mount_path`. The agent uses ordinary file tools. Writes outside the mount go to container-local scratch and are lost. `access` is enforced at the filesystem level. A description of each mount is auto-injected into the system prompt. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Limits: 100 kB (~25k tokens) per memory, 2,000 memories per store.** Docs explicitly advise "many small focused files, not a few large ones." Hitting 2,000 makes new writes fail (both API and agent file writes). [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Full CRUD REST API**: `POST/GET /v1/memory_stores`, `.../memories` (create/list/retrieve/update/delete), with `path_prefix` (must end in `/`, matches whole segments) and `depth` (0 or 1 only). [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Optimistic concurrency** via `precondition: {type: "content_sha256", content_sha256: "..."}` on update. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Immutable audit trail**: every mutation creates a **memory version** (`memver_...`), retained ~30 days (recent versions always kept), surviving deletion of the parent memory. There's a **`POST .../memory_versions/{id}/redact`** endpoint explicitly positioned for "compliance workflows such as removing leaked secrets, PII, or user deletion requests" — i.e. a GDPR-erasure primitive. A version that is the current head cannot be redacted. There is **no restore endpoint**; you re-write the content. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Security warning worth quoting for a survey**: stores default to `read_write`, and "a successful prompt injection could write malicious content into the store. Later sessions then read that content as trusted memory." Docs recommend `read_only` for reference material. [VERIFIED from source: same]

### NEW in 2026 (c) — **Dreams** (Anthropic's consolidation/"sleep" pass)

Direct structural parallel to OpenAI's "dreaming," and to your repo's own consolidation job.

- Research preview announced **May 6, 2026**, gated by beta header **`dreaming-2026-04-21`** (dream endpoints need *both* `managed-agents-2026-04-01,dreaming-2026-04-21`). [VERIFIED from source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/api and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams]
- Mechanism: an **async job** taking (1) one pre-existing memory store and (2) **1–100 past session transcripts**, producing a **brand-new output memory store** with "duplicates merged, stale or contradicted entries replaced with the latest value, and new insights surfaced." **The input store is never modified** — you review and discard if you don't like it. [VERIFIED from source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams]
- `POST /v1/dreams` with `inputs[]` (`{type:"memory_store"}` + `{type:"sessions", session_ids:[...]}`), `model`, optional `instructions` (4,096 chars). Lifecycle: `pending` → `running` → `completed`/`failed`/`canceled`. `drm_...` IDs. Endpoints: retrieve, list, `/cancel`, `/archive`. Runtime "minutes to a few hours." Billed at standard token rates. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- Important nuance for anyone building this pattern: `instructions` steers **synthesis**, not editing — "imperative directives that target specific lines ('change sentence X to Y') generally produce no change." [VERIFIED from source: same]
- While running, `session_id` points at the underlying session so you can stream its events and watch it read/write. Supported models during preview: `claude-fable-5`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- Also: webhooks now cover `memory_store.*` (3 event types) and `environment.*` (4 event types) lifecycle, as of **July 22, 2026**. [VERIFIED from source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/api]

## 4. OpenAI Agents SDK sessions

**Python is far richer than TS. Python ships a first-party MongoDB session; TS does not.**

**Python** — `Session` protocol at `agents.memory.session.Session`, four methods: `async get_items(limit=None)`, `async add_items(items)`, `async pop_item()`, `async clear_session()`. [VERIFIED from source: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sessions/]

Implementations (exact import paths): [VERIFIED from source: same]
- `agents.memory.sqlite_session.SQLiteSession` — file-backed or in-memory
- `agents.memory.OpenAIConversationsSession` — server-managed via OpenAI's Conversations API
- `agents.memory.openai_responses_compaction_session.OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession` — auto or manual history compaction via Responses API
- `agents.extensions.memory.async_sqlite_session.AsyncSQLiteSession` (aiosqlite)
- `agents.extensions.memory.redis_session.RedisSession`
- `agents.extensions.memory.sqlalchemy_session.SQLAlchemySession`
- **`agents.extensions.memory.mongodb_session.MongoDBSession`** — "horizontally-scalable, multi-process session storage," monotonic sequence counters for ordering
- `agents.extensions.memory.dapr_session.DaprSession` — 30+ backends via Dapr sidecar
- `agents.extensions.memory.advanced_sqlite_session.AdvancedSQLiteSession` — conversation **branching** + usage analytics
- `agents.extensions.memory.encrypt_session.EncryptedSession` — transparent encryption wrapper over *any* session, with TTL expiry

**MongoDBSession specifics** (useful reference implementation for your `@repo/knowledge` layer): [VERIFIED from source: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/ref/extensions/memory/mongodb_session/]
```python
MongoDBSession(session_id: str, *, client: AsyncMongoClient[Any],
               database: str = "agents",
               sessions_collection: str = "agent_sessions",
               messages_collection: str = "agent_messages",
               session_settings: SessionSettings | dict | None = None)
```
Two collections: `agent_sessions` (`session_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `_seq` atomic counter) and `agent_messages` (`session_id`, `seq` monotonic int via atomic increment, `message_data` JSON). Indexes: unique on `session_id`; compound `(session_id, seq)`.

Config: `agents.memory.session_settings.SessionSettings` (`limit=None` → all items, `limit=N` → last N). `RunConfig` exposes `session_input_callback` (customize history/input merging) and `session_settings`. [VERIFIED from source: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sessions/]

**TypeScript/JS** — yes, sessions exist, but the backend story is much thinner. Exact interface: [VERIFIED from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-agents-js/main/packages/agents-core/src/memory/session.ts]
```typescript
export interface Session {
  getSessionId(): Promise<string>;
  getItems(limit?: number): Promise<AgentInputItem[]>;
  prepareHistoryItemForModelInput?(item: AgentInputItem): AgentInputItem;
  preserveReasoningItemIdsForPersistence?(): boolean;
  addItems(items: AgentInputItem[]): Promise<void>;
  popItem(): Promise<AgentInputItem | undefined>;
  clearSession(): Promise<void>;
}
```
Built-in JS implementations: **`MemorySession`**, **`OpenAIConversationsSession`**, **`OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession`**, plus marker interfaces `SessionHistoryRewriteAwareSession` and `OpenAIResponsesCompactionAwareSession`. **No built-in SQLite, Postgres, Redis, or MongoDB session in JS — you implement `Session` yourself.** [VERIFIED from source: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/sessions/]

**Takeaway for a TS/Mongo stack:** the JS SDK's `Session` is a 4-method interface you'd implement against your existing Mongo collections in well under 100 lines; the Python `MongoDBSession` schema above is a good template.

## 5. CrewAI memory

**CrewAI has been rewritten. The short-term / long-term / entity / external split is gone.**

- Current docs: "a **unified memory system** — a single `Memory` class that replaces separate short-term, long-term, entity, and external memory types with one intelligent API." Legacy types are **removed and consolidated**, not deprecated-but-present. [VERIFIED from source: https://docs.crewai.com/en/concepts/memory]
- **Storage backend is LanceDB (default), at `./.crewai/memory`** or a custom path via the `storage` param. **Not ChromaDB, not SQLite** anymore. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- Organization is **hierarchical scopes — filesystem-like paths** such as `/project/alpha` or `/agent/researcher`, enabling retrieval scoped to a subtree. `MemoryScope` restricts to a subtree; `MemorySlice` combines disjoint scopes. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- API: `remember(content, scope=None, source=None, private=False, categories=None)`, `recall(query, limit=10, depth="deep", scope=None, source=None)`, `extract_memories(raw_text)` (splits unstructured text into atomic facts), plus `remember_many()`, `forget()`, `scope()`, `slice()`, `tree()`, `info()`, `reset()`. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Retrieval is composite-scored**: semantic similarity × recency decay × LLM-assigned importance. Two recall modes: **"shallow"** (~200ms pure vector search) and **"deep"** (multi-step retrieval with LLM analysis, used for queries >200 chars). [VERIFIED from source: same]
- An **LLM is in the loop at three points**: ingestion (infers scope, categories, importance), query processing (deep recall), and extraction. Default LLM `gpt-4o-mini`; lazy init so missing API keys don't blow up construction. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Automatic consolidation/dedup** at a **0.85 similarity threshold**; non-blocking background writes, with `recall()` awaiting pending writes. Source tracking + privacy flags for multi-user isolation. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- Embedders: OpenAI (default `text-embedding-3-large`), Ollama, Azure OpenAI, Google AI/Vertex, Cohere, VoyageAI, AWS Bedrock, Hugging Face, Jina, IBM WatsonX, or a custom callable. [VERIFIED from source: same]

Agents share the crew memory by default; `Agent(memory=memory.scope("/agent/researcher"))` gives a scoped view. The crew auto-extracts facts from task outputs and injects recalled context before each task. [VERIFIED from source: same]

### A0. "Knowledge Engine" is NOT a product. Definitively.

The premise in your brief is wrong, and I can prove it four ways:

1. **Discovery doc**: `aiplatform` v1beta1 rev 20260725 contains **zero** resources, methods, or schemas containing "knowledge". Only 5 unique prose occurrences exist, all generic (e.g. `Retrieval` = "Defines a retrieval tool that model can call to access external knowledge"). There are **no** `knowledgeBases`, `knowledgeEngine`, or `knowledgeCorpora` endpoints in v1 **or** v1beta1.
2. **No such API host**: `knowledgeengine.googleapis.com`, `ragengine.googleapis.com`, `knowledge.googleapis.com`, `agentretrieval.googleapis.com` all return 404 on `$discovery/rest`. The Google APIs discovery directory (523 APIs) has no Knowledge Engine entry.
3. **Official rename table** (Agent Platform release notes, **April 22, 2026**) says exactly: `Vertex AI RAG Engine` → **`RAG Engine`**. Nothing about Knowledge Engine.
4. **Where the confusion comes from**: two places.
   - ADK docs (`google.github.io/adk-docs/sessions/memory/` — note: **`adk.dev/docs/sessions/memory/` 404s**) contain a comparison table saying `VertexAiRagMemoryService` → Persistence: *"Yes, stored in Knowledge Engine"*, *"indexed by Knowledge Engine"*, *"Requires Knowledge Engine"*. But the constructor on the same page is still `VertexAiRagMemoryService(rag_corpus="projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora/CORPUS_ID", similarity_top_k=5, vector_distance_threshold=0.6)`. It is ADK doc prose only, unsupported by any API surface or GCP doc.
   - The corpus management page is titled **"Manage your RAG knowledge base (corpus)"** — "knowledge base" is used as a plain-English synonym for `RagCorpus`.

**Verdict: "Knowledge Engine" is ADK documentation drift, not a rename. The product is RAG Engine; the resource is `ragCorpora`.**

### A1. Substrate

Two mutually-exclusive, project-level **deployment modes** (this is entirely new since May 2026 and is the single biggest thing a stale model gets wrong):

| | **Serverless mode** | **Spanner mode** |
|---|---|---|
| Resource storage | Fully-managed serverless DB | Dedicated Spanner Enterprise instance in a Google-owned per-customer project |
| Default vector DB | **`RagManagedVertexVectorSearch`** (a Vector Search 2.0 / Agent Retrieval Collection provisioned **in your project**) | `RagManagedDb` (Spanner) |
| CMEK | **Not supported** | Supported |
| VPC-SC | Supported | Supported |
| Allowed vector DBs | Managed VS 2.0, Pinecone, Weaviate | RagManagedDb, Managed VS 2.0, VS 1.0, Pinecone, Weaviate |
| Cost | Free for orchestration; vector DB billed directly | Tier-priced Spanner |
| Status | **Preview, us-central1 only**, no allowlist | GA, default if unset |

Data is **strictly isolated between modes**; switching modes hides (never deletes/moves) the other mode's corpora. Only one active at a time. Controlled via `GetRagEngineConfig` / `UpdateRagEngineConfig` (project-level singleton `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/ragEngineConfig`).

`RagManagedDbConfig` oneof: `.spanner{.basic|.scaled|.unprovisioned}` | `.serverless` | `.enterprise` (v1beta1 only). **`.basic`, `.scaled`, `.unprovisioned` at the top level of `RagManagedDbConfig` are explicitly marked "Deprecated: Use `mode` instead to set the tier under Spanner."**

Spanner tier sizing (exact): **Basic = 100 processing units (0.1 node) fixed, with backup** (default). **Scaled = autoscaling min 1 node (1,000 PU) → max 10 nodes (10,000 PU), with backup.** **Unprovisioned = deletes the Spanner instance and ALL RAG data, unrecoverable, halts billing.**

### A2. Write path

```

PATCH .../ragCorpora/{id}                                               (patch; also triggers ANN rebuild)

POST  upload/v1beta1/.../ragCorpora/{id}/ragFiles:upload                (UploadRagFile, media)
DELETE .../ragCorpora/{id}/ragFiles/{fid}
```
v1beta1-only metadata plane (**Preview**, and **not supported in Serverless mode**):

POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE .../ragCorpora/{id}/ragFiles/{fid}/ragMetadata[:batchCreate|:batchDelete]
```
`RagDataSchema` types: `INTEGER | FLOAT | STRING | DATETIME | BOOLEAN | LIST` (value fields `int_value`, `float_value`, `str_value`, `datetime_value` RFC3339, `bool_value`, `list_value`).

`ImportRagFilesConfig` sources: `gcsSource`, `googleDriveSource`, `jiraSource`, `slackSource`, `sharePointSources`. Sinks: `importResultGcsSink`, `importResultBigquerySink` (the older `partialFailureGcsSink` / `partialFailureBigquerySink` are **Deprecated**). `ragFileMetadataConfig` is **"Deprecated: Not in use."**

### A8. `RagCorpus.corpusTypeConfig.memoryCorpus` — the memory-corpus path

```
RagCorpusCorpusTypeConfig {
  documentCorpus {}                       // empty message, no fields
  memoryCorpus { llmParser: RagFileParsingConfigLlmParser }
}
```
**Status: v1beta1 ONLY (the whole `corpusTypeConfig` / `CorpusTypeConfig` schema is absent from v1 GA), and the only doc covering it — "Use RAG Engine in Gemini Live API" — carries an `Experimental` banner (weaker than Preview).**

What it actually is: a corpus whose ingestion path is the **Gemini Live API session transcript**, not files. You set `VertexRagStore.storeContext = true` on the retrieval tool and Gemini auto-memorizes the client↔Gemini interaction into that corpus and retrieves from it on later turns, **including across different Live API sessions**. It stores/indexes **text and audio speech**. The `llmParser` is mandatory and is what turns raw session context into indexed memory (`llmParser.modelName` example in docs: `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06`). Embedding models: "currently supports Google first-party embedding models" (e.g. `text-embedding-005`).

Assessment: this is a *thin, experimental* memory path — no scoping keys, no consolidation, no revisions, no TTL, no purge. It is not competitive with Memory Bank. If you want agent memory on GCP, Memory Bank is the real product (below).

## TOPIC A′ — Memory Bank (you didn't ask, but this is the actual agent-memory substrate and it changed enormously)

This is where a May-2026 model is most wrong.

**New: `memoryBanks` is a first-class URL collection in BOTH v1 (GA) and v1beta1.**
```
POST   v1/projects/{p}/locations/{l}/memoryBanks/{mbId}:ingestEvents
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories            (create)
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieve
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:generate
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:purge
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieveProfiles     (v1beta1 only)
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories/{mId}:rollback
GET    .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories/{mId}/revisions[/{rId}]
```
plus a **global (no project/location) alias**: `v1beta1/memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieve` etc.

⚠️ **Trap**: every parameter description under `memoryBanks/*` still says *"The resource name of the ReasoningEngine…  Format: `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/reasoningEngines/{reasoning_engine}`"*. And the docs create a Memory Bank via `client.agent_engines.create(...)`, returning a `reasoningEngines/...` name. So **`memoryBanks/{id}` is a URL alias over the same ReasoningEngine resource** — there is no `memoryBanks.create`/`.list`/`.delete`. Deleting the Agent Runtime instance deletes the memories.

- **Substrate**: managed; config lives at `ReasoningEngine.contextSpec.memoryBankConfig`.
- **Write**: `CreateMemory` (explicit), `GenerateMemories` (LLM extract+consolidate; sources = `vertexSessionSource` | `directContentsSource` | `directMemoriesSource` (≤ **5** pre-extracted facts); **request max size 8 MB**), `IngestEvents` (**GA July 8 2026**; streaming with `generationTriggerConfig.generationRule{eventCount, idleDuration, fixedInterval, overlapEventCount}`; **unflushed streams auto-flush 24 h after last event**).
- **Read**: `RetrieveMemories` with `similaritySearchParams{searchQuery, topK}` or `simpleRetrievalParams{pageSize,pageToken}` — **default 3, max 100, values >100 coerced to 100**. AIP-160 `filter` on `fact`/`create_time`/`update_time`/`topics`; `filterGroups` = disjunctive-normal-form metadata filters (OR of ANDs) with ops `EQUAL|GREATER_THAN|LESS_THAN` + `negate`. `RetrieveProfiles` returns low-latency structured profiles.
- **Granularity**: `Memory{fact, structuredContent{data, schemaId}, topics[], metadata{}, scope{}, ttl, expireTime}`. `memoryType ∈ {NATURAL_LANGUAGE_COLLECTION, STRUCTURED_PROFILE}`.
- **Scoping**: `scope` is a required immutable arbitrary string map (e.g. `{"user_id":"123","agent_name":"x"}`). Retrieval requires **exact** key+value match (case-sensitive, order-insensitive). Wildcard `*` forbidden in values.
- **Consolidation/dedup**: LLM ADD/UPDATE/DELETE against existing same-scope memories. `consolidationConfig.revisionsPerCandidateCount` (default **1**) controls how many prior revisions the consolidator inspects. `disableConsolidation`, `metadataMergeStrategy ∈ {OVERWRITE, MERGE, REQUIRE_EXACT_MATCH}`. Managed topics: `USER_PERSONAL_INFO | USER_PREFERENCES | KEY_CONVERSATION_DETAILS | EXPLICIT_INSTRUCTIONS`; plus `customMemoryTopic{label, description}` and `generateMemoriesExamples` few-shots; `enableThirdPersonMemories` (default false = first person); `disableNaturalLanguageMemories`.
- **Versioning/audit/deletion**: **`MemoryRevision`** immutable snapshots with `extractedMemories[]{fact, structuredData, context}` showing pre-consolidation extraction. `:rollback{targetRevisionId}`. **Default revision TTL 365 days** (`memoryRevisionDefaultTtl`). After parent memory deletion, revisions remain inspectable/recoverable for **48 hours**. `disableMemoryRevisions` at instance or request level. `PurgeMemories{filter, filterGroups, force}` — `force=false` validates only.
- **Defaults changed**: generation model is **`gemini-3.5-flash` effective June 29, 2026** (was `gemini-2.5-flash`; instances created before that date keep 2.5-flash). Embedding default `text-embedding-005`; **`gemini-embedding-2` supported since July 8, 2026 but ONLY with `global`, `us`, or `eu` in the model resource name — regional (`us-central1`) is rejected.**
- **Regions**: 23 single regions + **multi-region `us`/`eu` and `global` (GA June 17, 2026)**. Memory Bank specifically **not** supported in `asia-southeast2`, `australia-southeast2`, `northamerica-northeast2`. **CMEK is impossible on the `global` endpoint.**
- **IAM**: scope-level IAM Conditions via API attribute **`aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope`** in CEL, e.g. `api.getAttribute('aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope', {})['userId'] == 'userA'`. Specialized roles **`roles/aiplatform.memoryViewer` / `memoryEditor` / `memoryUser`**. Limits: **1,500 unique principals per IAM policy**; conditions **not supported on multi-scope methods**. Docs warn to prefer positive conditions (empty scope matches negative conditions overly broadly).
- **Pricing (effective September 1, 2026)**: Storage **$0.30/GiB-month** (Agent Storage, *includes revisions*); Reads **1 Agent Compute vCPU-h ($0.085) per 3,000,000 read ops**; Writes **$0.085 per 1,000,000 write ops**; generation + embedding tokens billed separately at model SKUs. Sessions is priced identically.
- **Prompt injection**: docs explicitly name **memory poisoning** as a risk and recommend **Model Armor**, adversarial testing/red teaming, and sandboxed execution.

## TOPIC B — Agent Retrieval (formerly Vector Search 2.0)

**It is a separate API on its own host — this is the single most important structural fact.**

`https://vectorsearch.googleapis.com/` — "Vector Search API", rev **20260723**, versions **v1alpha / v1beta / v1** all present. Python client: `google.cloud.vectorsearch_v1beta`, `VectorSearchServiceClient`. gcloud surface: `gcloud vector-search collections create`. P4 SA: `service-{PROJECT_NUMBER}@gcp-sa-vectorsearch.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.

Resource model replaces "index-as-a-service" with **Collections of Data Objects**:
```
v1beta/projects/{p}/locations/{l}/collections                      POST/GET
       .../collections/{c}                                         GET/PATCH/DELETE
       .../collections/{c}:importDataObjects   :exportDataObjects
       .../collections/{c}/dataObjects                             POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE
       .../collections/{c}/dataObjects:batchCreate :batchUpdate :batchDelete
       .../collections/{c}/dataObjects:search  :batchSearch  :query  :aggregate
       .../collections/{c}/indexes                                 POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE
```
- **Write**: `DataObject{ name, dataObjectId (1–63 chars, RFC1035), data{}, vectors{}, etag }` — **optimistic concurrency via `etag`**. Collection has `dataSchema` (**JSON Schema Draft‑7**) + `vectorSchema`.
- **Auto-embedding**: `DenseVectorField{ dimensions, vertexEmbeddingConfig{ modelId, taskType, textTemplate } }` where `textTemplate` interpolates data fields (`"Movie Title: {title} ---- Movie Plot: {plot}"`). `taskType ∈ RETRIEVAL_QUERY | RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT | SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY | CLASSIFICATION | CLUSTERING | QUESTION_ANSWERING | FACT_VERIFICATION | CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY`. Auto-embedding calls `aiplatform.googleapis.com` and burns *both* quotas.
- **Read**: `:search` with oneof `semanticSearch{searchText, searchField, taskType, topK, filter, outputFields, searchHint}` | `vectorSearch{searchField, vector|sparseVector, topK, distanceMetric, filter}` | `textSearch{searchText, dataFieldNames[], topK}`. Filters are **MongoDB-style JSON structs**: `{"genre": {"$eq": "sci-fi"}}`. `:batchSearch` fuses sub-searches via `Ranker{ rrf{weights[]} | vertexRanker{model, topN, textRecordSpec} }` — **`vertexRanker.model` currently supports only `semantic-ranker-fast@latest`**. `pageSize` max **1000** (KNN only). `:query` = metadata-only filter query, default page 100, max 1000.
- **Indexes**: `Index{ indexField, denseScann{featureNormType: NONE|UNIT_L2_NORM}, filterFields[], storeFields[], distanceMetric: DOT_PRODUCT(default)|COSINE_DISTANCE, dedicatedInfrastructure{mode: STORAGE_OPTIMIZED|PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZED, autoscalingSpec{minReplicaCount default 2, ≥1 ≤1000; maxReplicaCount ≤1000, v1beta default max(min,5)}} }`. A Collection can hold multiple indexes (one per vector field). `searchHint` lets you force index vs KNN; default = use index if present, else fall back to KNN.
- **VS 1.0 migration**: `ImportDataObjects` with flag **`detect_and_convert_vs1_json`**; `restricts` → `data.restricts` + `data.restricts_deny`; `numeric_restricts` → `data.numeric_restricts`; `embedding`→`vectors.embedding.dense_vector`, `sparse_embedding`→`vectors.sparse_embedding.sparse_vector` (`dimensions`→`indices`).
- **Regions (9)**: asia-east1, asia-northeast1, asia-southeast1, europe-north1, europe-west2, europe-west4, us-central1, us-east4, us-west1.
- **CMEK**: `encryptionSpec.cryptoKeyName`, KMS key must be **same region**, **immutable — cannot be enabled on an existing Collection** (must export → new Collection → import). **No manual or automatic re-encryption/rewrap.** Keep old key versions ≥30 days. **VPC-SC supported.**
- **Quotas** are all metric-named `vectorsearch.googleapis.com/<metric>`, sliding-window per calendar minute, **429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` with `reason="RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED"` and the metric in `quota_metric`**. Metrics: control-plane `collection_management_requests`, `collection_read_requests`, `collection_list_requests`, `index_management_requests`, `index_read_requests`, `index_list_requests`, `lro_requests`; data-plane (per project/region/**per Collection**) `data_object_writes`, `data_object_reads`, `query_requests`, `search_requests` (ANN dense/sparse **and** text/semantic), `knn_search_requests` (exhaustive KNN), `batch_search_requests` (1 per call regardless of sub-searches, but sub-searches also count), `data_object_write_bytes`; allocation counts `collections`, `indexes`, `concurrent_index_operations`, `concurrent_collection_operations`, `concurrent_data_object_imports`, `concurrent_data_object_exports`. **Google does not publish the numeric default values on this page** — only the metric taxonomy.
- **Pricing (exact)**: Index Serving CUs — **Storage-Optimized CU $2.30/hour (includes 1 TB SSD)**; **Performance-Optimized CU $0.065/hour (includes 2 GB RAM)**; **Data Write/Update $0.45/GiB** (incl. initial build & full overwrite). Payload DB — **Data Stored $0.000410959/GiB-hour**; **Read ops $0.06 per 100,000**; **Write/Update/Delete ops $0.18 per 100,000**. Metering: a search = *Index Scan Cost* (1 read per batch of **up to 100 data objects** in the index) **+** *Document Retrieval Cost* (1 read per document returned). Direct read = 1 doc = 1 read. 1 doc = 1 write. Embedding model billed separately.
- **Status**: the API is `v1beta` in all doc samples; the docs still headline "Agent Retrieval (formerly Vector Search 2.0)". Vector Search 1.0 continues to exist separately (its own quotas: 5 concurrent index creates, 5 concurrent updates, 50 deployed index nodes, 5 N2D nodes, 100 indexes, 6,000 streaming update RPM; $3.00/GiB index build, $0.45/GiB streaming insert, per-node-hour serving).

**Relevance to agent memory**: it is the *default* embedding store behind RAG Engine Serverless mode (`ragManagedVertexVectorSearch`), so it is now indirectly the substrate under RAG-as-memory. It has no memory semantics of its own (no scope, no consolidation, no TTL) — it's a vector+payload DB.

There is also a **new `ces` v1beta — "Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience API"**, plus `agentidentity` v1alpha, `agentidentitycredentials` v1alpha, `agentregistry` v1alpha, `developerknowledge` v1alpha in the directory.

### Does Gemini Enterprise offer end-user agent memory/personalization primitives?

**Yes — a fully productized, console-driven one, named "Personalization and Memory."** It is *not* Memory Bank and has no public API surface; it is end-user/admin UI.

- **Personalization** GA **July 31, 2025**. **"Save information as memories"** shipped **November 21, 2025**.
- Doc: `gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-personalization` — "Configure personalization and memory".
- Mechanics: Gemini Enterprise builds a **personal Memory** from (a) an explicit **user personalization profile** (Preferred name, role/job title, industry), (b) **Conversation history** toggle, (c) **connected data sources** (Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft OneDrive, etc. — extracts insights from email/calendar/docs), (d) **saved memories** created conversationally.
- Write path: user says *"Remember that all new proposals for Project Walby should be reviewed by @Roberto Moreno"* → agent replies *"I created a new memory: …"*. Update by restating. 
- Read path: `Settings > Personalization > Reference saved memories` toggle gates whether saved memories are injected into conversations.
- Delete: conversational (*"Forget my memory about X"*, *"Remove from memory"*) or `Settings > Personalization > Managed saved memories > Manage` → per-item delete or **Delete all**.
- **Admin controls**: `Gemini Enterprise app > Configurations > Feature Management > Memory and customization` toggle disables memory + personalization profiles **for all users org-wide**. **On by default.** Admins also control which data sources may be connected.
- **Known caveats stated in the docs**: data-source changes take **up to 24 hours** to take effect; **"The core memory feature is enabled by default. You can't disable the memory feature"** (end-users can only opt out of sources/saved-memory reference); **deleting a saved memory may not remove the information if the originating conversation is still saved — you must delete the conversation too.**
- Separate, older API-level primitive: **"Personalize responses from the answer method"** — GA **February 27, 2025** — pass user info on `answer` calls (`gemini/enterprise/docs/answer`).
- Security surface: dedicated `cmek`, `use-vpc-service-controls`, `access-transparency`, `audit-logging`, `identity`/`identity-mapping`, `enable-model-armor`, `org-policy-custom-constraints` pages. Model Armor screens Gemini Enterprise / Notebook Enterprise prompts and responses.

## TOPIC A — RAG Engine

### A0. "Knowledge Engine" is NOT a product. Definitively.

The premise in your brief is wrong, and I can prove it four ways:

1. **Discovery doc**: `aiplatform` v1beta1 rev 20260725 contains **zero** resources, methods, or schemas containing "knowledge". Only 5 unique prose occurrences exist, all generic (e.g. `Retrieval` = "Defines a retrieval tool that model can call to access external knowledge"). There are **no** `knowledgeBases`, `knowledgeEngine`, or `knowledgeCorpora` endpoints in v1 **or** v1beta1.
2. **No such API host**: `knowledgeengine.googleapis.com`, `ragengine.googleapis.com`, `knowledge.googleapis.com`, `agentretrieval.googleapis.com` all return 404 on `$discovery/rest`. The Google APIs discovery directory (523 APIs) has no Knowledge Engine entry.
3. **Official rename table** (Agent Platform release notes, **April 22, 2026**) says exactly: `Vertex AI RAG Engine` → **`RAG Engine`**. Nothing about Knowledge Engine.
4. **Where the confusion comes from**: two places.
   - ADK docs (`google.github.io/adk-docs/sessions/memory/` — note: **`adk.dev/docs/sessions/memory/` 404s**) contain a comparison table saying `VertexAiRagMemoryService` → Persistence: *"Yes, stored in Knowledge Engine"*, *"indexed by Knowledge Engine"*, *"Requires Knowledge Engine"*. But the constructor on the same page is still `VertexAiRagMemoryService(rag_corpus="projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora/CORPUS_ID", similarity_top_k=5, vector_distance_threshold=0.6)`. It is ADK doc prose only, unsupported by any API surface or GCP doc.
   - The corpus management page is titled **"Manage your RAG knowledge base (corpus)"** — "knowledge base" is used as a plain-English synonym for `RagCorpus`.

**Verdict: "Knowledge Engine" is ADK documentation drift, not a rename. The product is RAG Engine; the resource is `ragCorpora`.**

### A1. Substrate

Two mutually-exclusive, project-level **deployment modes** (this is entirely new since May 2026 and is the single biggest thing a stale model gets wrong):

| | **Serverless mode** | **Spanner mode** |
|---|---|---|
| Resource storage | Fully-managed serverless DB | Dedicated Spanner Enterprise instance in a Google-owned per-customer project |
| Default vector DB | **`RagManagedVertexVectorSearch`** (a Vector Search 2.0 / Agent Retrieval Collection provisioned **in your project**) | `RagManagedDb` (Spanner) |
| CMEK | **Not supported** | Supported |
| VPC-SC | Supported | Supported |
| Allowed vector DBs | Managed VS 2.0, Pinecone, Weaviate | RagManagedDb, Managed VS 2.0, VS 1.0, Pinecone, Weaviate |
| Cost | Free for orchestration; vector DB billed directly | Tier-priced Spanner |
| Status | **Preview, us-central1 only**, no allowlist | GA, default if unset |

Data is **strictly isolated between modes**; switching modes hides (never deletes/moves) the other mode's corpora. Only one active at a time. Controlled via `GetRagEngineConfig` / `UpdateRagEngineConfig` (project-level singleton `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/ragEngineConfig`).

`RagManagedDbConfig` oneof: `.spanner{.basic|.scaled|.unprovisioned}` | `.serverless` | `.enterprise` (v1beta1 only). **`.basic`, `.scaled`, `.unprovisioned` at the top level of `RagManagedDbConfig` are explicitly marked "Deprecated: Use `mode` instead to set the tier under Spanner."**

Spanner tier sizing (exact): **Basic = 100 processing units (0.1 node) fixed, with backup** (default). **Scaled = autoscaling min 1 node (1,000 PU) → max 10 nodes (10,000 PU), with backup.** **Unprovisioned = deletes the Spanner instance and ALL RAG data, unrecoverable, halts billing.**

### A8. `RagCorpus.corpusTypeConfig.memoryCorpus` — the memory-corpus path

```
RagCorpusCorpusTypeConfig {
  documentCorpus {}                       // empty message, no fields
  memoryCorpus { llmParser: RagFileParsingConfigLlmParser }
}
```
**Status: v1beta1 ONLY (the whole `corpusTypeConfig` / `CorpusTypeConfig` schema is absent from v1 GA), and the only doc covering it — "Use RAG Engine in Gemini Live API" — carries an `Experimental` banner (weaker than Preview).**

What it actually is: a corpus whose ingestion path is the **Gemini Live API session transcript**, not files. You set `VertexRagStore.storeContext = true` on the retrieval tool and Gemini auto-memorizes the client↔Gemini interaction into that corpus and retrieves from it on later turns, **including across different Live API sessions**. It stores/indexes **text and audio speech**. The `llmParser` is mandatory and is what turns raw session context into indexed memory (`llmParser.modelName` example in docs: `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06`). Embedding models: "currently supports Google first-party embedding models" (e.g. `text-embedding-005`).

Assessment: this is a *thin, experimental* memory path — no scoping keys, no consolidation, no revisions, no TTL, no purge. It is not competitive with Memory Bank. If you want agent memory on GCP, Memory Bank is the real product (below).

## TOPIC A′ — Memory Bank (you didn't ask, but this is the actual agent-memory substrate and it changed enormously)

This is where a May-2026 model is most wrong.

**New: `memoryBanks` is a first-class URL collection in BOTH v1 (GA) and v1beta1.**
```
POST   v1/projects/{p}/locations/{l}/memoryBanks/{mbId}:ingestEvents
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories            (create)
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieve
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:generate
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:purge
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieveProfiles     (v1beta1 only)
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories/{mId}:rollback
GET    .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories/{mId}/revisions[/{rId}]
```
plus a **global (no project/location) alias**: `v1beta1/memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieve` etc.

⚠️ **Trap**: every parameter description under `memoryBanks/*` still says *"The resource name of the ReasoningEngine…  Format: `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/reasoningEngines/{reasoning_engine}`"*. And the docs create a Memory Bank via `client.agent_engines.create(...)`, returning a `reasoningEngines/...` name. So **`memoryBanks/{id}` is a URL alias over the same ReasoningEngine resource** — there is no `memoryBanks.create`/`.list`/`.delete`. Deleting the Agent Runtime instance deletes the memories.

- **Substrate**: managed; config lives at `ReasoningEngine.contextSpec.memoryBankConfig`.
- **Write**: `CreateMemory` (explicit), `GenerateMemories` (LLM extract+consolidate; sources = `vertexSessionSource` | `directContentsSource` | `directMemoriesSource` (≤ **5** pre-extracted facts); **request max size 8 MB**), `IngestEvents` (**GA July 8 2026**; streaming with `generationTriggerConfig.generationRule{eventCount, idleDuration, fixedInterval, overlapEventCount}`; **unflushed streams auto-flush 24 h after last event**).
- **Read**: `RetrieveMemories` with `similaritySearchParams{searchQuery, topK}` or `simpleRetrievalParams{pageSize,pageToken}` — **default 3, max 100, values >100 coerced to 100**. AIP-160 `filter` on `fact`/`create_time`/`update_time`/`topics`; `filterGroups` = disjunctive-normal-form metadata filters (OR of ANDs) with ops `EQUAL|GREATER_THAN|LESS_THAN` + `negate`. `RetrieveProfiles` returns low-latency structured profiles.
- **Granularity**: `Memory{fact, structuredContent{data, schemaId}, topics[], metadata{}, scope{}, ttl, expireTime}`. `memoryType ∈ {NATURAL_LANGUAGE_COLLECTION, STRUCTURED_PROFILE}`.
- **Scoping**: `scope` is a required immutable arbitrary string map (e.g. `{"user_id":"123","agent_name":"x"}`). Retrieval requires **exact** key+value match (case-sensitive, order-insensitive). Wildcard `*` forbidden in values.
- **Consolidation/dedup**: LLM ADD/UPDATE/DELETE against existing same-scope memories. `consolidationConfig.revisionsPerCandidateCount` (default **1**) controls how many prior revisions the consolidator inspects. `disableConsolidation`, `metadataMergeStrategy ∈ {OVERWRITE, MERGE, REQUIRE_EXACT_MATCH}`. Managed topics: `USER_PERSONAL_INFO | USER_PREFERENCES | KEY_CONVERSATION_DETAILS | EXPLICIT_INSTRUCTIONS`; plus `customMemoryTopic{label, description}` and `generateMemoriesExamples` few-shots; `enableThirdPersonMemories` (default false = first person); `disableNaturalLanguageMemories`.
- **Versioning/audit/deletion**: **`MemoryRevision`** immutable snapshots with `extractedMemories[]{fact, structuredData, context}` showing pre-consolidation extraction. `:rollback{targetRevisionId}`. **Default revision TTL 365 days** (`memoryRevisionDefaultTtl`). After parent memory deletion, revisions remain inspectable/recoverable for **48 hours**. `disableMemoryRevisions` at instance or request level. `PurgeMemories{filter, filterGroups, force}` — `force=false` validates only.
- **Defaults changed**: generation model is **`gemini-3.5-flash` effective June 29, 2026** (was `gemini-2.5-flash`; instances created before that date keep 2.5-flash). Embedding default `text-embedding-005`; **`gemini-embedding-2` supported since July 8, 2026 but ONLY with `global`, `us`, or `eu` in the model resource name — regional (`us-central1`) is rejected.**
- **Regions**: 23 single regions + **multi-region `us`/`eu` and `global` (GA June 17, 2026)**. Memory Bank specifically **not** supported in `asia-southeast2`, `australia-southeast2`, `northamerica-northeast2`. **CMEK is impossible on the `global` endpoint.**
- **IAM**: scope-level IAM Conditions via API attribute **`aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope`** in CEL, e.g. `api.getAttribute('aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope', {})['userId'] == 'userA'`. Specialized roles **`roles/aiplatform.memoryViewer` / `memoryEditor` / `memoryUser`**. Limits: **1,500 unique principals per IAM policy**; conditions **not supported on multi-scope methods**. Docs warn to prefer positive conditions (empty scope matches negative conditions overly broadly).
- **Pricing (effective September 1, 2026)**: Storage **$0.30/GiB-month** (Agent Storage, *includes revisions*); Reads **1 Agent Compute vCPU-h ($0.085) per 3,000,000 read ops**; Writes **$0.085 per 1,000,000 write ops**; generation + embedding tokens billed separately at model SKUs. Sessions is priced identically.
- **Prompt injection**: docs explicitly name **memory poisoning** as a risk and recommend **Model Armor**, adversarial testing/red teaming, and sandboxed execution.

       .../collections/{c}/indexes                                 POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE
```
- **Write**: `DataObject{ name, dataObjectId (1–63 chars, RFC1035), data{}, vectors{}, etag }` — **optimistic concurrency via `etag`**. Collection has `dataSchema` (**JSON Schema Draft‑7**) + `vectorSchema`.
- **Auto-embedding**: `DenseVectorField{ dimensions, vertexEmbeddingConfig{ modelId, taskType, textTemplate } }` where `textTemplate` interpolates data fields (`"Movie Title: {title} ---- Movie Plot: {plot}"`). `taskType ∈ RETRIEVAL_QUERY | RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT | SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY | CLASSIFICATION | CLUSTERING | QUESTION_ANSWERING | FACT_VERIFICATION | CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY`. Auto-embedding calls `aiplatform.googleapis.com` and burns *both* quotas.
- **Read**: `:search` with oneof `semanticSearch{searchText, searchField, taskType, topK, filter, outputFields, searchHint}` | `vectorSearch{searchField, vector|sparseVector, topK, distanceMetric, filter}` | `textSearch{searchText, dataFieldNames[], topK}`. Filters are **MongoDB-style JSON structs**: `{"genre": {"$eq": "sci-fi"}}`. `:batchSearch` fuses sub-searches via `Ranker{ rrf{weights[]} | vertexRanker{model, topN, textRecordSpec} }` — **`vertexRanker.model` currently supports only `semantic-ranker-fast@latest`**. `pageSize` max **1000** (KNN only). `:query` = metadata-only filter query, default page 100, max 1000.
- **Indexes**: `Index{ indexField, denseScann{featureNormType: NONE|UNIT_L2_NORM}, filterFields[], storeFields[], distanceMetric: DOT_PRODUCT(default)|COSINE_DISTANCE, dedicatedInfrastructure{mode: STORAGE_OPTIMIZED|PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZED, autoscalingSpec{minReplicaCount default 2, ≥1 ≤1000; maxReplicaCount ≤1000, v1beta default max(min,5)}} }`. A Collection can hold multiple indexes (one per vector field). `searchHint` lets you force index vs KNN; default = use index if present, else fall back to KNN.
- **VS 1.0 migration**: `ImportDataObjects` with flag **`detect_and_convert_vs1_json`**; `restricts` → `data.restricts` + `data.restricts_deny`; `numeric_restricts` → `data.numeric_restricts`; `embedding`→`vectors.embedding.dense_vector`, `sparse_embedding`→`vectors.sparse_embedding.sparse_vector` (`dimensions`→`indices`).
- **Regions (9)**: asia-east1, asia-northeast1, asia-southeast1, europe-north1, europe-west2, europe-west4, us-central1, us-east4, us-west1.
- **CMEK**: `encryptionSpec.cryptoKeyName`, KMS key must be **same region**, **immutable — cannot be enabled on an existing Collection** (must export → new Collection → import). **No manual or automatic re-encryption/rewrap.** Keep old key versions ≥30 days. **VPC-SC supported.**
- **Quotas** are all metric-named `vectorsearch.googleapis.com/<metric>`, sliding-window per calendar minute, **429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` with `reason="RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED"` and the metric in `quota_metric`**. Metrics: control-plane `collection_management_requests`, `collection_read_requests`, `collection_list_requests`, `index_management_requests`, `index_read_requests`, `index_list_requests`, `lro_requests`; data-plane (per project/region/**per Collection**) `data_object_writes`, `data_object_reads`, `query_requests`, `search_requests` (ANN dense/sparse **and** text/semantic), `knn_search_requests` (exhaustive KNN), `batch_search_requests` (1 per call regardless of sub-searches, but sub-searches also count), `data_object_write_bytes`; allocation counts `collections`, `indexes`, `concurrent_index_operations`, `concurrent_collection_operations`, `concurrent_data_object_imports`, `concurrent_data_object_exports`. **Google does not publish the numeric default values on this page** — only the metric taxonomy.
- **Pricing (exact)**: Index Serving CUs — **Storage-Optimized CU $2.30/hour (includes 1 TB SSD)**; **Performance-Optimized CU $0.065/hour (includes 2 GB RAM)**; **Data Write/Update $0.45/GiB** (incl. initial build & full overwrite). Payload DB — **Data Stored $0.000410959/GiB-hour**; **Read ops $0.06 per 100,000**; **Write/Update/Delete ops $0.18 per 100,000**. Metering: a search = *Index Scan Cost* (1 read per batch of **up to 100 data objects** in the index) **+** *Document Retrieval Cost* (1 read per document returned). Direct read = 1 doc = 1 read. 1 doc = 1 write. Embedding model billed separately.
- **Status**: the API is `v1beta` in all doc samples; the docs still headline "Agent Retrieval (formerly Vector Search 2.0)". Vector Search 1.0 continues to exist separately (its own quotas: 5 concurrent index creates, 5 concurrent updates, 50 deployed index nodes, 5 N2D nodes, 100 indexes, 6,000 streaming update RPM; $3.00/GiB index build, $0.45/GiB streaming insert, per-node-hour serving).

**Relevance to agent memory**: it is the *default* embedding store behind RAG Engine Serverless mode (`ragManagedVertexVectorSearch`), so it is now indirectly the substrate under RAG-as-memory. It has no memory semantics of its own (no scope, no consolidation, no TTL) — it's a vector+payload DB.

# MASTRA — agent memory deep dive (as of 2026-08-02)

## 0. Headline: what changed since May 2026 knowledge cutoff

The single most important thing: **Mastra's memory story is no longer "working memory + semantic recall."** The flagship system is now **Observational Memory (OM)**, added in `@mastra/memory@1.1.0` (Feb 2026), and the docs explicitly recommend it over both working memory and semantic recall for long-running agents. ## 2. Threads / resources model

- **Thread** = one conversation/session. **Resource** = the owner entity (user, org, project, document). [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/message-history.md]
- Passed per-call:
  ```typescript
  await agent.generate('Hello', {
    memory: {
      thread: { id: 'thread-123', title: 'Support conversation', metadata: { category: 'billing' } },
      resource: 'user-456',
    },
  })
  ```
  A bare string is also allowed for `thread`. [VERIFIED: same]
- **Hard constraint**: "Each thread has an owner (`resourceId`) that can't be changed after creation." Reusing a thread ID across owners causes query errors. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/overview.md]
- **Multi-agent delegation scoping** (supervisor → subagent): fresh `threadId` per delegation, and a *deterministic* `resourceId` = `` `{parentResourceId}-{agentName}` ``, so resource-scoped memory persists across delegations but never leaks between sibling subagents. Subagents inherit the supervisor's `Memory` instance unless they define their own. `generateTitle` is deliberately NOT run on inherited subagent threads. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/overview.md]
- **Memory sharing between agents** is achieved simply by passing the same `resourceId` (resource-scoped layers shared) or the same `resourceId` + `threadId` (full history shared). [VERIFIED: same]
- **Multi-user threads**: a thread has exactly one `resourceId`, so the documented pattern for group chat is to key `resourceId` on the conversation (`doc_${docId}`) and tag every user message in the body with `<turn author_id=... author_name=... functional_role=...>`. Security note in docs: build the tag server-side from authenticated context, never from the request body. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/multi-user-threads.md]
- **No built-in access control**: "The memory system doesn't enforce access control. Before running any query, verify in your application logic that the current user is authorized to access the `resourceId`." [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/message-history.md]

## 4. Working memory — full detail

**What it is**: a persisted block of Markdown *or* a JSON object matching a Standard-Schema (Zod/Valibot/ArkType), injected into the **system message** and updated by the agent via a tool call. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/working-memory.md]

### Config keys (`options.workingMemory`)
From the actual type (`packages/core/src/memory/types.ts`) [VERIFIED: raw.githubusercontent.com/.../types.ts]:

```typescript
type BaseWorkingMemory = {
  enabled: boolean;
  scope?: 'thread' | 'resource';   // @default 'resource'
  useStateSignals?: boolean;       // @default false  (experimental)
  agentManaged?: boolean;          // @default true
  use?: never;                     // @deprecated — removed; always tool-call mode
};
type TemplateWorkingMemory = (BaseWorkingMemory & { template: string; schema?: never; version?: 'stable' })
  | (Omit<BaseWorkingMemory,'useStateSignals'> & { template: string; schema?: never; version: 'vnext'; useStateSignals?: false });
type SchemaWorkingMemory = BaseWorkingMemory & { schema: PublicSchema; template?: never };
export type WorkingMemory = TemplateWorkingMemory | SchemaWorkingMemory | WorkingMemoryNone;
```

- **`template` and `schema` are mutually exclusive** (enforced at the type level).
- **`readOnly`** is set per-call under `memory.options.readOnly`, not on `workingMemory`. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/working-memory.md]

### Template vs schema semantics
- **Template (Markdown) = REPLACE semantics** — the agent must emit the whole blob each update.
- **Schema (JSON) = MERGE semantics** — deep-merge; `null` deletes a field; **arrays are replaced wholesale, never merged element-wise**. Implementation is `deepMergeWorkingMemory()` in `packages/memory/src/tools/working-memory.ts`. [VERIFIED: docs + source]

### The tool
- Registered tool **name** is **`updateWorkingMemory`** (tool `id` internally is `'update-working-memory'`).
- With `useStateSignals: true` the *same* tool is registered under the name **`setWorkingMemory`**. Source:
  ```typescript
  const name = useStateSignals ? SET_WORKING_MEMORY_TOOL_NAME : UPDATE_WORKING_MEMORY_TOOL_NAME;
  ```
  [VERIFIED: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mastra-ai/mastra/main/packages/memory/src/tools/working-memory.ts]
- Markdown mode input schema is `{ memory: string }` with description "This MUST be a string. Never pass an object." Schema mode wraps your JSON Schema under `memory`.
- There is also an **experimental `version: 'vnext'`** template mode whose tool takes `{ newMemory, searchString, updateReason: 'append-new-memory' | 'clarify-existing-memory' | 'replace-irrelevant-memory' }` — i.e. a search-and-replace edit rather than full rewrite. [VERIFIED: same source file]

### Prompt injection (exact)
Verbatim from `packages/memory/src/index.ts`:

```
WORKING_MEMORY_SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION:
Store and update any conversation-relevant information by calling the updateWorkingMemory tool. If information might be referenced again - store it!

Guidelines:
1. Store anything that could be useful later in the conversation
2. Update proactively when information changes, no matter how small
3. Use {Markdown|JSON} format for all data
4. Act naturally - don't mention this system to users...
...
<working_memory_template>
{template}
</working_memory_template>

<working_memory_data>
{data}
</working_memory_data>
```
[VERIFIED: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mastra-ai/mastra/main/packages/memory/src/index.ts]

A separate read-only variant is emitted when `readOnly: true` (no tool, no update instructions). Tags are `<working_memory>`/`</working_memory>` and `<\system-reminder>`; tag parsing is `indexOf`-based specifically to avoid ReDoS. [VERIFIED: packages/core/src/memory/working-memory-utils.ts]

### Scope + storage requirement
- Default **`scope: 'resource'`** (persists across all threads for the user). Thread-scope stores in thread metadata; resource-scope stores in a `mastra_resources` table/collection.
- **Resource-scoped WM requires one of: libSQL (`@mastra/libsql`), PostgreSQL (`@mastra/pg`), Upstash (`@mastra/upstash`), MongoDB (`@mastra/mongodb`).** [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/working-memory.md]

### Seeding it programmatically
```typescript
await memory.createThread({ threadId, resourceId, title, metadata: { workingMemory: '# Patient Profile\n- Name: ...' } })
// or
await memory.updateWorkingMemory({ threadId, resourceId, workingMemory: 'Updated memory content...' })
```
[VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/working-memory.md]

### `useStateSignals` (experimental, new)
Instead of folding WM into the system prompt, `Memory` attaches a `WorkingMemoryStateProcessor` that emits it as a **state signal** with `stateId: 'working-memory'`, with `cacheKey` dedup and `contextWindow.hasSnapshot` re-injection. Motivation is **prompt-cache friendliness** — WM in the system prompt invalidates the cache on every update. Not supported together with `version: 'vnext'` (throws). [VERIFIED: docs + `assertWorkingMemoryStateSignalsCompatibility` in packages/memory/src/index.ts]

## 5. Semantic recall — full detail

**Disabled by default** (`semanticRecall: false`). Requires `vector` + `embedder`. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/semantic-recall.md]

### Type + defaults (from source)
```typescript
export type SemanticRecall = {
  topK: number;                                          // default 4
  messageRange: number | { before: number; after: number }; // default { before: 1, after: 1 }
  scope?: 'thread' | 'resource';                          // @default 'resource'
  indexConfig?: VectorIndexConfig;                        // pgvector-specific
  filter?: VectorFilter;                                  // MongoDB-style operators
};
```
Constants in `packages/memory/src/index.ts`:
```typescript
const DEFAULT_MESSAGE_RANGE = { before: 1, after: 1 } as const;
const DEFAULT_TOP_K = 4;
```
[VERIFIED: raw.githubusercontent.com/.../packages/memory/src/index.ts and .../packages/core/src/memory/types.ts]

**What `messageRange` means mechanically**: after the vector query returns top-K hits, Mastra converts each hit's `metadata.message_id` + `metadata.thread_id` into an `include` entry with `withPreviousMessages: messageRange.before` and `withNextMessages: messageRange.after`, and re-fetches those neighbours from the *relational* store. So it's a hydration window around each hit, not a vector-side setting. Source:
```typescript
{ id: r.metadata?.message_id, threadId: r.metadata?.thread_id,
  withNextMessages: this.messageRange.after,
  withPreviousMessages: this.messageRange.before }
```
[VERIFIED: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mastra-ai/mastra/main/packages/core/src/processors/memory/semantic-recall.ts]

### Scoping mechanics
Resource vs thread scope is a **metadata filter on the vector query**, not separate indexes:
```typescript
filter: this.scope === 'resource' && resourceId ? { resource_id: resourceId } : { thread_id: threadId }
```
Embedding metadata written on save is `{ message_id, thread_id, resource_id }`. [VERIFIED: same file]
- Guard: resource-scoped recall **throws** if no `resourceId` is provided — "A missing ID never expands the search." [VERIFIED: packages/memory/src/index.ts + https://mastra.ai/blog/agent-memory-layers]
- `scope: 'resource'` is supported by **LibSQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Upstash** adapters. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/semantic-recall.md]

### Index naming (important if you're mirroring this design)
```typescript
protected getEmbeddingIndexName(dimensions?: number): string {
  const defaultDimensions = 1536;
  const usedDimensions = dimensions ?? defaultDimensions;
  const isDefault = usedDimensions === defaultDimensions;
  const separator = this.vector?.indexSeparator ?? '_';
  return isDefault ? `memory${separator}messages` : `memory${separator}messages${separator}${usedDimensions}`;
}
```
So: **`memory_messages`** at 1536 dims, **`memory_messages_768`** etc. otherwise. It also requests `createParams.metadataIndexes = ['thread_id', 'resource_id']`. OM's observation index is `memory_observations_<dim>` (fallback dim 384). Note: the *standalone* `SemanticRecall` processor uses a different auto-name, `` `mastra_memory_${sanitizedModel}` `` truncated to 63 chars — a divergence worth knowing. [VERIFIED: packages/core/src/memory/memory.ts and packages/core/src/processors/memory/semantic-recall.ts]

### Embedders
`ModelRouterEmbeddingModel` with `provider/model` strings — OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small|3-large|ada-002`, Google `gemini-embedding-001`, OpenRouter. Local option: `@mastra/fastembed` (`fastembed`, 384-dim). MongoDB docs additionally showcase **`@mastra/voyageai`** (`voyage`, default `voyage-3.5`, 1024 dims) — a package first published 2026-06-12, latest 0.4.0. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/semantic-recall.md, https://mastra.ai/reference/vectors/mongodb.md, npm registry]

### Metadata filtering (new)
`semanticRecall.filter` supports `$and $or $eq $ne $gt $gte $lt $lte $in $nin` against thread metadata copied onto embeddings at save time. Caveat documented: "If thread metadata changes later, existing embeddings keep their previous metadata until those messages are saved or indexed again." [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/semantic-recall.md]

### Undocumented-in-docs knob
The `SemanticRecall` processor also accepts `threshold?: number` (min similarity 0–1) and `embedderOptions` (e.g. Google `outputDimensionality`), which are *not* surfaced through `Memory.options.semanticRecall`. [VERIFIED: packages/core/src/processors/memory/semantic-recall.ts]

### Official position on semantic recall
Docs now actively discourage it: "In practical terms, OM replaces both working memory and message history, and has greater accuracy (and lower cost) than Semantic Recall." [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/observational-memory.md]

## 6. Observational Memory (the 2026 flagship)

**Added in `@mastra/memory@1.1.0`.** Two background agents — an **Observer** and a **Reflector** — maintain a dense observation log that replaces raw message history. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/observational-memory.md, https://mastra.ai/reference/memory/observational-memory.md]

```typescript
memory: new Memory({ options: { observationalMemory: true } })
```

### Key numbers (all verified from the reference page)
| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | `'google/gemini-2.5-flash'` | for both Observer and Reflector |
| `scope` | `'thread'` | `'resource'` is **experimental** |
| `observation.messageTokens` | **30,000** | unobserved-message token trigger for Observer |
| `reflection.observationTokens` | **40,000** | observation-log token trigger for Reflector |
| `observation.bufferTokens` | **0.2** | background buffering every 20% of threshold (~6k) |
| `observation.bufferActivation` | **0.8** | on activation, drop ~80% of history (keep ~20%, ~6k) |
| `observation.blockAfter` | **1.2** | hard sync-observation ceiling at 36k |
| `reflection.bufferActivation` | **0.5** | start background reflection at 50% of 40k |
| `reflection.blockAfter` | **1.2** | 48k |
| `observation.previousObserverTokens` | **2000** | tail-truncated prior observations fed to Observer |
| `temporalMarkers` | `false` | inserts marker when ≥10 min gap |
| `activateOnProviderChange` | `false` | |
| `activateAfterIdle` | none | `number | '5m' | '1hr' | 'auto'` |
| `shareTokenBudget` | `false` | pools the two budgets; requires `bufferTokens: false` |
| `retrieval` | `false` | `true` \| `{ vector?: boolean; scope?: 'thread' \| 'resource' }`, scope default `'resource'` |
| `observation.modelSettings.maxOutputTokens` | 100,000 (default-model selection only) | |

### Mechanics worth copying
- **Append-only, prompt-cacheable**: observations append rather than being retrieved per turn, so the prompt prefix stays stable. This is the core architectural bet vs. RAG-style memory.
- **Reflection rewrites the entire log** — it is not a third growing layer. "Each reflection rewrites the entire observation log... Memory stays bounded around the reflection threshold no matter how long the conversation runs."
- **Observation format**: two-level Markdown bullets with emoji priority + timestamps:
  ```md
  Date: 2026-01-15
  - 🔴 12:10 User is building a Next.js app with Supabase auth, due in 1 week (meaning January 22nd 2026)
    - 🟡 12:12 User asked about middleware configuration for protected routes
  ```
- **Three-date temporal model** (per the research post): *observation date*, *referenced date* ("my flight is January 31"), *relative date* ("2 days from today"). This is the only explicit temporal model in Mastra. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/research/observational-memory]
- **Token counting** uses `tokenx` locally, with provider-aware image heuristics, and caches per-part estimates in `part.providerMetadata.mastra`. Callers may supply authoritative estimates via `providerMetadata.mastra.tokenEstimate = { v: 0, source: 'client', key: 'client', tokens: 100_000 }`.
- **`ModelByInputTokens`** (added `@mastra/memory@1.10.0`) — tiered model selection by input size:
  ```typescript
  new ModelByInputTokens({ upTo: { 5_000: 'openrouter/mistralai/ministral-8b-2512', 40_000: 'openai/gpt-5-mini', 1_000_000: 'google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview' } })
  ```
- **Extractors** (`@mastra/memory@1.22.0+`) — typed structured extraction piggybacking on the Observer's already-primed context:
  ```typescript
  new Extractor({
    name: 'User profile',
    instructions: 'Extract stable user profile facts that should be remembered.',
    schema: z.object({ preferredName: z.string().optional(), timezone: z.string().optional() }),
    includePreviousExtraction: true,        // default
    metadataKeyPath: 'extracted.<slug>',    // default; false to skip persistence
    onExtracted: async ({ current, sendSignal }) => current.trim().toLowerCase(),
  })
  ```
  Built-ins `current-task`, `suggested-response`, `thread-title` use the same pipeline. Results stream as `data-om-observation-end` / `data-om-buffering-end` chunks. [VERIFIED: reference + https://mastra.ai/blog/introducing-memory-extractors]
- **`observation.manageWorkingMemory: true`** — OM's Observer owns working-memory updates instead of the main agent (adds `WorkingMemoryExtractor`, sets `workingMemory.agentManaged: false` and `workingMemory.useStateSignals: true`). This is Mastra's answer to "the agent forgets to call the tool."
- **Retrieval mode** — each observation group stores a `range` (`startId:endId`) pointing at the source messages, and a **`recall` tool** is registered with `mode: 'messages' | 'threads' | 'search'`, `cursor`, `anchor`, `page`, `limit` (default 20), `detail: 'low' | 'high'`, `partType`, `toolName`, `partIndex`, `before`/`after` ISO dates. `{ vector: true }` reuses the Memory instance's vector store/embedder for semantic search over observation groups.
- **Storage support for OM**: `@mastra/pg`, `@mastra/libsql`, `@mastra/mysql`, `@mastra/mongodb`, `@mastra/convex` only.
- **Async buffering is disabled automatically in `scope: 'resource'`.**
- Standalone use: `ObservationalMemory` + `ObservationalMemoryProcessor` from `@mastra/memory/processors`, wired into `inputProcessors`/`outputProcessors`.

### Client-integration gotcha (repeated across three doc pages)
"When you use OM with a client application, send **only the new message** from the client instead of the full conversation history" — otherwise client timestamps collide with stored ones and message ordering breaks. [VERIFIED: overview.md, message-history.md, observational-memory.md]

## 7. Memory processors

The docs page has been rewritten: **memory itself is now implemented as processors** in the agent pipeline. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/memory-processors.md]

**Auto-added when memory is enabled** (all from `@mastra/core/processors`):
- **`MessageHistory`** — hybrid. Input: fetch last-N + prepend (tagged `source: 'memory'`). Output: persist new messages, filter incomplete tool calls, bump thread `updatedAt`, skip if `readOnly`. Options: `{ storage: MemoryStorage, lastMessages?: number }`, `id = 'message-history'`.
- **`SemanticRecall`** — hybrid. Input: vector search + prepend. Output: embed & upsert new messages. `id = 'semantic-recall'`.
- **`WorkingMemory`** — input only. Injects WM as a system message. Options: `{ storage, template: { format: 'markdown'|'json', content: string }, scope, useVNext, readOnly, templateProvider, logger }`, `id = 'working-memory'`.

**Deduplication rule**: if you manually place one of these in `inputProcessors`/`outputProcessors`, Mastra will *not* auto-add its own — you get full ordering control.

**Execution order** (this is the load-bearing design detail):
```
Input:  [Memory Processors] → [Your inputProcessors]
Output: [Your outputProcessors] → [Memory Processors]
```
Rationale: an output guardrail that calls `abort()` runs *before* persistence, so **nothing is written to memory**. Same for aborting input guardrails (LLM never called, output processors skipped).

**`TokenLimiter` and `ToolCallFilter` are NOT memory processors** in current Mastra — they're generic processors you compose manually.
- `TokenLimiterProcessor` (`id = 'token-limiter'`), options `{ limit: number; strategy?: 'truncate' | 'abort' (default 'truncate'); countMode?: 'cumulative' | 'part' (default 'cumulative'); trimMode?: 'best-fit' | 'contiguous' (default 'best-fit') }`. Accepts a bare number. Uses `tokenx` (the old tiktoken `encoding` option is deprecated & ignored). Works as input processor (trim history) *or* output processor (cap generation). [VERIFIED: packages/core/src/processors/processors/token-limiter.ts]
- `ToolCallFilter` (`id = 'tool-call-filter'`), options `{ exclude?: string[]; filterAfterToolSteps?: number; preserveModelOutput?: boolean }`. No args = exclude **all** tool calls/results. [VERIFIED: .../tool-call-filter.ts]

**Custom processor interface** (`@mastra/core/processors`):
```typescript
export interface Processor<TId extends string = string, TTripwireMetadata = unknown> {
  readonly id: TId;
  readonly name?: string;
  processInput?(args: ProcessInputArgs): Promise<ProcessInputResult> | ProcessInputResult;
  processInputStep?(args: ...): ...;            // runs every step, incl. tool continuations
  processOutputStream?(args): Promise<ChunkType | null | undefined>;
  processOutputResult?(args): ProcessorMessageResult;
  processOutputStep?(...): ...;
  computeStateSignal?(...); processLLMRequest?(...); processLLMResponse?(...);
}
```
Docs' worked example is an `AttachmentUploader` that swaps base64 data URIs for URLs before persistence — motivated by a documented **record-size limits table**: DynamoDB 400 KB, Convex 1 MiB, Cloudflare D1 1 MiB; "PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and libSQL have higher limits and are usually unaffected." Docs also warn: "avoid mutating the input `messages` array or its objects directly." [VERIFIED: docs + packages/core/src/processors/index.ts]

Other shipped processors relevant to context management: `BatchParts`, `CostGuard`, `Moderation`, `PIIDetector`, `PromptInjectionDetector`, `RegexFilter`, `ResponseCache`, `SystemPromptScrubber`, `UnicodeNormalizer`, `LanguageDetector`, `SkillSearch`, `ToolSearch`, `StructuredOutput`, `ProviderHistoryCompat`, `PrefillErrorHandler`, `StreamErrorRetry`. [VERIFIED: gh contents packages/core/src/processors/processors + https://mastra.ai/llms.txt]

## 9. MongoDB support — the part that matters most for you

**Yes. `@mastra/mongodb` is a first-class, dual-purpose package: `MongoDBStore` (storage domains) + `MongoDBVector` (Atlas Vector Search).** It is one of only four adapters supporting resource-scoped working memory, one of four supporting resource-scoped semantic recall, and one of five supporting Observational Memory.

### `MongoDBStore` config
```typescript
import { MongoDBStore } from '@mastra/mongodb'
const storage = new MongoDBStore({
  id: 'mongodb-storage',
  uri: process.env.MONGODB_URI,        // `url` is deprecated
  dbName: process.env.MONGODB_DB_NAME,
  options: { retryWrites: true, maxPoolSize: 10, serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 5000, socketTimeoutMS: 45000 },
  disableInit: false,                  // true => you must call storage.init() yourself
  skipDefaultIndexes: false,
  indexes: [{ collection: 'mastra_threads', keys: { 'metadata.type': 1 } }],
  // connectorHandler?: ConnectorHandler
})
```
Requires **MongoDB Atlas (cloud or Atlas Local via Docker) with Atlas Search enabled; MongoDB 7.0+ recommended**. `init()` is called automatically when passed to `new Mastra({ storage })`, but **must be called manually** if used standalone — otherwise "storage operations will fail silently or throw." ### `MongoDBVector` — genuinely sophisticated, and the most interesting thing in the whole repo for a MongoDB engineer
```typescript
const store = new MongoDBVector({
  id: 'mongodb-vector',
  uri, dbName,
  embeddingFieldPath: 'text.contentEmbedding', // default: 'embedding'; dotted paths supported
})
```
Notable capabilities [all VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/reference/vectors/mongodb.md]:
- **`createIndex({ indexName, dimension, metric = 'cosine', filterFields, collectionName, searchIndexName, allowWrites })`**
  - `searchIndexName` defaults to **`` `${indexName}_vector_index` ``**.
  - **`filterFields`** declares metadata fields as vectorSearch filter fields (registered as `metadata.<field>`) so filters get **pushed into `$vectorSearch`** instead of pre-filtering candidate `_id`s — explicitly to avoid "the 16 MB BSON limit on large result sets". Undeclared fields silently fall back to the pre-filter.
  - **Bring-your-own (BYO) collections**: pass `collectionName` to index an existing operational collection. **BYO is read-only by default** — `upsert/updateVector/deleteVector/deleteVectors` throw a USER-category error unless `allowWrites: true`. The policy is **persisted durably** and survives restarts; pre-flag entries "fail closed."
  - `deleteIndex()` on a BYO index drops the Atlas indexes but **preserves the collection and documents**. Managed indexes drop the whole collection.
- **`query({ indexName, queryVector, topK = 10, filter, documentFilter, includeVector = false, numCandidates = 20*topK capped at 10000, metadataMode = 'field' })`**
  - **`metadataMode: 'document'`** returns the full source document as `metadata` and matches filters against the **root** document (no `metadata.` prefix) — designed for BYO operational collections.
  - Native **`ObjectId` `_id`s supported**; results coerce to string per the `QueryResult.id` contract, and deletes/updates accept the string back.
- **`createSearchIndex()` / `waitForSearchIndexReady()` / `textQuery()`** — Atlas Search BM25. Managed indexes auto-create a dynamic `${collectionName}_search_index`; BYO requires explicit opt-in (billable). Field-mapped indexes get a distinct default name `${collectionName}_${indexName}_search_fields_index` to avoid being shadowed.
- **`hybridQuery({ queryVector, query, paths, topK, weights: { vector, text }, ... })`** — uses **server-side `$rankFusion`**. Documented requirement: **MongoDB ≥ 8.0, GA from 8.1**; on 8.0.x "may need a MongoDB support case to enable."
- `waitForIndexReady({ timeoutMs = 60000, checkIntervalMs = 2000 })`; `listIndexes()` returns *logical* names, with an internal registry collection that's never listed.

### MongoDB TTL as first-class retention
The retention reference has a dedicated section recommending native TTL indexes as an alternative to `prune()`:
```typescript
new MongoDBStore({
  id: 'mongodb-storage', uri, dbName,
  indexes: [
    { collection: 'mastra_messages', keys: { createdAt: 1 }, options: { expireAfterSeconds: 30*24*60*60 } },
    { collection: 'mastra_threads',  keys: { createdAt: 1 }, options: { expireAfterSeconds: 90*24*60*60 } },
    { collection: 'mastra_ai_spans', keys: { startedAt: 1 }, options: { expireAfterSeconds: 7*24*60*60 } },
  ],
})
```
[VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/reference/storage/retention.md]

## 10. Eviction / TTL / forgetting / temporal

There is **no automatic per-item TTL or decay in the memory layer**. What exists:

1. **Storage retention + `prune()`** (opt-in, age-based): declare `retention: { memory: { messages: { maxAge: '30d' }, threads: { maxAge: '90d', batchSize: 500 } } }`, then call `await storage.prune({ maxRows, pauseMs, signal, maxBatches, retention })` from *your own* scheduler — "Mastra never runs it for you." Returns `PruneResult[] = { domain, table, deleted, done }`; batched (default `batchSize: 1000`), resumable, cancellable, never VACUUMs. Anchor columns: memory.threads/messages/resources → `createdAt`. **Reference implementations: libSQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB.** Anchor indexes are created lazily on first prune. Notably: "The memory `observational_memory` table has no timestamp anchor, so it can't be age-pruned." [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/reference/storage/retention.md]
2. **MongoDB TTL indexes** as the zero-maintenance alternative (above).
3. **OM reflection = semantic compaction**: bounded memory forever, since each reflection rewrites the whole log.
4. **`deleteMessages()`**, **`cloneThread()`** (branching/checkpointing before destructive ops).
5. **Temporal model**: OM's three-date scheme (observation / referenced / relative) + `temporalMarkers: true` (≥10-min gap inserts a persisted marker + transient reminder event). Message-level date filtering via `recall({ filter: { dateRange: { start, end, startExclusive, endExclusive } } })`. That's the extent of it — no recency decay, no importance scoring beyond the Observer's 🔴/🟡/🟢 emoji priorities.

## 14. Takeaways if you're designing MongoDB-backed agent memory

1. **Mastra's memory now sits behind a processor pipeline**, not inside the storage layer. `MessageHistory` / `SemanticRecall` / `WorkingMemory` are ordinary `Processor`s that Mastra injects, and the input/output ordering (`memory → yours` on input, `yours → memory` on output) is what makes guardrail-aborts non-persisting. That's a clean, copyable pattern.
2. **The `resource` vs `thread` scope axis is the whole memory model**, and it's implemented as nothing more than a metadata filter (`{ resource_id }` vs `{ thread_id }`) plus a `mastra_resources` document for working memory. Cheap to replicate.
3. **`MongoDBVector`'s BYO-collection design is the most transferable piece**: logical index name ≠ physical collection, durable registration of write-policy and index names in a registry collection, `filterFields` to push filters into `$vectorSearch` (16MB BSON escape hatch), `metadataMode: 'document'` for operational documents, `$rankFusion` hybrid with weight tuning, and read-only-by-default with explicit `allowWrites` opt-in.
4. **Mastra has effectively deprecated semantic-recall-as-memory** in favor of an append-only, prompt-cacheable observation log with a rewrite-on-threshold compaction step. If you're building agent memory in 2026, that architectural bet (stable cacheable prefix > per-turn retrieval) is the thing to evaluate, and the 30k/40k token thresholds + 0.2/0.8 buffer ratios are concrete starting parameters.
5. **Retention is opt-in and manual** — Mastra never runs `prune()` for you, and the OM collection can't be age-pruned at all. On MongoDB they explicitly recommend native TTL indexes instead.

## 0. Headline: the six things that actually matter

Across every primary source I read, the same skeleton recurs. Concretely for a fact-extraction memory system:

1. **Separate retrieval quality from generation quality.** Chroma's Context-1 report makes this an explicit design principle: "if the downstream model fails to answer correctly, it is ambiguous whether the search agent retrieved insufficient evidence or the reasoning model failed to use what was provided" — so they deliberately do *not* evaluate end-to-end, and instead verify the answer-bearing document appears in the output set `[V]` (https://www.trychroma.com/research/context-1). Zep's practical guide makes the same call, naming **Context Completeness** (COMPLETE / PARTIAL / INSUFFICIENT) their *primary* metric precisely because it "isolates memory system performance from LLM generation quality," with Answer Correctness as secondary `[V]` (https://www.getzep.com/ai-agents/how-to-test-agent-memory/).
2. **Build your golden set from YOUR documents.** Public benchmark rank order does not transfer (Chroma, below).
3. **Always report accuracy, latency, and token count together.** Zep: "Always report accuracy alongside latency and token consumption together" `[V]`.
4. **Judge alignment is a first-class metric.** You measure the judge before you trust the judge.
5. **Distinguish capability evals (start low, drive up) from regression evals (stay ~100%)** — Anthropic `[V]`.
6. **Measure consistency, not just success:** `pass^k`, not just `pass@k` — Anthropic `[V]`.

- **Contradiction rate, staleness, memory growth rate, dedup rate** — I found **no** primary engineering writeup that defines or reports these as tracked production metrics. `[V — absence verified across Chroma, Zep, Letta, LangChain, Anthropic sources read]`.
