### D.8 RAG metric formulas worth borrowing

[V] [RAGAS](https://docs.ragas.io/en/stable/concepts/metrics/available_metrics/):
- **Faithfulness** = supported claims / total claims. **= your extraction precision.** A non-LLM variant uses **Vectara HHEM‑2.1‑Open**, cheap enough for continuous scoring.
- **Context Precision@K** = `Σ(Precision@k × v_k) / (total relevant in top K)` — rank-sensitive. **The ID-based variant** = matching IDs / total retrieved IDs is deterministic and free for a fact store where everything has an `_id`.
- **Context Recall** = reference claims supported by retrieved context / total reference claims. **= your extraction recall** against a hand-written reference fact list.
- **Context Entities Recall** — **= your entity coverage** on people/orgs.
- **Noise Sensitivity** = incorrect claims / total claims.

[V] [TruLens RAG triad](https://www.trulens.org/getting_started/core_concepts/rag_triad/): Context Relevance (**per chunk**, because *"any irrelevant information in the context could be weaved into a hallucination"*), Groundedness (claim-by-claim evidence search), Answer Relevance. Designed for *"the common case in enterprises where ground truth data sets are often limited."*

[V] [DeepEval](https://deepeval.com/docs/metrics-introduction): all metrics 0–1 against a threshold (default 0.5); **DAG** gives deterministic decision-tree scoring; **Knowledge Retention** (multi-turn) is the closest off-the-shelf metric to "did the memory keep what it should have"; **PIILeakage** for your GDPR path.

### D.9 Human review queue metrics

**Krippendorff's α, not Cohen's κ** [V] ([κ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohen%27s_kappa), [α](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krippendorff%27s_alpha)). Reviewers dip in and out and coverage per fact is uneven — κ can't handle incomplete data, α can (needs ≥2 values per unit, any number of coders, any measurement level). **Thresholds: α ≥ 0.800 reliable; 0.667–0.800 tentative only; <0.667 discard.** Beware the **kappa paradox**: κ *"tends to underestimate agreement on the rare category"* — with a 90% accept rate κ will look terrible even with excellent agreement. Report raw agreement, α, **and** the confusion matrix.

**Fellegi–Sunter for the review queue itself** [V] ([record linkage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_linkage)): per-identifier `m` = P(agree | match), `u` = P(agree | non-match by chance); agreement weight `log₂(m/u)`, disagreement weight `log₂((1−m)/(1−u))`; sum and compare against **two thresholds** → **match / non-match / uncertain**, where **uncertain routes to manual review**. That is literally the architecture of your review queue, from 1969. **Blocking** raises precision at the cost of recall.

**Calibration for auto-accept thresholds** [V] ([Guo et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.04599), [sklearn](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html)):
- `ECE = Σ_m (n_m/n)·|acc_m − conf_m|`, **M=15 bins**
- `MCE = max_m |acc_m − conf_m|` — **use MCE for the band you auto-accept without review**; one badly-calibrated band is unacceptable there
- **Temperature scaling** `softmax(z/T)`: one parameter, preserves ranking — the right default
- ⚠️ *"A lower Brier loss doesn't necessarily mean better calibration"* — Brier conflates reliability, resolution and uncertainty. Pair ECE with a reliability diagram.
- Platt/sigmoid for small samples; **isotonic needs ≥1000 samples**.

**Active learning for queue prioritization** [V] ([wiki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Active_learning_(machine_learning))): **uncertainty sampling** (label where the model is least certain), **query by committee** (run two extractor prompts/models, prioritize disagreements — cheap and effective), and **diversity/density weighting** so the queue isn't full of near-duplicates.

I read `packages/knowledge/` and found four concrete items.

**E.1 — The erasure cascade does not follow `derivedFrom`.** [V-mine]

`erasure.ts:273` deletes facts with `personFactFilter = { "anchors.personId": personId, tenantId }`. Grepping the whole package, **`derivedFrom` appears nowhere in `erasure.ts` or `erasure.test.ts`.** There is no transitive sweep.

**E.2 — Consolidation narrows anchors, which makes E.1 exploitable.** [V-mine]

`consolidation.ts:134-143`, `anchorDraftField()` returns a **single** field (`{organizationId}` OR `{personId}` OR `{engagementId}`), and line ~283 sets `anchors: anchorDraftField(anchor)` on every merge draft. So parent facts' *other* anchors are dropped.

Concrete leak: consolidate under org "Acme". Fact A `{organizationId: Acme, personId: Anna}` and Fact B `{organizationId: Acme, personId: Petra}` merge into "Anna and Petra both pushed back on the Q3 timeline", anchored **only to Acme**, `derivedFrom: [A, B]`. Now `erasePerson(Anna)` deletes A but the merged fact survives — still naming Anna, with a dangling `derivedFrom`. **This is an Art. 17 gap.**

*Fixes:* (a) union parent anchors into the merge draft; (b) add a bounded fixpoint over `derivedFrom` in `erasePerson` (depth cap ~8, visited set); (c) run the existing name-token redactor over `facts.text`, not just sources and proposal drafts; (d) assert post-erasure referential integrity — no surviving `derivedFrom` points at a deleted `_id`.

**E.3 — `validUntil` is declared but never written.** [V-mine]

It appears only in `schemas/facts.ts` (definition + `currentlyValidFilter`). You have transaction-time supersession without valid-time. Adding it gives you Graphiti's bitemporal model and lets you answer "as of date X" queries — which is exactly what Zep's testing guide and GroupMemBench's knowledge-update category probe.

**E.4 — The consolidation prompt handles redundancy but not contradiction; and there's no judge log.** [V-mine]

`buildConsolidationPrompt` says *"propose only merges that reduce redundancy with ZERO information loss"* and *"Do not invent, embellish, or drop information."* Contradictory facts ("budget is 50k" vs "budget is 80k") are neither redundant nor mergeable under those rules, so the dream cycle skips them. Contradiction is handled only at extraction time (`extraction.ts:138`: *"If a fact updates or contradicts a currently valid fact, list that fact's id in `supersedes`"*), which means **a contradiction between two facts extracted from different sources at different times is never detected.** That's the inter-context conflict case — your most common one.

Also, per TOKI: your LLM is a judge on the write path, and `proposals` records `resolvedBy`/`resolvedAt` but **not the model, prompt, or verdict**. That admits **replay inconsistency**. Add a keyed judge log committed before the operator commits.

## F. Recommended plan

**Metrics to adopt (top-line first):**
1. **MGS = U · (1−A) · (1−F)** from GateMem — utility × (1 − access-control violation) × (1 − forgetting failure). Multiplicative, so you can't buy governance with uselessness or vice versa.
2. **Context Completeness** (COMPLETE/PARTIAL/INSUFFICIENT), Zep's primary — isolates memory from generation.
3. **Recall@5/10, NDCG@10** on fact IDs (RAGAS ID-based variants: deterministic and free).
4. **Faithfulness** (supported claims / total) = extraction precision; **Context Recall** vs a reference fact list = extraction recall.
5. **pass^3**, not pass@3, on the consolidation job.
6. **Latency p50/p95** and **median context tokens** on every accuracy row.
7. **Krippendorff's α ≥ 0.800** on double-reviewed samples; **ECE (15 bins) + MCE** on extractor confidence; audited precision of the auto-accept band.
8. **Judge TPR/TNR vs human labels** (not accuracy), target >90%, re-measured on every judge change.

**Eval suites to build (~40–60 cases each, from real failures):**
- **Extraction** — source → hand-written reference fact list
- **Write** — Letta's design: ingest, **delete the source**, then ask
- **Read** — Recall@k / NDCG@k on fact IDs
- **Update** — seed a fact, contradict it later, ask "what's true now?" and "what was true as of X?"
- **Erasure** — port the ForgetEval adversarial categories, especially `shared_attribute` (does erasing Anna preserve Petra?), `compound_fact` (a fact naming two people), `identifier_obfuscation` and `cross_lingual_identifier` (check `Özdemir`/`Oezdemir`/`Ozdemir`, and email-vs-display-name mismatch)
- **Multi-tenant isolation** — GateMem-style: can tenant A's query surface tenant B's facts?

**Architecture changes worth making:**
- **Index by `K = V + fact`** — keep verbatim source chunks as retrieval values, use extracted facts as additional index keys. This is the LongMemEval finding (+9.4% recall, +5.4% accuracy) and it resolves the verbatim-vs-extracted tension.
- **Add a contradiction pass to the dream cycle** — NLI cross-encoder over same-anchor same-category valid facts, escalating only `contradiction` pairs to the LLM adjudicator.
- **Give the consolidator a `get_source` tool** (Auto-Dreamer) so it can check the transcript before merging.
- **Add valid-time writes** (`validFrom`/`validUntil`) alongside `supersededBy`.
- **Add a keyed judge log** (model, version, prompt hash, verdict) committed before merge commit.
- **Fix the erasure cascade** (E.1/E.2).
- **Run the dumb baselines** — grep-over-sources and BM25-over-facts — as permanent control arms. On GroupMemBench, BM25 beat every agent memory system but one.

**Two calibration warnings:** generated benchmarks run optimistic in absolute terms but preserve ordering (use for relative decisions); and at your likely scale (<150 conversations per anchor), ConvoMem says full-context may simply beat you — measure before you optimize.

### 1.1 The headline: MongoDB shipped three new retrieval primitives in 2026

This is the biggest change since your cutoff, and it directly changes how you should build retrieval for `@repo/knowledge`.

| Stage | Min version | Status | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$rankFusion` | **MongoDB 8.0+** | **GA 2026-06-30** | Native RRF over N sub-pipelines |
| `$scoreFusion` | **MongoDB 8.3+** | **GA 2026-06-30** | Score-based fusion w/ normalization + custom expression |

[VERIFIED: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/rankFusion/ · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/scoreFusion/ · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/score/ · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/rerank/ · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/search-changelog/ · https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/product-release-announcements/boost-search-relevance-mongodb-atlas-native-hybrid-search]

#### `$rankFusion` — exact syntax [VERIFIED]

```javascript
{
  $rankFusion: {
    input: {
      pipelines: {
        <name1>: [ ...stages ],
        <name2>: [ ...stages ]
      }
    },
    combination: { weights: { <name1>: <number>, <name2>: <number> } },  // default 1 each
    scoreDetails: <bool>   // default false
  }
}
```

- **RRF formula, verbatim:** `RRFscore(d) = Σ(r∈R) w(r) / (60 + r(d))` — the rank constant is **hardcoded 60**, not configurable.
- Result score lands in the **`score`** metadata field. `scoreDetails` populates a nested per-pipeline breakdown (`inputPipelineName`, `rank`, `weight`, `value`) — retrieve with `{$meta: "scoreDetails"}`.
- **Input pipeline restrictions:** each must be a *Selection* AND *Ranked* pipeline. Allowed stages only: `$match`, `$search`, `$vectorSearch`, `$sample`, `$geoNear`, `$sort`, `$skip`, `$limit`. Must either begin with `$search`/`$vectorSearch`/`$geoNear` or contain an explicit `$sort`.
- Pipeline names: non-empty, no leading `$`, no `.`, no `\0`.
- De-duplicates: a doc appears at most once regardless of how many pipelines return it.
- Single collection only; no database scope.
- ⚠️ On 8.0.X you must **open a support case** to enable it. Fine from 8.1+.

**Real working example from MongoDB's own hybrid tutorial** [VERIFIED: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/vector-search-with-full-text-search.md]:

```javascript
[
  { "$rankFusion": {
      "input": { "pipelines": {
          "vectorPipeline": [{ "$vectorSearch": {
              "index": "hybrid-vector-search",
              "path": "plot_embedding_voyage_4_large",
              "queryVector": [...],
              "numCandidates": 500,
              "limit": 50 }}],
          "fullTextPipeline": [
              { "$search": { "index": "hybrid-full-text-search",
                  "text": { "query": "charming animal", "path": "fullplot", "fuzzy": {} }}},
              { "$limit": 50 }
          ]
      }},
      "combination": { "weights": { "vectorPipeline": 0.5, "fullTextPipeline": 0.5 }},
      "scoreDetails": true
  }},
  { "$project": { "_id":1, "title":1, "fullplot":1, "scoreDetails": {"$meta":"scoreDetails"} }},
  { "$limit": 10 }
]
```

#### `$scoreFusion` + `$score` — the recency/importance lever you want [VERIFIED]

```javascript
{
  $scoreFusion: {
    input: {
      pipelines: { <name>: [...] },
      normalization: "none" | "sigmoid" | "minMaxScaler"
    },
    combination: {
      weights: { <name>: <number> },
      method: "avg" | "expression",       // default "avg"
      expression: { $sum: [ {$multiply: ["$$pipeA", 10]}, "$$pipeB" ] }
    },
    scoreDetails: <bool>
  }
}
```

- `sigmoid` = `1/(1+e^-x)`; `minMaxScaler` = `(s - min_s)/(max_s - min_s)`.
- **Key insight for a knowledge brain:** input pipelines that don't natively produce a score can supply one via the new **`$score` stage** — `{$score: {score: <expression>, normalization: "sigmoid", weight: <n>}}`. This is how you fold **recency decay** or **importance/confidence** into hybrid ranking *inside the database*, alongside vector and text, rather than re-sorting in Node. That's the single most directly applicable new capability for your `facts`/`sources` collections.
- Docs note: **8.3+** (the GA blog post says 8.2+ — trust the manual).

#### `$rerank` — native Voyage cross-encoder [VERIFIED]

```json
{ "$rerank": {
    "query": { "text": "<query-text>" },
    "path": "<field>" | ["<f1>","<f2>"],
    "numDocsToRerank": <int, max 1000>,
    "model": "rerank-2.5" | "rerank-2.5-lite" | "rerank-2" | "rerank-2-lite"
}}
```

- Score via `{$addFields: {rerankScore: {$meta: "score"}}}`. **`$rerank` overwrites `$meta:"score"`** — project the prior `$rankFusion` score into a named field *before* `$rerank` if you need both.
- **Errors if any `path` field is missing on any input doc.** Mitigate with a prior `$set` to `""` or `$match` with `$exists`.
- **Hard limitations:** cannot be used on self-managed or **Atlas Local** deployments; cannot appear inside `$rankFusion`/`$scoreFusion` input pipelines; not on Views. Must be enabled per-project by a Project Owner (org-level Cedar `forbid` policy available to block it).
- Runs off-cluster on MongoDB's infra — does not consume your cluster CPU, but adds real latency. Docs: "best suited for workloads where retrieval quality is prioritized over ultra-low latency, such as RAG and agentic AI."
- **Pricing:** `rerank-2.5` $0.05/1M tokens, `rerank-2.5-lite` $0.02/1M. **200M free tokens one-time per org.** Billing formula: `(query_tokens × numDocsToRerank) + sum(document_tokens)`. Rate limits 4,000 RPM / 4M TPM (`2.5`) or 8M TPM (`2.5-lite`). [VERIFIED: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/native-reranking/billing.md · .../managing.md]

**The canonical full-stack memory retrieval pipeline is now: `$rankFusion`(vector + text [+ `$score` recency]) → `$rerank` → `$limit`.** MongoDB documents exactly this composition.

### 1.2 Automated Embedding — you may not need to embed in app code anymore

Public Preview announced **2026-05-11** ("AI Search for Agents: Announcing Automated Embedding in MongoDB Atlas"). [VERIFIED: https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/channel/artificial-intelligence]

**Index definition** — new `autoEmbed` field type [VERIFIED: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/index/vector-search-type.md]:
```json
{ "fields": [
    { "type": "autoEmbed", "modality": "text", "path": "<field>",
      "model": "voyage-4-large | voyage-4 | voyage-4-lite | voyage-code-3",
      "numDimensions": 256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048,
      "quantization": "float | scalar | binary | binaryNoRescore",
      "similarity": "dotProduct | cosine | euclidean",
      "indexingMethod": "flat | hnsw",
      "hnswOptions": { "maxEdges": <n>, "numEdgeCandidates": <n> } },
    { "type": "filter", "path": "<field>" }
]}
```

**Query** — pass text, not vectors:
```json
{ "$vectorSearch": { "index": "<name>", "path": "<field>",
    "query": "<query-text>", "model": "<embedding-model>" }}
```

Mechanics [VERIFIED: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/crud-embeddings/automated-embedding/overview.md]:
- Initial sync scans the collection, embeds via Voyage, stores vectors in a **separate internal system collection** (`__mdb_internal_search`, naming format `<index_id>-<hash>-<mv_version>-<def_version>` since 2026-06-30) — **your documents stay clean, no `embedding: number[]` field bloating them**. This is a genuinely nice property for a document-model knowledge brain.
- Ongoing sync via **change streams** on insert/update/delete. Updates to non-indexed fields do not trigger re-embedding.
- Self-managed Community/Enterprise supported by supplying a Voyage API key; Atlas uses MongoDB-hosted multi-tenant inference (GCP, US region).
- **Pricing / 1M tokens:** `voyage-4-lite` $0.02 · `voyage-4` $0.06 (recommended) · `voyage-4-large` $0.12 · `voyage-code-3` $0.18. **200M free tokens per org, one-time, non-refreshing.** Index rate limits 2,000 RPM; TPM 3M/8M/16M/3M respectively. [VERIFIED: .../automated-embedding/models.md]

**Trade-off for you:** you lose control of chunking and input_type asymmetry, and you pay per query. For a knowledge brain where facts are short and writes are bursty, it removes a whole embedding pipeline. For high-QPS retrieval it may be cheaper to keep embedding yourself.

### 1.4 Is there an official `mongodb-agent-memory` package? — **No, but there's something better for you**

**Nothing named `mongodb-agent-memory` exists on npm or PyPI** [VERIFIED]. Instead MongoDB DevRel shipped a family of framework-specific memory integrations in Q2 2026:

#### ⭐ `@mongodb-developer/vercel-ai-memory` — the most directly relevant artifact in this entire survey

- npm **v0.4.2, published 2026-06-25**; repo https://github.com/mongodb-developer/vercel-ai-memory (⭐2, pushed 2026-06-25, Apache-2.0); author **Pavel Duchovny** (MongoDB DevRel). Peers: `ai ^6||^7`, `mongodb ^6||^7`, `zod ^3.25||^4`. Tracks AI SDK v7 and driver v7 actively.
- **It is listed as a first-class memory provider in the official Vercel AI SDK v7 docs** alongside Letta, Mem0, Supermemory, and Hindsight — so despite 2 GitHub stars, it's the canonical MongoDB path. [VERIFIED: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/agents/memory]

**Five memory tiers, each a collection** [VERIFIED from `src/types.ts`]:

| Type | Collection | Vector index | Default retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| session | `session_memory` | — | TTL 86,400s on `created_at` |
| semantic | `semantic_memory` | `semantic_vector_index` | none |
| procedural | `procedural_memory` | `procedural_vector_index` | none |
| episodic | `episodic_memory` | `episodic_vector_index` | TTL 31,536,000s on **`stats.last_retrieved`** |
| scratchpad | `scratchpad_memory` | — | TTL 3,600s on `created_at` |

The `SemanticMemory` document shape, verbatim:
```ts
interface SemanticMemory {
  _id: ObjectId
  user_id: string
  name: string                    // entity name
  category: 'semantic'
  description: string
  embedding: number[]
  importance: number              // LLM-assigned 1–10
  stats: { retrieval_ct: number; avg_importance: number; last_retrieved: Date }
  timestamp: Date
  is_latest: boolean              // ← temporal versioning
  tags?: string[]
  expire_at?: Date | null         // ← TTL index expireAfterSeconds: 0
}
```

Mechanisms worth stealing:
- **Temporal versioning via `is_latest`**: `semanticSave` does `updateMany({user_id, name}, {$set:{is_latest:false}})` then `insertOne({..., is_latest:true})` when `keepHistory`, else an in-place upsert. Retrieval pre-filters `is_latest: {$eq: true}` **inside `$vectorSearch.filter`**.
- **Four retention modes:** `none` | `ttl` | **`ttl+importance`** (TTL only applies below `minImportance` — important memories immune) | **`dynamic`** (`computeExpireAt({importance, stats, createdAt})` per doc, backed by an `expire_at` TTL index with `expireAfterSeconds: 0`, recomputed on read when `refreshOnRead: true`). That last one is a **real forgetting curve**, e.g. `2^importance` hours, or `24 * 1.5^importance + retrieval_ct * 12`.
- **`memory_forget` tool**: sets `expire_at = now`; TTL monitor reaps within ~60s. A clean agent-driven GDPR-adjacent delete.
- **Retrieval-time filters:** `minImportance`, `recencyWindowHours` (applied as `$match` on `stats.last_retrieved` after `$vectorSearch`), `numCandidatesMultiplier` (default 10 → `numCandidates = limit * 10`).
- **Read-side write-back:** every search `$inc`s `stats.retrieval_ct` and `$set`s `stats.last_retrieved` (bulk-written), which is what feeds decay.
- **Hook-driven vs tool-driven session persistence.** The README is refreshingly honest that tool-driven is "**not deterministic**: the model sometimes skips writes." Production mode uses `prepareCall` + `onFinish` hooks with `topology.hideToolCommands: ['session']` so the runtime persists every turn exactly once. **This is the right lesson: don't let the LLM decide whether to persist the transcript.**
- Multi-tenant via `topology.extraFilterFields: { semantic: ['tenant_id'] }` → registered as `{type:'filter'}` paths in the vector index.

⚠️ **Gap:** it uses **plain `$vectorSearch` only** — no `$rankFusion`, no `$search`, no `$rerank`. Given your Atlas Search setup in `packages/knowledge/search.ts`, you're already ahead of it on retrieval.

https://github.com/RichmondAlake/memorizz · **⭐757**, pushed **2026-07-19**, PyPI v0.4.0 (2026-07-19). - Memory types: episodic, semantic, procedural, short-term, shared; providers: **MongoDB, Oracle, filesystem**.

Short-term: **working memory**, **semantic cache**, **shared memory**. Long-term: **episodic** (conversational, summarization), **semantic** (knowledge base, entity, persona, associative), **procedural** (toolbox, workflow). Application modes: assistant / workflow / deep research. Named integrations: LangGraph, **Agno**, **Mastra**, LangChain.

## PART 2 — Mastra (the other Priority 1)

**Status: very healthy, and its memory model changed fundamentally since your cutoff.** ⭐26,828, pushed 2026-08-02, Apache-2.0 (© Kepler Software). `@mastra/core` **1.55.0** (2026-07-30), `@mastra/memory` **1.24.0** (2026-07-28). 1.0 shipped 2026-01-20. **$22M Series A led by Spark Capital, 2026-04-09** ($35M total; Gradient, basecase, YC W25). Weekly npm downloads: core 1.36M, memory 851K. [VERIFIED: GitHub API, npm registry, https://mastra.ai/blog/series-a]

### 2.1 The big shift: Observational Memory replaced the old model

Since `@mastra/memory@1.1.0` (Feb 2026), the flagship is **Observational Memory (OM)**, and the docs now say verbatim: *"In practical terms, OM replaces both working memory and message history, and has greater accuracy (and lower cost) than Semantic Recall."* [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/observational-memory.md]

**Mechanism:** two background agents — an **Observer** and a **Reflector** — maintain a dense, **append-only** observation log that substitutes for raw history.
- Observer fires when unobserved messages cross **30,000 tokens**; Reflector fires when the observation log crosses **40,000 tokens**.
- **Reflection rewrites the *entire* log**, so memory stays bounded forever rather than accumulating a third layer.
- Buffering ratios: `bufferTokens: 0.2` (background pass every 20% of threshold), `bufferActivation: 0.8` (drop ~80% of history on activation), `blockAfter: 1.2` (hard sync ceiling at 36k / 48k).
- Observation format: two-level Markdown bullets with **emoji priority + timestamps** (`- 🔴 12:10 User is building a Next.js app…`).
- **Three-date temporal model:** *observation date*, *referenced date* ("my flight is January 31"), *relative date* ("2 days from today"). This is the only real temporal model in Mastra.
- **The architectural bet: an append-only, prompt-cacheable prefix beats per-turn retrieval.** That's the opposite of RAG-style memory and worth serious consideration for your design.
- Storage support for OM: `@mastra/pg`, `@mastra/libsql`, `@mastra/mysql`, **`@mastra/mongodb`**, `@mastra/convex`.
- **Extractors** (1.22.0+) piggyback typed Zod extraction on the Observer's already-primed context — cheap structured extraction as a side effect of observation.

### 2.2 Working memory — exact mechanism

- Markdown **template** (REPLACE semantics — agent emits the whole blob) **XOR** Zod/Standard-Schema **`schema`** (**MERGE semantics** — deep-merge, `null` deletes, **arrays replaced wholesale**). Mutually exclusive at the type level.
- Tool name is **`updateWorkingMemory`** (or `setWorkingMemory` when `useStateSignals: true`).
- Config: `{ enabled, template | schema, scope: 'thread'|'resource' (default **'resource'**), useStateSignals: false, agentManaged: true }`.
- Injected into the **system message** wrapped in `<working_memory_template>` / `<working_memory_data>` tags; tag parsing is `indexOf`-based specifically to avoid ReDoS.
- Experimental `version: 'vnext'` swaps full-rewrite for a **search-and-replace edit** tool taking `{newMemory, searchString, updateReason: 'append-new-memory'|'clarify-existing-memory'|'replace-irrelevant-memory'}`.
- `useStateSignals` moves WM out of the system prompt into a state signal — motivated purely by **prompt-cache invalidation**.
- Resource-scoped WM requires **libSQL, Postgres, Upstash, or MongoDB**.

### 2.3 Semantic recall — exact mechanism and defaults

```ts
semanticRecall: {
  topK: 4,                                    // default
  messageRange: { before: 1, after: 1 },      // default
  scope: 'resource',                          // default
  filter?: VectorFilter,                      // MongoDB-style $and/$or/$eq/$in/...
  indexConfig?: VectorIndexConfig
}
```
- **`messageRange` is a hydration window, not a vector setting.** After top-K, each hit's `metadata.message_id` + `thread_id` is turned into a relational re-fetch with `withPreviousMessages`/`withNextMessages`. That's a clean pattern: vector index finds anchors, relational store supplies contiguous context.
- Scope is implemented as **nothing more than a metadata filter**: `{resource_id}` vs `{thread_id}`. Embedding metadata written on save is `{message_id, thread_id, resource_id}`. Resource-scoped recall **throws** without a `resourceId` — "a missing ID never expands the search."
- Index naming: **`memory_messages`** at 1536 dims, `memory_messages_<dim>` otherwise; requests `metadataIndexes: ['thread_id','resource_id']`.
- **Disabled by default** (`semanticRecall: false`); `lastMessages` default **10**.

### 2.4 Memory processors — the pattern worth copying

Memory is now *implemented as* processors in the agent pipeline: `MessageHistory`, `SemanticRecall`, `WorkingMemory` (all `@mastra/core/processors`). Execution order:

```
Input:  [Memory Processors] → [Your inputProcessors]
Output: [Your outputProcessors] → [Memory Processors]
```

**Rationale: an output guardrail that calls `abort()` runs *before* persistence, so nothing gets written to memory.** That's a genuinely good design constraint for a system with GDPR/PII concerns. If you place one manually, Mastra won't auto-add its own.
- `TokenLimiter` and `ToolCallFilter` are **generic** processors, not memory processors: `TokenLimiterProcessor {limit, strategy:'truncate'|'abort', countMode:'cumulative'|'part', trimMode:'best-fit'|'contiguous'}`; `ToolCallFilter {exclude, filterAfterToolSteps, preserveModelOutput}`.

### 2.5 MongoDB support — yes, and `MongoDBVector` is the most transferable code in the repo

**`@mastra/mongodb` v1.15.1 (2026-07-30)** ships **both** `MongoDBStore` (storage domains) and `MongoDBVector` (Atlas Vector Search). Requires Atlas cloud or **Atlas Local via Docker**; MongoDB 7.0+ recommended. [VERIFIED: https://mastra.ai/reference/storage/mongodb.md · .../vectors/mongodb.md · GitHub `stores/mongodb/src/{storage,vector}`]

Collections: `mastra_threads`, `mastra_messages`, `mastra_resources`, `mastra_observational_memory`, plus workflow/trace/scorer tables. Default indexes include `{resourceId:1, createdAt:-1}`, `{thread_id:1, createdAt:1}`, unique `{id:1}`.

`MongoDBVector` capabilities that are directly worth stealing:
- **`filterFields`** declares metadata fields as vector-index filter paths (`metadata.<field>`) so filters get **pushed into `$vectorSearch`** instead of pre-filtering candidate `_id`s — explicitly to dodge **the 16 MB BSON limit on large result sets**. Undeclared fields silently fall back to slow pre-filtering.
- **BYO-collection mode**: index an existing operational collection; **read-only by default**, writes require explicit `allowWrites: true`, and the policy is **persisted durably** and "fails closed." `deleteIndex()` on a BYO index drops Atlas indexes but preserves documents.
- **`metadataMode: 'document'`** returns the whole source document as metadata and matches filters against the **root** (no `metadata.` prefix) — for operational collections.
- **`hybridQuery({queryVector, query, paths, weights: {vector, text}})`** uses **server-side `$rankFusion`**; docs state MongoDB ≥8.0, GA from 8.1.
- `numCandidates` defaults to `20 × topK`, capped 10,000; native `ObjectId` `_id`s supported.
- **Retention:** `@mastra/mongodb` has a real `retention.ts` with age-based `prune()` (batched, resumable, cancellable, lazy anchor-index creation), but Mastra **never runs it for you** — and the OM collection has no timestamp anchor so **cannot be age-pruned**. Docs recommend **native MongoDB TTL indexes** instead, via `indexes: [{collection:'mastra_messages', keys:{createdAt:1}, options:{expireAfterSeconds: 30*86400}}]`.

**LongMemEval-S: OM + gpt-5-mini = 94.87%**, claimed "highest score ever recorded on this benchmark, by any system, with any model." Oracle gpt-4o baseline 82.40%; full-context gpt-4o 60.20%; average context ~30k tokens; 3–6× text compression. [VERIFIED as a claim: https://mastra.ai/research/observational-memory, 2026-02-09] Self-published, self-run, mixed actor models across the leaderboard rows — treat accordingly.

### 3.1 Supermemory — healthy, but **the OSS repo is a shell**

⭐**28,741**, MIT, pushed 2026-08-02, TypeScript. **$3M pre-seed, 2025-10-06, Susa Ventures** (no later round found; searches unavailable). [VERIFIED: GitHub API, https://supermemory.ai/blog/supermemory-raises-3-million]

[VERIFIED: `gh api .../contents`, `.../releases/tags/server-v0.0.6`]

- **Memory unit:** three artifact classes — document chunks, extracted memories, profile. Memory fields: `memory`, `isStatic`, `metadata`, `isLatest`, `isForgotten`, `forgetReason`, **`forgetAfter`** (ISO TTL), **`temporalContext: {documentDate, eventDate[]}`**, `containerTag` (required tenant key).
- **Write:** async 6-stage pipeline. **"Dynamic Dreaming"** (2026-05-25) uses adaptive scheduling triggered on user quiet — worst case **~15 min** lag. "Instant" mode costs extra ops.
- **Update:** **version chain** (`PATCH` → new version, old gets `isLatest=false`) + typed graph edges **`updates` / `extends` / `derives`**. ⚠️ Ordering-sensitive: "ingest sequentially within a containerTag… that's how supermemory determines what came first."

- **Forgetting — best of the five:** per-memory `forgetAfter`, soft delete (`isForgotten`/`forgetReason`, recoverable), and **semantic bulk forget** ("forget everything about a topic") with `threshold`, `maxForget` 1–500, and a **`dryRun` preview**.

Published: **LongMemEval 95% Recall@15, ~720 mean tokens, 99.4% context reduction**. ⚠️ **No LoCoMo or ConvoMem numbers published, and no competitor numbers anywhere.** Their own `memorybench` harness (⭐303) ships a `compare -p supermemory,mem0,zep` command with **zero populated result tables**. ### 3.2 Honcho — healthy, uniquely *perspectival*, AGPL

⭐**6,382**, **AGPL-3.0**, Python, pushed 2026-07-31, 91 commits since May, latest tag **v3.0.12**. Honcho 3 shipped 2026-01-26. Funding not verifiable. [VERIFIED: GitHub API, https://plasticlabs.ai/blog/posts/Honcho-3]

- **Model:** `Workspace → Peers + Sessions → Messages`. **Peers, not users** (agents are peers too; peers↔sessions many-to-many).
- **Memory unit = "conclusion":**
  ```
  id, content, observer_id, observed_id, session_id,
  level: "explicit" | "deductive" | "inductive" | "contradiction", created_at
  ```
  **The `(observer_id, observed_id)` pair is the differentiator — memory is perspectival.** Alice's model of Bob is a distinct object from the system's global model of Bob. Nobody else in this survey has this. Directly relevant if your knowledge brain ever needs "what does person X believe about person Y."
- `observe_me` (global rep from all messages) vs `observe_others` (local, only from messages that peer actually saw).
- **Write path:** message + task enqueued synchronously; reasoning async. **Token-batched:** the deriver accumulates until ~**1,000 tokens** pending per representation, then processes in one call. **Recent memories are not immediately queryable.** Extraction uses their fine-tuned **Neuromancer** models, not frontier LLMs.
- **Consolidation — "the Dreamer":** two sequential agents. *Deduction* handles knowledge updates/contradictions and **hard-deletes the outdated conclusion, creating a new one** (no tombstone). *Induction* finds patterns requiring **≥2 source conclusions**. Trigger requires **all three**: ≥50 new conclusions, ≥8 hours since last dream, enabled — plus a **60-min idle timeout**; new messages cancel and reset.
- **Retrieval — two paths:** `context()` (~200ms, **free and unlimited**, packs summaries + recent messages + representation + peer card into a token budget, `.to_openai()`/`.to_anthropic()`); and `chat()` — **the Dialectic** — which spawns an agent that searches conclusions, **traces a conclusion back to the premises it was drawn from**, and synthesizes. Five reasoning levels `minimal→max`, each with its own model and tools. Search is hybrid BM25 + vector, limit 10/max 100; ⚠️ keyword hits are available immediately, semantic hits lag embedding by seconds; **fusion method undocumented**.
- Summaries: short every 20 messages, long every 60.
- **Forgetting:** none — no TTL, no decay. Only Dreamer consolidation + explicit deletes.
- **Temporal: weakest here.** `created_at` only. Docs list "multi-hop and temporal reasoning" as **future work**.
- **Benchmarks:** LoCoMo **89.9%**, LongMemEval-S **90.4%**, BEAM-100K **0.630** (0.646 @500K → 0.409 @10M), 60–90% token savings. Neuromancer XR (Qwen3-8B fine-tuned on ~10,000 curated conclusion-derivations): LoCoMo **86.9%** vs Claude 4 Sonnet 80.0% vs base Qwen3-8B 69.6%. ⚠️ `honcho.dev/evals` is JS-rendered and returned empty; the repro repo `plastic-labs/honcho-benchmarks` was last pushed **2025-12-19** and is a stub.
- **Storage: PostgreSQL only, no MongoDB** (docs say so explicitly; 0 code hits). Vector pluggable: `pgvector|turbopuffer|lancedb`. `EMBEDDING_VECTOR_DIMENSIONS=1536` is **immutable for the life of a deployment**.
- **TS SDK: excellent** — `@honcho-ai/sdk` **v2.2.0 (2026-07-02)**, released in lockstep with Python.
- **Pricing:** ingest **$2.00/M tokens**; `context()` **free/unlimited**; per-query reasoning $0.001 (minimal) → **$0.50 (max)**. Startups <$5M raised get $1,000 credits.

### 3.5 Redis Agent Memory Server — **repositioned, not abandoned**

⭐**301** (far smaller than the others), Apache-2.0, Python.

**The structural change:** on **2026-07-09** commit *"Relocate project into `V0/` and add Redis Agent Memory landing layer (#319)"* moved the whole OSS server into a `V0/` subdirectory. The new root README says in Redis's own words that V0 *"serves as the research foundation and architectural starting point"* but **"it is not the current supported production path"** — supported teams use **Redis Cloud**, not the OSS version. [VERIFIED: GitHub API + raw README]

**Redis is pushing hard, but commercially.** **Redis Iris** is a four-service managed context engine: RDI (CDC from Oracle/MySQL/Postgres/etc.), Context Retriever, **Redis Agent Memory** (GA on Redis Cloud, private preview on Redis Software w/ license key), and LangCache. The managed API surface is **not drop-in compatible** with OSS: `/v1/stores/{storeId}/long-term-memory` with camelCase (`memoryType`, `ownerId`) vs OSS `/v1/long-term-memory` with snake_case (`memory_type`, `user_id`). [VERIFIED: https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/ai/context-engine/agent-memory/]

OSS momentum has stopped: last release **server/v0.15.2, 2026-04-10** (~4 months); 32 commits since May of which **10 of the last 15 are Dependabot**; npm `agent-memory-client` **0.3.1, 2026-01-31** (~6 months stale).

**But the design is the best-specified forgetting model in the entire survey, and it's Apache-2.0 so you can lift it freely:**

- **`MemoryRecord`:** `text, id, memory_type, topics[], entities[], user_id, namespace, event_date, session_id`. Types `semantic` | `episodic` | `message` (+ `preference`, `summary`). **`event_date` is distinct from creation time — a genuine event-time vs system-time separation.**
- **Four named extraction strategies:** `discrete` (default, individual facts), `summary` (`max_summary_length` 500), `preferences`, `custom` (domain prompt; docs warn about prompt injection).
- **Retrieval:** `semantic` (default, `distance_threshold: 0.8`) | `keyword` (BM25) | **`hybrid` (`hybrid_alpha` default 0.7)**.
- **⭐ Recency boost — a real published ranking formula:**
  ```python
  final_score   = semantic_weight * semantic_similarity + recency_weight * recency_score
  recency_score = freshness_weight * freshness_score + novelty_weight * novelty_score
  freshness     = exp(-ln(2) * days_since_creation    / freshness_half_life)
  novelty       = exp(-ln(2) * days_since_last_access / novelty_half_life)
  ```
  Defaults: semantic **0.8** / recency **0.2**; freshness **0.6** / novelty **0.4**; half-lives **30 days** (created) and **7 days** (last access). **Nobody else publishes numbers this precise.** This maps directly onto a `$score` stage inside `$scoreFusion` on your stack.
- **Forgetting lifecycle:** working memory **TTL 1 hour** default; long-term forgetting **off by default** (`FORGETTING_MAX_AGE_DAYS` 90, `FORGETTING_MAX_INACTIVE_DAYS` 30, `FORGETTING_BUDGET_KEEP_TOP_N`); four strategies — age, inactivity, combined, **budget-based keep-top-N by access**. Compaction every 10 min. ⚠️ *"Without a running task worker, automatic forgetting will not occur regardless of configuration settings."*
- **Benchmarks: none. Zero published numbers** anywhere. Redis markets on latency/infra credibility.
- **Storage: Redis only. No MongoDB.** `BACKEND_TYPE=[redis|custom]`; custom requires subclassing `MemoryVectorDatabase` and no other production-ready backend is documented.
- Native **MCP server** alongside REST (port 8000) is a real differentiator.

**(c) NEW 2026 — Managed Agents *memory stores* (server-side) + *Dreams* (consolidation).** These are the most directly analogous prior art to what you're building. [VERIFIED: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory · .../dreams]
- Memory store (`memstore_…`) = workspace-scoped collection of **path-addressed text documents**, **mounted as a real directory** in the session sandbox at `/mnt/memory/<slug>/`; attached at session creation only, max 8 per session, `access: read_write|read_only` enforced at the filesystem level. Lifecycle `pending→running→completed/failed/canceled`, runtime "minutes to a few hours." Nuance: `instructions` steers *synthesis*, not editing — "imperative directives that target specific lines generally produce no change."
- ⚠️ **Security warning worth quoting:** stores default to `read_write`, and "a successful prompt injection could write malicious content into the store. Later sessions then read that content as trusted memory."

Latest `crewai` **1.15.10, 2026-07-31**. No MongoDB, Python-only. [VERIFIED: https://docs.crewai.com/en/concepts/memory · https://pypi.org/project/crewai/] Note MongoDB DevRel independently built `crewai-mongodb-memory` implementing the `StorageBackend` protocol.

[VERIFIED: https://docs.ag2.ai/docs/user-guide/advanced/knowledge_store/ · https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/overview/agent-framework-overview · .../agents/conversations/session]

[VERIFIED: https://eve.dev/docs/patterns/multi-tenant-memory · https://eve.dev/docs/guides/state]

[VERIFIED: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/sessions/ · .../store-and-sync-state/]

https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight — **⭐19,023** (independently re-verified by me), created 2025-10-30, pushed 2026-07-31, Python, **MIT**, ~weekly releases (v0.8.6 2026-07-29). Product site hindsight.vectorize.io. **Also a first-class provider in the Vercel AI SDK docs.**

- **Four "biomimetic" networks:** *World* (facts), *Experiences* (own episodes), *Opinion* (beliefs with confidence scores), *Observation* (mental models derived by reflecting over facts + experiences). Each memory holds entities, relationships, and time series with sparse + dense vectors.
- **Five operations:** `retain`, `recall`, `reflect`, `getMentalModel`, `getDocument`, scoped by `bankId`.
- **Write:** `retain` runs LLM extraction (facts, temporal data, relationships) into normalized entities + indexes. `reflect` synthesizes mental models — the "learns, not just remembers" pitch.
- **Retrieval:** four parallel strategies — **semantic + BM25 keyword + graph (entity/temporal/causal) + temporal range** — merged by **RRF**, then **cross-encoder reranking**, then trimmed to a token budget. Exactly the stack MongoDB's new primitives give you natively.
- **Forgetting/decay: not documented.**
- **Storage: PostgreSQL primary, Oracle AI Database enterprise, embedded `pg0`. No MongoDB.**
- **TS client exists:** npm `hindsight-ai` **1.6.0**. Self-hostable via Docker.
- **Self-published leaderboard** (benchmarks.hindsight.vectorize.io): LongMemEval-S **94.6%**, LoCoMo-10 **92.0%**, PersonaMem-32K 86.6%, **BEAM-100K 75%, BEAM-1M 73.9%, BEAM-10M 64.1%**, LifeBench-EN 71.5%.

### 5.2 Memvid — v1 was a gimmick and **its own authors deprecated it**

https://github.com/memvid/memvid — ⭐**16,092**, Rust, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-07-14 (moved org from `Olow304/memvid`).

**The key finding: the text-in-video-frames trick no longer exists in the codebase.** The v2 README says verbatim **"Memvid v1 (QR-based memory) is deprecated"** and **"if you are referencing QR codes, you are using outdated information."** v2 is a single-file `.mv2` format: 4KB header, embedded WAL, compressed segments, **Lex (full-text) + HNSW (vector) indices**, chronological time index, TOC footer. "Smart Frames" is an **append-only log structure** *metaphorically* inspired by I-frame/delta framing — not video. Effectively "SQLite for agent memory." [VERIFIED: raw README]

- Claims: "+35% SOTA on LoCoMo", "0.025ms P50 / 0.075ms P99, 1,372× higher throughput" — self-reported, unaudited.
- Node SDK `@memvid/sdk` 2.0.160. **No MongoDB.**
- **Criticism of v1 was correct**: a critique piece (esoteriic.com) noted MP4 is *lossy* with no explanation of the effect on semantic precision. **GitHub issue #86 ("misleading compression claims") has been deleted — `gh api` returns HTTP 410 "This issue was deleted."** That's a notable signal about how criticism is handled. A 2026 evaluation flags a real limitation: **synchronous Rust, single-writer** vs. async multi-agent concurrent read/write workloads.

**Verdict: v1 = gimmick, disowned. v2 = a real embedded hybrid-search store.** Not relevant to your stack, but no longer vaporware.

### 5.6 New benchmarks — the field moved from recall to task outcome

This is the most important intellectual shift of 2026. **LOCOMO and LongMemEval are now widely considered saturated and mis-specified** — they test recall, not whether memory helps an agent *do the task*.

1. **BEAM** — ICLR 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.27246. **100 conversations, 2,000 validated questions, contexts up to 10M tokens, 10 memory dimensions** (abstention, contradiction resolution, event ordering, instruction-following over time). **Everyone's scores collapse on it** (Hindsight 73.9% @1M → 64.1% @10M). This is now the de-facto hard benchmark.
2. **STATE-Bench** — **Microsoft**, 2026-05-19, https://opensource.microsoft.com/blog/2026/05/19/introducing-state-bench-a-benchmark-for-ai-agent-memory/ · https://github.com/microsoft/STATE-Bench (⭐72, MIT — I re-verified). **Memory-agnostic: measures whether agents *improve with experience*** on 450 realistic enterprise tasks (support/travel/shopping). Metrics: **pass@1, pass^5 (succeeds all 5 runs), cost/task, LLM-judged UX**. Baseline: **GPT-5.1 with no memory completes fewer than half of tasks reliably; only ~30% of travel tasks pass^5.** Leaderboard currently **has no published system results** — it's an open challenge. **The most credible new benchmark and the one to watch.**
3. **MemoryArena** — https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16313 (Feb 2026; authors incl. Yejin Choi, Alex Pentland). Human-crafted **interdependent** multi-session tasks. **Headline finding: agents near-perfect on LoCoMo "perform poorly in our agentic setting."** Swapping memory-equipped for long-context-only drops task completion **80% → 45%**.
4. **LifeBench** — https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03781 (Mar 2026). Declarative **and** non-declarative (habitual/procedural) memory from diverse digital traces. **"Top-tier SOTA memory systems reach just 55.2% accuracy."**
5. **⭐ GateMem** — https://github.com/rzhub/GateMem (⭐192, Jun 2026, MIT). *"Benchmark and evaluation toolkit for **memory governance** in multi-principal settings"* — multiple principals write to a shared pool and query under different roles/scopes/relationships. **Evaluates utility, access control, and deletion enforcement.** **This is the first benchmark that scores whether deletion is actually enforced — directly relevant to your GDPR Art. 17 erasure cascade.** Very new, low activity, but worth tracking.

Also: **ConvoMem** (Salesforce AI Research, 75,336 QA pairs), **HaluMem** (first operation-level hallucination benchmark for memory systems — does the memory layer itself fabricate), **PersonaMem** (COLM 2025).

⚠️ **Do not build a cross-vendor LongMemEval table.** Published numbers for the *same* systems differ wildly across 2026 sources — Zep appears as **90.2** in one article and **63.8** in another; Mem0 as **94.4** and **49.0**. Different judges, retrievers, backbone LLMs, and R@k-vs-accuracy conflation. Any number must be stated with its backbone model and metric.

## PART 7 — Synthesis for Your Stack

**Five things that actually changed in this window:**

1. **Vector-only memory is over.** Every serious 2026 system is hybrid: dense + BM25 + RRF + cross-encoder rerank, usually plus a graph or temporal index. **MongoDB just made that entire stack a native aggregation pipeline** — you're one of the few people who can implement it without a second datastore.
2. **Filesystem/Markdown-as-memory beat database-as-memory in the OSS wave.** Anthropic's `/memories` and `/mnt/memory/`, AG2's `KnowledgeStore`, OpenViking's `viking://`, EverOS, memU, memsearch, basic-memory — human-readable, Git-diffable files as the source of truth, with the vector store demoted to a **rebuildable shadow index**. Worth considering for auditability even on a Mongo backbone.
3. **"Dream"/consolidation passes are now a named pattern at both major labs** within a month of each other. Your `09c49c6` "dream cycle" is aligned. Copy Anthropic's non-destructive variant: write consolidation output to a *new* store, review, then swap.
4. **Benchmarks moved from recall to task outcome.** STATE-Bench, MemoryArena, LifeBench, GateMem. MemoryArena's "LoCoMo-perfect agents fail in agentic settings" is the single most important result of 2026.
5. **Forgetting is still the least-solved primitive**, and prompt-injection-into-memory is now an explicitly documented threat (Anthropic, eve, Microsoft all warn about it in different ways).

**Concrete mechanisms worth stealing, ranked by fit:**

1. **Redis's recency-boost formula** (exp half-life on freshness + novelty, 0.8/0.2 and 0.6/0.4 weights, 30d/7d half-lives) implemented as a **`$score` pipeline inside `$scoreFusion`** alongside your `$vectorSearch` and `$search`. Apache-2.0, so lift it freely. This is the highest-leverage single change.
2. **`@mongodb-developer/vercel-ai-memory`'s retention model** — `ttl+importance` (important memories immune to TTL) and `dynamic` with a per-doc `computeExpireAt` backed by an `expire_at` TTL index at `expireAfterSeconds: 0`. Plus `memory_forget` = set `expire_at = now`. This is a complete, tested forgetting curve on MongoDB.
3. **Supermemory's soft-delete + semantic bulk-forget with `dryRun`** (`isForgotten`, `forgetReason`, `maxForget` 1–500) — a much better UX than hard deletes, and it composes with your erasure cascade.
4. **Anthropic's memory-version `redact` endpoint** — immutable version history plus a redaction primitive that preserves the audit trail. That's the published state of the art for GDPR-with-audit, and the closest analogue to `erasePerson`.
5. **Mastra's processor ordering** — memory processors run *before* your input processors and *after* your output processors, so an aborting guardrail prevents persistence entirely. Cheap to replicate, and it's the right safety property for a PII-bearing knowledge brain.
6. **MemMachine's `citations` table** (`profile_id → episode_id`) — you already have `sources ↔ facts`; note that it's the only one of the five that makes provenance a first-class queryable join, which validates your design.
7. **`is_latest` temporal versioning pre-filtered inside `$vectorSearch.filter`** — cheap supersession semantics that keep history without polluting retrieval.
8. **Hook-driven, not tool-driven, transcript persistence.** MongoDB's own package documents that LLM-controlled session writes are "not deterministic — the model sometimes skips writes." Persist from the runtime.
9. **`voyage-context-4`** for chunk embeddings if your facts carry document context — it removes the manual context-augmentation step entirely.
10. **`filterFields` pushed into `$vectorSearch`** (from Mastra's `MongoDBVector`) to avoid the 16 MB BSON limit on pre-filtered `_id` lists at scale.

**And the reassuring finding:** across ~25 verified OSS projects and 5 commercial systems, **essentially nobody has built MongoDB-native agent memory.** The only one is Papr (⭐73, AGPL, stale). ## 2. Deep dives — the five most transferable designs

### 2.1 Graphiti's bi-temporal model (the reference implementation)

Everything below is `[V-direct]` from `graphiti_core` at commit `7cf0cab`, v0.29.3, 2026-08-01.

**Four timestamps, two axes.** On `EntityEdge`:
- `created_at` — when the system learned it (transaction time start)
- `expired_at` — when the system learned it was no longer true (transaction time end)
- `valid_at` — when the fact became true in the world (event time start)
- `invalid_at` — when it stopped being true in the world (event time end)
- plus `reference_time` — the episode's timestamp that produced this edge, and `episodes: list[str]` — provenance to the raw episodes

**The write path, precisely.** For each extracted edge, Graphiti retrieves **two different candidate sets**:

1. **Duplicate candidates** = `EntityEdge.get_between_nodes(source_uuid, target_uuid)` — every existing edge between *the same directed node pair* — then ranked by hybrid search over the extracted fact text.
2. **Invalidation candidates** = unfiltered hybrid search over the whole graph (`EDGE_HYBRID_SEARCH_RRF`, limit 10) for the same fact text, minus anything already in set 1.

Both lists go into **one** LLM call with **continuous index numbering across both lists**, returning:

```python
class EdgeDuplicate(BaseModel):
    duplicate_facts: list[int]     # only from EXISTING FACTS range
    contradicted_facts: list[int]  # from either list
```

The prompt's decisive examples:
- `"Alice works at Acme as a software engineer"` vs `"...as a senior engineer"` → `duplicate_facts=[], contradicted_facts=[1]` — "same relationship but updated title — contradiction, NOT a duplicate"
- `"Bob ran 5 miles on Tuesday"` vs `"Bob ran 3 miles on Wednesday"` → both empty — "different events on different days"

**Then the temporal arithmetic** (`resolve_edge_contradictions`), which is the part people get wrong:

```python
# Skip if the windows don't actually overlap:
if (edge.invalid_at <= new.valid_at) or (new.invalid_at <= edge.valid_at):
    continue
# Only supersede if the old edge started EARLIER:
elif edge.valid_at < new.valid_at:
    edge.invalid_at = new.valid_at          # close event-time window
    edge.expired_at = edge.expired_at or utc_now()   # close transaction-time window
```

**And the inverse case, which is the genuinely clever bit.** Before checking contradictions, Graphiti checks whether the *new* edge should be born already-expired — for out-of-order/backfilled ingestion:

```python
if resolved_edge.expired_at is None:
    invalidation_candidates.sort(key=lambda c: (c.valid_at is None, ensure_utc(c.valid_at)))
    for candidate in invalidation_candidates:
        if candidate.valid_at > resolved_edge.valid_at:
            resolved_edge.invalid_at = candidate.valid_at
            resolved_edge.expired_at = now
            break   # "Expire new edge since we have information about more recent events"
```

Timestamps themselves come from a separate small-model call (`extract_edges.extract_timestamps`) given only `{fact, reference_time}` — cheap and isolated.

**What Zep hands the agent.** The context block renders facts as
`(2024-11-15 14:23:00 - present) [CONTACTED_SUPPORT_ABOUT] <Emily contacted support regarding API rate limits>`
and entities as `{ name: X, types: [...], summary: Y }`. Configurable via `%{edges limit=N types=[...]}`, `%{entities}`, `%{observations limit=N}` (capped 20), `%{thread_summaries}` (capped 20).

**Zep "observations"** are productized reflection: cross-entity, evidence-backed patterns detected from graph structure, auto-deduped and merged when new evidence aligns — distinct from single-edge facts and single-node summaries.

**Applied to your schema.** You have `supersededBy` (a pointer, transaction-time-ish) and `validUntil` (event-time end) — and my read of `packages/knowledge/` confirms **`validUntil` is declared in `schemas/facts.ts` and `currentlyValidFilter` but never written by any code path.** You are missing `validFrom` and a `supersededAt` timestamp. Adding those four fields is what lets you answer "what was true on date X" and "what did we believe on date X" as separate queries — which is exactly what LongMemEval's knowledge-update category and GroupMemBench probe.

### 2.2 Graphiti's entity resolution ladder (deterministic-first, LLM-last)

`[V-direct]` from `dedup_helpers.py` + `node_operations.py`. This runs **before** any LLM call and resolves the majority of cases for free:

1. **Exact normalized-name match** (`lower()`, collapse whitespace). Exactly 1 hit → resolve. **More than 1 hit → escalate to LLM** (ambiguity is a signal, not a tie-break).
2. **Entropy gate**, guarding the fuzzy path only: reject if `len < 6 AND tokens < 2`, or if Shannon character entropy `< 1.5`.
3. **MinHash + LSH**: 3-gram shingles over `[a-z0-9' ]`, 32 blake2b-seeded permutations, banded at size 4 (8 bands).
4. **Jaccard ≥ 0.90** on the shingle sets → resolve.
5. Otherwise → LLM dedup pass with the candidate list.

Bulk ingestion adds union-find with path compression (`_build_directed_uuid_map`) to collapse transitive duplicate chains, plus a Redis "recent dedup cache" override so edges resolved seconds ago but not yet visible in the search index still participate.

**Guardrail worth copying:** `apply_capped_attributes` caps LLM-emitted attribute strings at **250 chars** (`GRAPHITI_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_LENGTH`) and **drops** over-length values, falling back to the prior value — rather than truncating. Prevents slow schema drift.

### 2.3 Generative Agents' reflection — and the paper/code discrepancies

`[V-direct]` from `joonspk-research/generative_agents`. **Three things the paper says are not what the code does:**

| | Paper | Released code |
|---|---|---|
| Weights | "all αs are set to 1" | `gw = [0.5, 3, 2]` on top of `w=1` → **relevance×3, importance×2, recency×0.5** |
| Decay | 0.995 | `recency_decay = 0.99` |
| Recency basis | hours since last access | `decay ** i` where **i is the rank index** in the chronologically sorted candidate list |

If you implement from the paper you get materially different behavior from the demo everyone saw. Relevance dominates.

**Reflection, verified from `reflect.py`:**
- Trigger is a **countdown**: `importance_trigger_curr` starts at `importance_trigger_max = 150` and decrements by each new event's poignancy; fires at ≤ 0. Roughly 2–3×/day.
- `generate_focal_points(persona, n=3)` builds the prompt from the **last `importance_ele_n` records** (events since the last reflection), not a fixed 100.
- Each focal point runs `new_retrieve(..., n_count=30)`, then `generate_insights_and_evidence(persona, nodes, n=5)` → 5 insights, **each with the node IDs that were its evidence**.
- Insights re-enter the memory stream as thoughts with their own poignancy and embedding → recursive reflection trees.
- **`expiration = created + 30 days` on every thought.** A TTL on derived memories that almost nobody mentions.

**Poignancy prompt, verbatim:** *"On the scale of 1 to 10, where 1 is purely mundane (e.g., brushing teeth, making bed) and 10 is extremely poignant (e.g., a break up, college acceptance), rate the likely poignancy of the following piece of memory."*

Ablation (TrueSkill μ): full 29.89 → no reflection 26.88 → no reflection+planning 25.64 → no memory/planning/reflection 21.21. Human baseline 22.95.

### 2.4 A-MEM's linking and memory evolution

`[V-direct]` from `agiresearch/A-mem`. Note the repo's last commit is **2025-12-12** — this is research code, not a maintained system.

Note structure: `content, timestamp, keywords[], tags[], context, links[], evolution_history[], retrieval_count, last_accessed`.

`process_memory(note)`:
1. `find_related_memories(note.content, **k=5**)`
2. One LLM call with the evolution prompt returning:
```json
{"should_evolve": bool,
 "actions": ["strengthen", "update_neighbor"],
 "suggested_connections": ["neighbor_ids"],
 "tags_to_update": [...],
 "new_context_neighborhood": ["...per neighbor, in input order..."],
 "new_tags_neighborhood": [[...], [...]]}
```
The prompt hard-constrains array lengths to the neighbor count. `strengthen` links the new note; `update_neighbor` **rewrites the existing neighbours' `context` and `tags`** in place — backward-propagating revision.

Separately, `evo_cnt % evo_threshold == 0` (threshold **100**) triggers `consolidate_memories()`, which rebuilds the retriever index.

**Transfer:** the "when you write a new fact, let it revise the *description* of nearby facts" move is the cheapest form of consolidation available and doesn't require merging anything.

### 2.5 mem0's update-op classifier — and why they deleted it

`[V-agent]`, from source at both v0.1.118 and `main`. This is the design most people mean by "mem0," and **it no longer exists.**

The old two-phase design:
- Extraction: `FACT_RETRIEVAL_PROMPT` → `{"facts": [...]}`
- For **each** extracted fact independently: `vector_store.search(limit=5)` → union, dedupe by id
- **UUID→integer remap before the prompt** (source comment: `# Map UUIDs to integers (anti-hallucination)`), mapped back after
- One LLM call → `{"memory": [{"id", "text", "event": "ADD|UPDATE|DELETE|NONE", "old_memory"}]}`
- DELETE = "the retrieved facts contain information that **contradicts**" existing

PR #4805 (2026-04-14) replaced all of it with a single-call, **ADD-only** pipeline. `grep -ic graph mem0/memory/main.py` on `main` returns **0**. The migration guide states plainly: *"Graph store support has been removed entirely"*, `add()` *"Returns ADD only"*.

**That's the finding, not the mechanism.** The vendor with the most production mileage on LLM-diffed memory shipped monotonic accumulation and pushed conflict resolution into ranking. Known failure modes of the old design: hallucinated IDs silently dropping ops (every branch wrapped in bare `except`); DELETE conflating "changed their mind" with "has two of these"; lossy UPDATE via the "keep the fact which has the most information" heuristic.

Two things still worth stealing:
- **The UUID→integer remap.** Cheap, general, applies to any prompt where the LLM must reference existing records.
- **`ADDITIVE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT`** (~470 lines) — specifically the Observation-Date-vs-Current-Date grounding, "contextually rich, not atomic," never-generalize-proper-nouns ("promoted to assistant manager" → keep "assistant manager"), and explicit anti-patterns for meta-extraction ("WRONG: 'User shared a case summary'") and echo-extraction.

One trap to avoid: their hybrid fusion computes `max_possible` **globally per query** (`1.0 + 1.0 if any bm25 + 0.5 if any entity`), so scores aren't comparable across queries and a fixed `threshold` won't transfer. Use RRF or per-candidate normalization.

### 2.6 (Bonus) The 2026 result that should change your write path

`[V-agent]` — **arXiv:2606.15903**, *"Control-Plane Placement Shapes Forgetting"* (Dongxu Yang, June 2026). I confirmed the paper is real. Thesis: **production failures are predominantly *forgetting* failures, not recall failures, yet every existing benchmark measures recall.**

Three placement regimes, tested across 13 configurations on **ForgetEval** (1,000 templated + 385 adversarial cases, Fleiss' κ = 0.958, MIT-licensed, 6-method adapter protocol):

| Where the LLM sits | Wins | Loses |
|---|---|---|
| **Nowhere** (deterministic) | lexical + temporal ≥95%, `temporal_qualifier` 37/37 | `identifier_obfuscation` **5%**, `cross_lingual` **0%** |
| **Inscribe-time** (during extraction) | canonicalization **100%** | intent-aware deletion **0%** |
| **Mutation-time hook** (during supersede/purge planning) | intent-aware deletion **78–85%**, overall **91.7–94.2%** | ~2.3 s/mutation vs 64–191 ms |

The regimes are **complementary, not redundant.** And the cost is trivial for a nightly job: ~$0.00044 per mutation call, and **recall latency is unchanged** — the hook only fires on writes.

The axis-flip result: **MemPalace scores 0/385 on ForgetEval-Adv and 40% on a recall benchmark** — mid-pack on recall, catastrophic on forgetting. Graphiti scores **7.0%** and HippoRAG **9.5%** on ForgetEval, because neither exposes deletion primitives. Recall rankings are close to the inverse of forgetting rankings.

Caveat the authors state themselves: 253/385 adversarial cases were drafted by DeepSeek-V3, admitted by a Qwen judge, and the winning hook is also DeepSeek-V3. On externally authored cases the deterministic band drops from 63–68% to 28–51%. The *directional* finding is solid; absolute numbers are soft.

## 3. Patterns catalog

**P1 — Bi-temporal supersession.** Four timestamps: two for event time (`valid_at`/`invalid_at`), two for transaction time (`created_at`/`expired_at`). Contradiction closes the old window rather than deleting the row. Enables "as of" queries on both axes and makes backfill correct. *Graphiti, Zep, mem0^g (paper only), Supermemory (partial).*

**P2 — Two candidate sets, one adjudication call.** Retrieve *duplicate* candidates (scope-constrained: same entity pair / same anchor) and *contradiction* candidates (broad semantic search) separately, then present both to one LLM call with continuous indexing. Scoping the duplicate set is what keeps this tractable — Zep's paper says so explicitly. *Graphiti.*

**P3 — Deterministic-first resolution ladder.** Exact match → cheap fuzzy (MinHash/LSH + Jaccard) → LLM only for the residue and for *ambiguous* exact matches. Treat ambiguity as an escalation signal, not a tie-break. *Graphiti, Cognee (UUID5 from identity fields).*

**P4 — Reflection over an importance budget.** Accumulate an importance/poignancy counter; fire consolidation when it crosses a threshold, not on a fixed clock. Generate a small number of questions, retrieve per question, synthesize insights **with citations to the evidence records**. *Generative Agents (threshold 150), A-MEM (every 100 notes), Honcho (≥50 conclusions AND ≥8h AND 60-min idle).*

**P5 — Backward-propagating revision.** A new memory doesn't just get linked; it triggers rewriting of its neighbours' *descriptions and tags*. Cheaper than merging and doesn't destroy anything. *A-MEM, Graphiti entity summaries, Zep observations.*

**P6 — Dual watermarks on incremental consolidation.** `[V-direct]` from Graphiti's `SagaNode`: `last_summarized_at` is **wall-clock** and is the *filter* watermark (pick up anything whose `created_at` > this, so backfilled items with old event times still get caught); `last_summarized_episode_valid_at` is the **event-time** watermark that answers "how fresh is this summary?" Two fields with deliberately different semantics. Directly applicable to your nightly job.

**P7 — Deltas merged by non-LLM logic.** Never let the LLM rewrite the whole store. Emit itemized deltas with stable IDs and helpful/harmful counters; merge deterministically. ACE (arXiv:2510.04618) measured the failure mode: **18,282 tokens → 122 tokens in one step, accuracy 66.7 → 57.1 — below the 63.7 no-adaptation baseline.** *ACE, Anthropic Dreams (writes to a new store, never mutates the input).*

**P8 — Mutation-time LLM hook.** Put the LLM in the *planning* of supersede/purge/release, not just in extraction. It's the only placement that recovers intent-aware deletion, and it costs nothing on the read path. *ForgetEval (arXiv:2606.15903).*

**P9 — Facts as index keys over verbatim values.** LongMemEval's ablation: replacing rounds with extracted facts *hurts* (information loss), but indexing `K = V + fact` beats both — Recall@5 0.582→**0.644**, Recall@10 0.692→**0.784**, QA 0.615→**0.657**. Extract for retrieval, keep the source for grounding.

**P10 — RRF-fused hybrid + optional cross-encoder.** Dense + BM25 → RRF → rerank. Constants in the wild: Graphiti `rank_const=1`, Letta/Turbopuffer `k=60` (0.5/0.5 weights), MongoDB `$rankFusion` **hardcoded 60**. Nobody uses cosine alone anymore.

**P11 — Score-shaped recency, not filtered recency.** Redis Agent Memory Server publishes the only fully-specified formula:
```
final    = 0.8·semantic + 0.2·recency
recency  = 0.6·freshness + 0.4·novelty
freshness = exp(-ln2 · days_since_created     / 30)
novelty   = exp(-ln2 · days_since_last_access /  7)
```
Apache-2.0, and it maps directly onto a `$score` stage inside `$scoreFusion`. Related: MemoryBank's `R = exp(-t/S)` with `S += 1` on recall. *(Note `[V-direct]`: MemoryBank's reference implementation has an operator-precedence bug — `math.exp(-t / 5*S)` evaluates as `exp(-(t/5)·S)`, so higher strength causes **faster** forgetting. Intended: `exp(-t/(5*S))`. And forgetting is stochastic: `if random.random() > retention: forget`.)*

**P12 — Decay as a multiplier, expiry as a filter-out-of-view.** mem0's platform decay never zeroes a candidate (worst case 0.3×); `expiration_date` hides but doesn't delete. Preserves recoverability.

**P13 — Provenance as a first-class queryable join.** MemMachine's `citations(profile_id → episode_id)` table; Graphiti's `EntityEdge.episodes[]`; Honcho's Dialectic tracing a conclusion back to its premises; Auto-Dreamer giving the consolidator a `get_source_trace` tool. Your `sources ↔ facts ↔ derivedFrom` is the same idea.

**P14 — Provenance semirings, not flat lineage.** `derivedFrom: ObjectId[]` is `Lineage(X)` — it cannot distinguish AND from OR. To answer "does this derived fact survive if I delete source S?", you need at least `PosBool(X)`: DNF nesting `derivedFrom: ObjectId[][]`, or a `derivation: "merge" | "corroboration" | "inference"` discriminator. (Green/Karvounarakis/Tannen, PODS 2007.)

**P15 — Non-destructive consolidation output.** Anthropic's Dreams writes a **brand-new memory store** and never mutates the input; you review and discard. Immutable memory *versions* (`memver_…`) plus a **`redact` endpoint** on them — the only published erasure-with-audit primitive from any vendor.

**P16 — Runtime-driven persistence, not tool-driven.** MongoDB's own `@mongodb-developer/vercel-ai-memory` README says tool-driven session writes are *"not deterministic: the model sometimes skips writes."* Persist from hooks. Corollary from Mastra: run memory processors **after** output guardrails, so an aborting guardrail prevents persistence entirely.

**P17 — Two-tier context loading.** Always-in-context core + tree-and-descriptions visible with contents fetched on demand. Letta after three years landed on `grep` over Markdown for the second tier and dropped the vector index. OpenViking compiles every entry to L0 (~100 tok) / L1 (~2k) / L2 (full).

**P18 — Absolute-date normalization at write time.** Letta's sleep-time prompt: *"do not write 'today' or 'recently'... because 'today' and 'recently' are relative, and the memory is persisted indefinitely."* mem0's extraction prompt grounds against an explicit `## Observation Date`. Trivial to implement, high value.

**P19 — Attributed beliefs are not contradictions.** "Anna says the deadline is tight" vs "Petra says it's comfortable" is two facts, not a conflict. Honcho makes this structural with `(observer_id, observed_id)`. GroupMemBench shows this is where team-context systems collapse — best system 27.1% on knowledge-update.

**P20 — Contradiction as an edge, resolution deferred.** Cognee logs a WARNING and writes a `contradicts` edge; nothing is rewritten. Your review queue *is* this pattern — TOKI (arXiv:2606.06240) types it as the **await-confirmation** operator, the strongest of four for correctness.

**P21 — Keyed judge logging.** TOKI's sharp result: *"keyed logging of the adjudicating judge is necessary for replay consistency, a discipline every deployed baseline we audit omits."* Log model + version + prompt hash + verdict, committed **before** the operator commits. Otherwise re-adjudicating the same contradiction can return a different winner.

**P22 — Exactly-once string matching on edits.** Letta's `memory_replace` requires `old_string` to occur exactly once and errors with line numbers otherwise; legacy `core_memory_replace` used `str.replace()` and silently replaced all occurrences. Anthropic's memory tool specifies the same strict behavior. Copy the strict one.

## 4. Evaluation and benchmarks

### The state of the field

**LOCOMO is broken and everyone knows it.** Verified by direct dataset inspection: the public `locomo10.json` has 1,986 questions, of which **446 are category 5 (adversarial) and 444 of those have no `answer` field at all** — they carry `adversarial_answer`, which is *the answer the model must not give*. A harness keying on `answer` silently drops them; a harness keying on `adversarial_answer` as gold **rewards hallucination**. That is the mechanical explanation for the Zep↔Mem0 dispute, where Mem0 alleged Zep's 84% excluded cat-5 from the denominator while counting cat-5 correct answers in the numerator (recomputed: 58.44%).

Additional measured defects: 99/1,540 wrong golden answers (6.4%, capping any system at ~93.57%); a gpt-4o-mini judge that **accepted 62.81% of deliberately wrong "vague-but-topical" answers**; conversations of only 16k–26k tokens, so full-context wins.

Two independent results that should end the argument:
- **Letta**: a plain filesystem with `grep`/`search_files` on **gpt-4o-mini** scores **74.0%**, beating mem0's best graph variant (68.5%). Their own conclusion: current memory benchmarks may not be meaningful.
- **Mem0's own paper**: full-context **72.90** beats Mem0 **66.88** and Mem0^g **68.44**. The paper's real claim is cost/latency, which marketing flattens into "SOTA."

**Independent reproduction gap:** Maximem's standardized harness reproduces Mem0's published LongMemEval **93.4% at 73.8%**, attributing the delta to dataset-specific equivalence rules mapped to public question IDs, judge prompts instructing "lean toward yes," and asymmetric verification gates (five steps required before marking WRONG, none before marking CORRECT).

### Statistical power — the thing nobody accounts for

Computed on verified counts (Wilson 95% CI, two-proportion at 80% power):

| Slice | n | CI half-width | Min detectable difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| LongMemEval overall | 500 | ±4.4 | 8.7 pts |
| temporal-reasoning | 133 | ±8.4 | 16.8 |
| **knowledge-update** | **78** | ±10.8 | **22.0** |
| **abstention** | **30** | ±16.8 | **35.4** |
| LoCoMo cats 1–4 | 1,540 | ±2.5 | 4.9 |

**The two categories that matter most for your product — knowledge-update and abstention — are the two least-powered in the benchmark.** Zep's "knowledge update +6.52%" is noise on n=78.

For your own golden set (paired design, McNemar): 93 per arm to detect 20 pts, 170 for 15 pts, 388 for 10 pts.

### What's actually current in mid-2026

| Purpose | Use | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Regression smoke test | LoCoMo cats 1–4 | never cat 5 |
| Knowledge update / abstention | **LongMemEval-S (`longmemeval-cleaned`)** | the original haystack contained contradicting sessions |
| Contradiction at scale | **BEAM** (ICLR 2026), MemoryAgentBench FactConsolidation | see below |
| **Your product shape** | **GroupMemBench**, **GateMem** | multi-party workplace threads; multi-principal governance |
| Deletion / GDPR | **ForgetEval** (MIT, 6-method adapter) | nothing else tests it |
| Does memory help the *task* | **MemoryArena** (ICML 2026), **STATE-Bench** (Microsoft, MIT) | the 2026 shift |

**The three numbers that should reframe your priorities:**

1. **BEAM, Contradiction Resolution: 0.006–0.050 across every model and method.** Effectively zero, while the same systems score 0.3–0.8 on retrieval. On MemoryAgentBench multi-hop conflict resolution, everything maxes out at 6%.
2. **GroupMemBench (multi-party workplace threads, the closest published analogue to your system):** BM25 43.22 avg > HippoRAG 39.72 > A-Mem 35.10 > MemGPT 28.15 > **Mem0 25.73** > GraphRAG 20.56. Mem0 scores **4.67%** on knowledge-update. The authors: *"current memory ingestion erases the structural and lexical features group memory depends on."* Notably, **abstention stays >80% while every content-bearing category collapses** — systems know when they don't know, but not what's true now.
3. **MemoryArena:** agents near-perfect on LoCoMo drop to 40–60%; swapping active memory for long-context-only took task completion from >80% to ~45%.

**GateMem's Memory Governance Score is the best top-line metric published for a system like yours:**

```
MGS = U · (1 − A) · (1 − F)
  U = utility (correct answer AND judge-confirmed factual coverage)
  A = access-control violation rate
  F = active-forgetting failure rate
```

Multiplicative on purpose: *"a system cannot obtain a high overall score merely by being highly useful if it leaks protected information, nor by being perfectly secure if it paralyzes legitimate authorized queries."* Track over-refusal rate separately.

### The metric stack to actually implement

From the 2026 survey (arXiv:2603.07670), four layers:
- **L1 task effectiveness** — success rate, factual correctness
- **L2 memory quality** — retrieved-record precision/recall, **contradiction rate**, **staleness distribution**, coverage
- **L3 efficiency** — latency p50/p95, prompt tokens, retrieval calls, storage growth
- **L4 governance** — privacy leakage, deletion compliance, access-scope violations

Plus, from practitioners:
- **Zep's Context Completeness** (COMPLETE / PARTIAL / INSUFFICIENT) as the *primary* metric, because it isolates memory quality from LLM generation quality.
- **`pass^k`, not `pass@k`.** At 75% per-trial success, pass@3 ≈ 98% but **pass^3 ≈ 42%**. For a nightly job that can silently poison the knowledge base, pass^k is the honest number.
- **Letta's Memory Write task design** — ingest a transcript, **delete the transcript**, then ask questions only answerable from extracted facts. Plus a penalty for extraneous memory operations, because "models good at archival memory might overuse memory operations when unnecessary."
- **Chroma's generative benchmarking** — build the golden set from *your* documents. Their headline: text-embedding-3-large scores 0.997 Recall@10 on clean Wikipedia and **0.552 on real production queries**, and jina-v3 beats text-embedding-3-large on *every MTEB English task* while losing on the real corpus. **Never pick an embedding model from MTEB.** Their 472-query eval set cost ~$4.72.
- **Chroma's Context Rot** (18 models, 194,480 calls): performance degrades with input length even for verbatim replication; degrades *faster* for low needle–question similarity; and across **all 18 models**, performance was better on shuffled haystacks than logically structured ones. Their LongMemEval slice: 113k-token full prompt vs ~300-token focused prompt, with the focused prompt scoring **significantly higher** — the strongest quantitative case for your architecture.
- **Krippendorff's α, not Cohen's κ**, for your review queue (reviewers dip in and out; κ can't handle incomplete data). α ≥ 0.800 reliable, 0.667–0.800 tentative. Beware the kappa paradox with a 90% accept rate.
- **ECE (15 bins) + MCE** on extractor confidence; use **MCE** for the band you auto-accept without review. Temperature scaling is the right default.

**One thing to skip:** truth-discovery algorithms (TruthFinder et al.). The QCRI experimental evaluation found that with fewer than ~8 distinct values per item, *"most of the methods perform worse than random guessing, with precision from .1 to .4"* — and MajorityVoting hits 0.9804 precision in 0.009s. A team knowledge base is exactly the low-conflict regime. What *is* worth taking is CATD's shrinkage idea: `reliability(s) = (accepted(s) + α·μ) / (total(s) + α)` with α ≈ 10–20, so a source with 2 accepted facts doesn't get reliability 1.0. Your review queue gives you `accepted`/`total` for free.
