| 4B | ~8.0 GB | ~10–13 GB |
| 8B | ~15.1–16.4 GB | ~18–22 GB |

**What fits — [I]:**
- **L4 (24 GB, Ada sm89, 72 W)** and **A10G (24 GB, Ampere sm86)**: 0.3B/0.6B trivially; you can co-host an embedder **and** a reranker in two TEI containers on one card. 4B comfortable. **8B fp16 fits (~16 GB) but leaves only ~6–8 GB** — fine at 512-token passages, tight at 8k context or large batches. L4 is the cheapest sane production card for TEI; A10G is ~15–25% faster on fp16 GEMM.
- **RTX 4090 (24 GB, sm89)**: ~1.5–2x an L4 on fp16 for the same models, but no ECC, no NVLink, and NVIDIA's datacenter EULA restricts GeForce in rented DCs — check your German host's terms.
- **L40S (48 GB, Ada)**: 8B embedder + 0.6B–4B reranker co-resident with room to spare. **[I]** This is the sweet spot if you want a single card doing both stages.
- **H100 (80 GB)**: everything, including 8B embed + 8B rerank + long context. Overkill unless you're batch-indexing millions of chunks.

**Batch-size and long-context effects — [I], arithmetic:**
- TEI's `--max-batch-tokens` (default **16384**) is the real VRAM dial, not "batch size". Activation memory scales ~linearly with total batch tokens when FlashAttention is on.
- **The 8k blowup is an attention-materialization problem.** Without FlashAttention, one attention score matrix costs `batch × heads × L² × 2 bytes`. For **L=8192, 16 heads: 16 × 8192² × 2 B = 2.15 GB for a single sequence, per layer step.** With FlashAttention it's O(L) and effectively free. Practical consequences:
  - **Turing/T4 images ship with FA off by default** (precision bug) → do not run 8k context on T4.
  - **ONNX Runtime / CPU paths generally do not use FlashAttention** → 8k-token CPU embedding is memory-hostile. Chunk to ≤1024 tokens on CPU.
- **Decoder-based embedders (Qwen3) additionally pay KV cache during prefill — [I]:** Qwen3-0.6B (28 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128) = `2×28×8×128×2 B` = **112 KiB/token** → **0.88 GiB for one 8k sequence**. Qwen3-8B (36 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128) = **144 KiB/token** → **1.13 GiB per 8k sequence**. Batch 8 of those on an L4 running an 8B model will OOM.
- **vLLM specific [V/I]**: `--gpu-memory-utilization` defaults to 0.9, so vLLM claims 90% of the card regardless of model size — you cannot naively co-host a vLLM reranker and a vLLM embedder on one GPU without lowering it on both.

**Third-party ballparks (secondary source, treat as order-of-magnitude only)** — Spheron blog https://www.spheron.network/blog/self-host-embedding-reranker-tei-gpu-cloud/ **[I, low authority]**: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B ~2 GB, 4B ~8 GB, 8B ~16 GB, BGE-M3 ~2.5 GB, BGE-large ~1.5 GB — consistent with the arithmetic above, which is the main reason to trust it at all.

## 6. Latency expectations

**Embedding, GPU** — **[I, low authority]** (Spheron, same caveat): tokens/s at batch 512 — BGE-M3 on A100 ~60,000; on H100 ~90,000; Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B on A100 ~55,000, on RTX 4090 ~20,000. Single-query p50 embed **5–15 ms**.
**[V]** TEI's own README benchmark banner is `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5` on an **NVIDIA A10 at 512 tokens**, charted at batch 1 and batch 32 (charts only, no tabulated figures).

**Embedding, CPU** — **[V]** BGE-large (355M) int8 on Sapphire Rapids: **<20 ms at batch 1**; e5-base-v2: **15 ms** int8 vs 50 ms fp32 on 8 vCPU.
**[V]** EmbeddingGemma-300M: **<15 ms for 256 input tokens on EdgeTPU**, sub-200 MB RAM with QAT. https://developers.googleblog.com/en/introducing-embeddinggemma/
**[V]** `gte-multilingual-base` (305M) claims **10x inference speedup vs decoder-only embedders** like gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct. https://huggingface.co/Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-base

**Cross-encoder reranking — this is your critical path. Best numbers found:**

**[V]** https://bigdataboutique.com/blog/rag-reranking-improving-retrieval-quality-with-cross-encoders (explicitly labelled "ballparks", A10/L4-class GPU):
| Model | Latency |
|---|---|
| MiniLM-class (22M) | **50–80 ms for 100 docs @ 256 tokens** |
| **BGE-reranker-v2-m3 (568M)** | **80–200 ms for 100 docs @ 512 tokens** |
| bge-reranker-v2-gemma (2B) | **200–400 ms** |

> "A single A10 typically handles **50–100 QPS at top-100 rerank depth at 512-token passages.**"
> Production systems see "**under 200 ms of added latency**" reranking 50–100 candidates.

**[V]** https://aimultiple.com/rerankers — measured, **NVIDIA H100 PCIe 80GB (Runpod), transformers 5.2.0 / torch 2.8.0 / CUDA 12.8.1, 100 candidates/query, 300 queries**, retriever `multilingual-e5-base`, corpus = English Amazon reviews (short docs, not 512 tokens):
| Model | Rerank time (100 docs) | Hit@1 |
|---|---|---|
| `gte-reranker-modernbert-base` (149M) | **~170 ms** | 83.00% |
| `jina-reranker-v3` (560M) | **~188 ms** | 81.33% |
| `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-1b-v2` (1.2B) | **~243 ms** | 83.00% |
| `Qwen3-Reranker-4B` (4B) | **>1,000 ms** | 77.67% |
| no reranker baseline | — | 62.67% |

**Practical read for your 20–50 candidates @ ~512 tokens — [I]:**
- **20–50 docs is ~0.2–0.5x the 100-doc cost** (compute is close to linear in doc count at these batch sizes).
- **`bge-reranker-v2-m3` (568M XLM-R, Apache-2.0) on an L4/A10G: ~40–100 ms for 20–50 passages @ 512 tokens.** This is the number to plan around for a German product.
- **`gte-multilingual-reranker-base` (306M, Apache-2.0, 8k ctx) on the same card: ~25–60 ms** — roughly half the FLOPs of bge-v2-m3, and it runs in TEI today.
- **Anything ≥4B (Qwen3-Reranker-4B/8B) pushes you past 500 ms–1 s** for 20–50 docs even on strong hardware. Not viable in an interactive path.
- **CPU reranking of 50 × 512-token passages is ~5–20 s** for a 300–568M cross-encoder even with int8. **Do not put a CPU cross-encoder on the request path.** If you must be CPU-only, use `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` (22.7M, Apache-2.0) — but it is English-only, so for German you'd need a distilled multilingual MiniLM.
- **Two-stage RAG budget [I]**: bi-encoder query embed (5–15 ms GPU) + vector search (5–30 ms) + rerank 30 candidates (40–100 ms) ≈ **60–150 ms** before the LLM. Matches the "<200 ms added" figure above.

## 8. Licensing landmines for a commercial German product — [V]

- **Every current Jina text model is CC-BY-NC-4.0**: `jina-embeddings-v3` (572M), `jina-embeddings-v5-text-small` (596M, released 2026-02-18, 32K ctx, MRL 32–1024, MTEB-multilingual 67.0 / English 71.7), `jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual` (278M), `jina-reranker-v3` (597M), `jina-reranker-v3.5` (0.6B, 131K ctx, released 2026-07-27). **Non-commercial. You cannot self-host these in a paid product** without a commercial licence from Jina. The one exception: **`jinaai/jina-embeddings-v2-base-de` is Apache-2.0** (161M, German+English bilingual) — and T-Systems hosts exactly that one in Germany.
- **`google/embeddinggemma-300m`** is under the **Gemma licence** (not OSI, gated on HF, use restrictions apply) — usually fine commercially but requires accepting terms and passing `HF_TOKEN` to TEI.
- **`nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-1b-v2`** is `license: other` (NVIDIA open model licence) — read it.
- **Clean Apache-2.0 / MIT stack for German**: `intfloat/multilingual-e5-large(-instruct)` (MIT), `BAAI/bge-m3` (MIT), `Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2.0` (Apache-2.0), `Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-base` (Apache-2.0), `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-*` (Apache-2.0) + `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` (Apache-2.0), `Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-reranker-base` (Apache-2.0), `mixedbread-ai/mxbai-rerank-*-v2` (Apache-2.0), `Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-*` (Apache-2.0).
- **Do not use `gte-reranker-modernbert-base` for German** — ModernBERT is an English-only backbone despite being the fastest option in the aimultiple benchmark.

## 9. Bottom line for your stack

**[I]** Recommendation, given a German-language RAG product that must self-host or use an EU host:

- **Engine: TEI v1.9.3 (Apache-2.0)** for both stages. Two containers on one GPU: `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference:89-1.9` (L4/L40S/4090) or `:86-1.9` (A10G). It has `/embed` + `/rerank` + `dimensions` (MRL) + Prometheus + OTLP + `--api-key`, boots in seconds, and is the lowest-latency option at batch 1. Local dev on your Mac via `brew install text-embeddings-inference` (Metal).
- **Embedder**: `intfloat/multilingual-e5-large-instruct` (560M, MIT) or `Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-base` (305M, Apache-2.0, 8192 ctx, 768 dims — ~1.8x cheaper to run, and 768 dims halves your Atlas Search vector index size vs 1024). Set `--default-prompt-name query` for e5.
- **Reranker**: `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` (568M, Apache-2.0, XLM-R — strong German) or `Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-reranker-base` (306M, Apache-2.0) if you need the extra ~2x speed. Both run in TEI today. Budget **40–100 ms for 20–50 passages @ 512 tokens on an L4**.
- **Avoid**: Qwen3-Reranker (unsupported in TEI, >500 ms in vLLM), any Jina model (CC-BY-NC), Scaleway's rerank endpoint (it's just cosine similarity), OVH for reranking (doesn't exist).
- **Reach for vLLM only** if you specifically need Qwen3-Reranker / mxbai-rerank-v2 / bge-reranker-v2-gemma, or a Cohere-compatible `/v2/rerank` wire format — and read its own warning that pooling models aren't optimized there.
- **EU managed fallback**: IONOS (Berlin, real rerank endpoint, $0.02/M for bge-m3 embeddings) is the only one that covers both stages today. Scaleway dedicated + custom HF model import is the escape hatch if you need a specific cross-encoder on French soil.
- **CPU is viable for indexing, not for the request path**: int8 ONNX via TEI's `ort` backend on VNNI-capable hardware gets you ~3–10 docs/s at 512 tokens for a 560M model. Cross-encoder reranking on CPU is 5–20 s for 50 passages — don't.

**The load-bearing caveat, quoted verbatim from the docs:**

> "Currently, there is no official support for inline citations with Streamdown or the Response component. This is because:
> - There isn't any good markdown syntax for inline citations
> - Language models don't naturally respond with inline citation syntax
> - The AI SDK doesn't have built-in support for inline citations"

The docs' recommended workaround is `experimental_useObject` / `streamObject` with a Zod schema (`content: string` + `citations: [{number, title, url, description?, quote?}]`), then splitting on `/(\[\d+\])/` and mapping markers to `<InlineCitation>`. That's structured-output, not text streaming — you lose token-by-token markdown streaming.

**The better path they hint at but don't document — and I verified it works.** Streamdown v2 (which `MessageResponse` wraps) supports custom tags:

```tsx
<Streamdown
  allowedTags={{ source: ["id"] }}
  components={{ source: ({ id, children }) => <YourCitation factId={id}>{children}</YourCitation> }}
  literalTagContent={["mention"]}
>
```

Without `allowedTags`, custom tags are stripped by sanitization; only listed attributes survive (`"data*"` allows all `data-*`). So for your "every claim cites the fact it came from": system-prompt the model to emit `<fact id="...">…</fact>`, allowlist it, and map it onto `InlineCitation` — you keep true streaming *and* get per-claim provenance. This is the approach I'd recommend. (Docs: [streamdown.ai/docs/components](https://streamdown.ai/docs/components))

## Section 2 — EU-resident retrieval on MongoDB Atlas

### The short version

Your instinct was right on `$rankFusion`/`$scoreFusion`/`$score`, and **the problem is worse than you thought: `autoEmbed` is disqualified for exactly the same reason as `$rerank`.** Same US inference platform, confirmed verbatim in two separate places plus MongoDB's subprocessor list.

### 1. `$rankFusion`, `$scoreFusion`, `$score` — CLEAN (VERIFIED)

All three are plain server aggregation stages. They execute inside `mongod`/`mongot` on your own cluster nodes, in your cluster's region. No model, no API key, no project-level enablement toggle, no usage-based model billing, no residency disclaimer — in sharp contrast to `$rerank` and `autoEmbed`, which have all five.

- `$rankFusion`: "first executes all input pipelines independently and then de-duplicates and combines the input pipeline results into a final ranked results set… This stage uses the Reciprocal Rank Fusion algorithm." Formula `Σ w/(60 + r(d))`. **"`$rankFusion` is only available for deployments that use MongoDB 8.0 and later."** ([docs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/rankFusion/))
- `$scoreFusion`: "de-duplicates and combines the input pipeline results into a final scored results set." `combination.method` = `avg` | `expression`; `normalization` = `none|sigmoid|minMaxScaler`. **"`$scoreFusion` is only available for deployments that use MongoDB 8.3+."** ([docs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/scoreFusion/))
- `$score`: "computes and returns a new score as metadata… optionally normalizes." **New in MongoDB 8.2.** ([docs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/score/))

Status: **VERIFIED clean** by direct doc reading plus absence of any inference/subprocessor mechanism. Strictly, MongoDB never writes "this runs in your region" — that's inferred, but it's inferred from the fact that these are aggregation stages with no model plane at all.

### 2. `$vectorSearch` — CLEAN (VERIFIED)

Runs on the `mongot` process on your cluster's own nodes — either colocated with `mongod` or on dedicated Search Nodes. HNSW for ANN, or ENN for exhaustive. From the deployment-options doc: testing/prototyping = "MongoDB and Search processes run on the same node"; production = "MongoDB and Search processes run on different nodes." No external calls when you supply your own vectors.

Caveat: this is only true if you supply vectors yourself. The moment the index field is `type: "autoEmbed"`, see below.

### 3. `autoEmbed` — DISQUALIFIED (VERIFIED, verbatim)

This is the crux, and the answer is no. Three independent primary sources:

**(a)** [Automated Embedding Architecture](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/crud-embeddings/automated-embedding/overview):
> "**Hosted Service**: All embedding models are hosted and maintained by MongoDB. The model inference platform runs on MongoDB's infrastructure in Google Cloud cloud in a US region. You don't need to deploy, configure, or manage any model infrastructure."

**(b)** [Vector Search index reference](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/index/vector-search-type) — the sharpest statement:
> "The embedding model inference runs on a multi-tenant service in the Atlas Data Plane, available in MongoDB's Google Cloud based infrastructure in a US region. **This means that your data is sent to MongoDB's inference infrastructure for embedding generation and retrieval, regardless of your cluster's cloud provider.** Data transfer costs apply."

Note "and retrieval" — this hits **query text at read time**, not just ingest. Every user question leaves the EU.

**(c)** [MongoDB Subprocessors](https://www.mongodb.com/products/platform/trust/subprocessors) — "Customer Personal Data may be processed by the following subprocessors if you choose to utilize certain optional AI features of the Cloud Services":

| Entity | Processing | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Google LLC | Model hosting services for the optional embedding and reranking model services | **United States** |
| Baseten Labs, Inc. | Inference services for the optional embedding and reranking model services | **United States** |
| Microsoft Corp (Azure OpenAI) | AI models for certain optional generative AI features | **United States** |

Models offered: `voyage-4-lite` ($0.02/M), `voyage-4` ($0.06/M, recommended), `voyage-4-large` ($0.12/M), `voyage-code-3` ($0.18/M). autoEmbed dims are constrained to **256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048** (default 1024) and `path`/`model`/`quantization`/`numDimensions` are immutable after index creation.

Mitigating facts worth recording: "Text sent to Automated Embedding service is used only to generate embeddings and is not stored or used for model training," and "All communication with the Automated Embedding service occurs over encrypted connections." MongoDB and Voyage AI Innovations self-certify under the **EU-US Data Privacy Framework**, so the transfer has a lawful mechanism — it is a *residency* failure, not automatically a *legality* failure. But it breaks a strict "no EU data leaves the EU" posture, and it's inconsistent with your AssemblyAI-EU choice.

**Self-managed escape hatch doesn't help either:** "For self-managed deployments that are configured to use Voyage AI API key, MongoDB sends text to Voyage AI's API endpoints to generate embeddings."

### 3b. `$rerank` — confirmed disqualified, with a blunter quote than you had

From [Manage Project Settings](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/manage-project-settings), section "Native Reranking: $rerank Aggregation Stage":
> "Atlas uses Voyage AI reranking models, which incur usage-based costs. The model inference platform runs on MongoDB infrastructure in a Google Cloud cloud deployment in a US region."
> "The `$rerank` stage is available only on clusters running MongoDB 8.3 or later, and it is disabled by default."

And from the [`$rerank` stage reference](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/rerank/), the decisive sentence:
> "`$rerank` does not run Voyage AI reranking models on your Atlas cluster resources."

Models: `rerank-2.5`, `rerank-2.5-lite`, `rerank-2`, `rerank-2-lite`. Currently **Preview** ("we don't recommend using this feature in production environments"). The standalone Embedding & Reranking API (`https://ai.mongodb.com/v1/{embeddings,rerank,...}`) is the same platform.

**Good news:** it's off by default and opt-in per project. Use an Atlas Resource Policy to keep it that way.

### 4. EU regions

Vector Search and the fusion stages are **version-gated, not region-gated** — they work in any Atlas region. Dedicated Search Nodes are the only regional constraint: "available in all the regions for Google Cloud but only available in a subset of AWS and Azure regions."

German-relevant options (VERIFIED):

| Cloud | Region | Search Nodes |
|---|---|---|
| AWS | `eu-central-1` (Frankfurt) | Yes |
| AWS | `eu-west-1`, `eu-central-2`, `eu-north-1`, `eu-south-2`, `eu-west-2` | Yes |
| GCP | `europe-west3` (Frankfurt), `europe-west10` (Berlin) | Yes (all GCP regions) |
| Azure | `germanywestcentral`, `germanynorth`, `switzerlandnorth` | Subset; `italynorth` is low-CPU Search Nodes only |

autoEmbed cluster support (M0/Flex/M10+, with mandatory storage + tier autoscaling on M10+) is irrelevant — it's the inference platform, not the cluster, that's US.

`numDimensions` max is **8192**. Quantization: `none` | `scalar` (1/3.75 RAM) | `binary` (1/24 RAM, requires dims to be a multiple of 8).

### 5. BYOK / private endpoints / Data Federation — do not change the answer

Customer-managed keys (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault, optionally over private endpoints) and PrivateLink control encryption and network path for *cluster* data. They do not touch the model inference plane, which is a separate MongoDB-operated multi-tenant service.

What *is* useful: **Atlas Resource Policies** (Cedar) can hard-enforce EU-only cluster placement:
```
forbid(principal, action == ResourcePolicy::Action::"cluster.modify", resource)
unless { [ResourcePolicy::Region::"aws:eu-central-1"].containsAll(context.cluster.regions) };
```
Pair that with leaving Native Reranking disabled and never using `type: "autoEmbed"`.

### Citations and provenance — the honest answer

**`Sources`** — 4 exports: `Sources`, `SourcesTrigger` (takes `count`), `SourcesContent`, `Source` (an `<a>` with `href`/`title`). It's a collapsible footer list. The canonical example filters `message.parts.filter(p => p.type === "source-url")`. That's it — it's URL-shaped and coarse-grained.

**The load-bearing caveat, quoted verbatim from the docs:**

> "Currently, there is no official support for inline citations with Streamdown or the Response component. This is because:
> - There isn't any good markdown syntax for inline citations
> - Language models don't naturally respond with inline citation syntax
> - The AI SDK doesn't have built-in support for inline citations"

The docs' recommended workaround is `experimental_useObject` / `streamObject` with a Zod schema (`content: string` + `citations: [{number, title, url, description?, quote?}]`), then splitting on `/(\[\d+\])/` and mapping markers to `<InlineCitation>`. That's structured-output, not text streaming — you lose token-by-token markdown streaming.

**The better path they hint at but don't document — and I verified it works.** Streamdown v2 (which `MessageResponse` wraps) supports custom tags:

```tsx
<Streamdown
  allowedTags={{ source: ["id"] }}
  components={{ source: ({ id, children }) => <YourCitation factId={id}>{children}</YourCitation> }}
  literalTagContent={["mention"]}
>
```

Without `allowedTags`, custom tags are stripped by sanitization; only listed attributes survive (`"data*"` allows all `data-*`). So for your "every claim cites the fact it came from": system-prompt the model to emit `<fact id="...">…</fact>`, allowlist it, and map it onto `InlineCitation` — you keep true streaming *and* get per-claim provenance. This is the approach I'd recommend. (Docs: [streamdown.ai/docs/components](https://streamdown.ai/docs/components))

Other provenance-adjacent components: `chain-of-thought` has `ChainOfThoughtSearchResults`/`SearchResult` badges for showing what was retrieved; `tool` shows raw tool I/O; `context` shows token/cost accounting.

## Section 2 — EU-resident retrieval on MongoDB Atlas

### The short version

Your instinct was right on `$rankFusion`/`$scoreFusion`/`$score`, and **the problem is worse than you thought: `autoEmbed` is disqualified for exactly the same reason as `$rerank`.** Same US inference platform, confirmed verbatim in two separate places plus MongoDB's subprocessor list.

### 1. `$rankFusion`, `$scoreFusion`, `$score` — CLEAN (VERIFIED)

All three are plain server aggregation stages. They execute inside `mongod`/`mongot` on your own cluster nodes, in your cluster's region. No model, no API key, no project-level enablement toggle, no usage-based model billing, no residency disclaimer — in sharp contrast to `$rerank` and `autoEmbed`, which have all five.

- `$rankFusion`: "first executes all input pipelines independently and then de-duplicates and combines the input pipeline results into a final ranked results set… This stage uses the Reciprocal Rank Fusion algorithm." Formula `Σ w/(60 + r(d))`. **"`$rankFusion` is only available for deployments that use MongoDB 8.0 and later."** ([docs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/rankFusion/))
- `$scoreFusion`: "de-duplicates and combines the input pipeline results into a final scored results set." `combination.method` = `avg` | `expression`; `normalization` = `none|sigmoid|minMaxScaler`. **"`$scoreFusion` is only available for deployments that use MongoDB 8.3+."** ([docs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/scoreFusion/))
- `$score`: "computes and returns a new score as metadata… optionally normalizes." **New in MongoDB 8.2.** ([docs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/score/))

Status: **VERIFIED clean** by direct doc reading plus absence of any inference/subprocessor mechanism. Strictly, MongoDB never writes "this runs in your region" — that's inferred, but it's inferred from the fact that these are aggregation stages with no model plane at all.

### 2. `$vectorSearch` — CLEAN (VERIFIED)

Runs on the `mongot` process on your cluster's own nodes — either colocated with `mongod` or on dedicated Search Nodes. HNSW for ANN, or ENN for exhaustive. From the deployment-options doc: testing/prototyping = "MongoDB and Search processes run on the same node"; production = "MongoDB and Search processes run on different nodes." No external calls when you supply your own vectors.

Caveat: this is only true if you supply vectors yourself. The moment the index field is `type: "autoEmbed"`, see below.

### 3. `autoEmbed` — DISQUALIFIED (VERIFIED, verbatim)

This is the crux, and the answer is no. Three independent primary sources:

**(a)** [Automated Embedding Architecture](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/crud-embeddings/automated-embedding/overview):
> "**Hosted Service**: All embedding models are hosted and maintained by MongoDB. The model inference platform runs on MongoDB's infrastructure in Google Cloud cloud in a US region. You don't need to deploy, configure, or manage any model infrastructure."

**(b)** [Vector Search index reference](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/index/vector-search-type) — the sharpest statement:
> "The embedding model inference runs on a multi-tenant service in the Atlas Data Plane, available in MongoDB's Google Cloud based infrastructure in a US region. **This means that your data is sent to MongoDB's inference infrastructure for embedding generation and retrieval, regardless of your cluster's cloud provider.** Data transfer costs apply."

Note "and retrieval" — this hits **query text at read time**, not just ingest. Every user question leaves the EU.

**(c)** [MongoDB Subprocessors](https://www.mongodb.com/products/platform/trust/subprocessors) — "Customer Personal Data may be processed by the following subprocessors if you choose to utilize certain optional AI features of the Cloud Services":

| Entity | Processing | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Google LLC | Model hosting services for the optional embedding and reranking model services | **United States** |
| Baseten Labs, Inc. | Inference services for the optional embedding and reranking model services | **United States** |
| Microsoft Corp (Azure OpenAI) | AI models for certain optional generative AI features | **United States** |

Models offered: `voyage-4-lite` ($0.02/M), `voyage-4` ($0.06/M, recommended), `voyage-4-large` ($0.12/M), `voyage-code-3` ($0.18/M). autoEmbed dims are constrained to **256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048** (default 1024) and `path`/`model`/`quantization`/`numDimensions` are immutable after index creation.

Mitigating facts worth recording: "Text sent to Automated Embedding service is used only to generate embeddings and is not stored or used for model training," and "All communication with the Automated Embedding service occurs over encrypted connections." MongoDB and Voyage AI Innovations self-certify under the **EU-US Data Privacy Framework**, so the transfer has a lawful mechanism — it is a *residency* failure, not automatically a *legality* failure. But it breaks a strict "no EU data leaves the EU" posture, and it's inconsistent with your AssemblyAI-EU choice.

**Self-managed escape hatch doesn't help either:** "For self-managed deployments that are configured to use Voyage AI API key, MongoDB sends text to Voyage AI's API endpoints to generate embeddings."

### 3b. `$rerank` — confirmed disqualified, with a blunter quote than you had

From [Manage Project Settings](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/manage-project-settings), section "Native Reranking: $rerank Aggregation Stage":
> "Atlas uses Voyage AI reranking models, which incur usage-based costs. The model inference platform runs on MongoDB infrastructure in a Google Cloud cloud deployment in a US region."
> "The `$rerank` stage is available only on clusters running MongoDB 8.3 or later, and it is disabled by default."

And from the [`$rerank` stage reference](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/rerank/), the decisive sentence:
> "`$rerank` does not run Voyage AI reranking models on your Atlas cluster resources."

Models: `rerank-2.5`, `rerank-2.5-lite`, `rerank-2`, `rerank-2-lite`. Currently **Preview** ("we don't recommend using this feature in production environments"). The standalone Embedding & Reranking API (`https://ai.mongodb.com/v1/{embeddings,rerank,...}`) is the same platform.

**Good news:** it's off by default and opt-in per project. Use an Atlas Resource Policy to keep it that way.

### 4. EU regions

Vector Search and the fusion stages are **version-gated, not region-gated** — they work in any Atlas region. Dedicated Search Nodes are the only regional constraint: "available in all the regions for Google Cloud but only available in a subset of AWS and Azure regions."

German-relevant options (VERIFIED):

| Cloud | Region | Search Nodes |
|---|---|---|
| AWS | `eu-central-1` (Frankfurt) | Yes |
| AWS | `eu-west-1`, `eu-central-2`, `eu-north-1`, `eu-south-2`, `eu-west-2` | Yes |
| GCP | `europe-west3` (Frankfurt), `europe-west10` (Berlin) | Yes (all GCP regions) |
| Azure | `germanywestcentral`, `germanynorth`, `switzerlandnorth` | Subset; `italynorth` is low-CPU Search Nodes only |

autoEmbed cluster support (M0/Flex/M10+, with mandatory storage + tier autoscaling on M10+) is irrelevant — it's the inference platform, not the cluster, that's US.

`numDimensions` max is **8192**. Quantization: `none` | `scalar` (1/3.75 RAM) | `binary` (1/24 RAM, requires dims to be a multiple of 8).

### 5. BYOK / private endpoints / Data Federation — do not change the answer

Customer-managed keys (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault, optionally over private endpoints) and PrivateLink control encryption and network path for *cluster* data. They do not touch the model inference plane, which is a separate MongoDB-operated multi-tenant service.

What *is* useful: **Atlas Resource Policies** (Cedar) can hard-enforce EU-only cluster placement:
```
forbid(principal, action == ResourcePolicy::Action::"cluster.modify", resource)
unless { [ResourcePolicy::Region::"aws:eu-central-1"].containsAll(context.cluster.regions) };
```
Pair that with leaving Native Reranking disabled and never using `type: "autoEmbed"`.

### EU-resident embeddings and reranking — what actually works

**Option A — AWS Bedrock in `eu-central-1` (Frankfurt). Best managed option, and it solves BOTH problems.** (VERIFIED from AWS docs)

Rerankers ([rerank-supported](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/rerank-supported.html)) — note the column header is literally "Single-region model support":

| Model | Model ID | Regions incl. |
|---|---|---|
| Cohere Rerank 3.5 | `cohere.rerank-v3-5:0` | ap-northeast-1, ca-central-1, **eu-central-1**, us-east-1, us-west-2 |
| Amazon Rerank 1.0 | `amazon.rerank-v1:0` | ap-northeast-1, ca-central-1, **eu-central-1**, us-west-2 |

Embeddings ([knowledge-base-supported](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base-supported.html)):

| Model | Model ID | Dims | eu-central-1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cohere Embed Multilingual v3 | `cohere.embed-multilingual-v3` | 1024 (float + **binary**) | Yes |
| Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 | `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` | 256/512/1024 (float + binary) | Yes (+ 9 other EU regions) |

Cohere Embed Multilingual v3 at 1024 dims is a strong German performer, fits well under MongoDB's 8192 cap, and 1024 is a multiple of 8 so **binary quantization is available** — and Bedrock can emit binary vectors natively, which pairs neatly with MongoDB's `quantization: "binary"` (1/24 RAM).

Critical config warning, quoted: **"If you use cross-Region inference, your data can be shared across Regions."** Use the plain single-region model IDs, or if you need throughput, only `eu.*` EU inference profiles — AWS states "Requests from a source Region that lies in the EU can only be routed to other AWS Regions with the European Union" and "For EU CRIS, all destination Regions lie within the European Union." Never use `global.*` profiles.

**Option B — IONOS AI Model Hub (Germany). The most sovereignty-clean option.** (VERIFIED)

> "Your data is processed within Germany… data processing is confined within Germany. Your input data remains exclusively for your use and is excluded from training purposes."

**Option C — self-deploy Voyage models into your own EU infrastructure.** (VERIFIED) If you want `rerank-2.5` specifically, MongoDB/Voyage publish deployable model packages:

- Azure Marketplace → managed app in "a customer Azure account and virtual network (VNet)"

- Only 22 of 313 models are EU-capable, all `language` type: Anthropic Claude (Haiku 4.5 through Opus 5), Google Gemini 2.5/3.x, Amazon Nova.

**Practical implication:** AI Gateway is viable for your *generation* step if you switch off DeepSeek to an EU-capable model (Claude or Gemini with `geoRegion: 'eu'`), but it cannot serve your embeddings or reranking under EU residency at all. Those must come from Bedrock eu-central-1, IONOS, or self-hosting.

Atlas in `aws:eu-central-1` (or `gcp:europe-west3`) with a Resource Policy pinning regions and Native Reranking left disabled → your own embeddings from **Bedrock `cohere.embed-multilingual-v3`** (1024d, binary-quantized) or **IONOS BGE-M3** → `$vectorSearch` + `$search` combined with **`$rankFusion`** (or `$scoreFusion` on 8.3+) → **Bedrock `cohere.rerank-v3-5:0` in eu-central-1** as the cross-encoder → generation via AI Gateway with `inferenceRegion: {scope:'zone', geoRegion:'eu'}` on an EU-capable model. Never touch `type: "autoEmbed"` or `$rerank`.

All research is in. Here's the synthesis.

---

# 1. The residency picture — including one finding about code you're running now

## `autoEmbed` is disqualified too, and worse than `$rerank`

MongoDB's own index reference, verbatim:

> "The embedding model inference runs on a multi-tenant service in the Atlas Data Plane, available in MongoDB's Google Cloud based infrastructure in a US region. **This means that your data is sent to MongoDB's inference infrastructure for embedding generation and retrieval, regardless of your cluster's cloud provider.**"

Note *"and retrieval"* — this hits **query text at read time**, not just ingest. Every user question would leave the EU. Their subprocessor list names Google LLC and Baseten Labs (both US) for "the optional embedding and reranking model services."

So both of the shiny new MongoDB features I recommended are out. What survives is clean:

| Stage | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `$rankFusion` (8.0+) | ✅ Clean | Plain aggregation stage. No model, no API key, no usage billing, no residency disclaimer |
| `$scoreFusion` + `$score` (8.3+ / 8.2+) | ✅ Clean | Same — pure ranking math in `mongod` |
| `$vectorSearch` | ✅ Clean | Runs on `mongot` on your own cluster nodes — **provided you supply your own vectors** |
| `type: "autoEmbed"` | ❌ US inference, incl. query text | |
| `$rerank` | ❌ US inference | Also Preview; off by default — keep it that way |

Your `$score` insight survives intact, and it's still the highest-leverage change available: it lets you fold `confidence`, recency decay and source tier into ranking inside the database.

## The live finding: your extraction path has no residency control at all

I had the agent query Vercel AI Gateway's `/v1/models` endpoint (313 models) and read the `regions` array. Your current extraction model, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731`, **has no `regions` field at all** — and per Vercel's docs, "a model with no `regions` field doesn't support regional routing." `deepseek-v4-pro` is `["us"]`. Every DeepSeek variant is either US-only or has no regional routing whatsoever.

That means every meeting transcript and forwarded client email you currently push through `createGatewayGenerate` goes wherever the gateway routes it, with no guarantee and no config that can fix it. Given you took the trouble to use AssemblyAI's EU endpoint with 14 PII-redaction policies immediately upstream, this is an inconsistency worth closing.

The good news is that AI Gateway *does* have a real answer, with hard-fail semantics:

```ts
providerOptions: { gateway: { inferenceRegion: { scope: 'zone', geoRegion: 'eu' } } }
```

> "If AI Gateway can't honor the chosen region, the request fails instead of silently running somewhere else."

No silent cross-region fallback, verifiable per response via `providerMetadata.gateway.routing`. Costs about +10%, provider-set. Two caveats: residency is **opt-in** (without the flag you have none), and it pins *inference*, not ingress — "your request can terminate and be processed in any Vercel region before AI Gateway forwards it."

But only **22 of 313 models are EU-capable**, all of them `language` type: Anthropic Claude (Haiku 4.5 → Opus 5), Google Gemini 2.5/3.x, Amazon Nova. **Zero embedding models and zero rerankers support EU routing** — including Mistral's, despite Mistral being French. Going through the Gateway strips Mistral's own residency benefit; you'd have to call La Plateforme directly.

# 2. The EU-safe retrieval stack

**AWS Bedrock in `eu-central-1` (Frankfurt) solves both halves in one vendor:**

| Role | Model | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Embeddings | `cohere.embed-multilingual-v3` | 1024d, strong German, emits **binary** vectors natively |
| Reranker | `cohere.rerank-v3-5:0` | Cross-encoder, available in `eu-central-1` |

1024 dims sits well under MongoDB's 8192 cap and is a multiple of 8, so `quantization: "binary"` is available — 1/24 the RAM, and Bedrock can emit binary directly.

One configuration warning, quoted from AWS: **"If you use cross-Region inference, your data can be shared across Regions."** Use plain single-region model IDs, or `eu.*` inference profiles only. Never `global.*`.

**The sovereignty-cleanest alternative is IONOS AI Model Hub** (German data centres, ISO 27001): "data processing is confined within Germany… Your input data remains exclusively for your use and is excluded from training purposes." BGE-M3 embeddings (1024d, multilingual, 8192-token context) plus a Qwen3 cross-encoder reranker, OpenAI-compatible API. Smaller catalogue, less operational track record.

**Two traps worth knowing.** All Jina rerankers — including `jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual` — are **CC-BY-NC-4.0, research only**; self-hosting one in a commercial SaaS is a licence breach. Use `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` (Apache-2.0) if you self-host. And Azure OpenAI's `text-embedding-3-large` appears to be global-standard only with no Data Zone deployment — confirm with Microsoft before relying on it.

**Enforce it structurally.** Atlas Resource Policies take Cedar, so EU-only placement can be a hard constraint rather than a convention:

```cedar
forbid(principal, action == ResourcePolicy::Action::"cluster.modify", resource)
unless { [ResourcePolicy::Region::"aws:eu-central-1"].containsAll(context.cluster.regions) };
```

Pair that with leaving Native Reranking disabled at the project level and never writing `type: "autoEmbed"` in an index definition.

**Resulting pipeline:** Atlas in `aws:eu-central-1` → your own Bedrock/IONOS embeddings → `$vectorSearch` + `$search` fused with `$rankFusion` (or `$scoreFusion` + `$score` on 8.3+) → Bedrock `cohere.rerank-v3-5:0` in Frankfurt → generation via AI Gateway with `geoRegion: 'eu'` on an EU-capable model.

# 3. The surface: what each Vercel layer actually gives you

## AI Elements

Not a runtime dependency — a **shadcn-style copy-in registry**, Apache-2.0, components vendored into `@/components/ai-elements/*.tsx` where you own and can modify them. 48 components across chatbot / code / voice / workflow families.

```bash
npx ai-elements@latest add message inline-citation sources tool reasoning
```

**The finding that matters most for you:** `InlineCitation` and `Sources` have **zero AI SDK coupling** — their only npm dep is `lucide-react`. You can drive them directly from MongoDB fact records without going through a message stream at all. `InlineCitation` gives you a hover-card with a carousel over multiple sources per marker, including `InlineCitationSource` (title/url/description) and `InlineCitationQuote` for the excerpt.

**One version conflict to check before you commit.** AI Elements targets `ai: ^6.0.105` and `@ai-sdk/react: ^3.0.41`. Your `packages/ai` is on `ai: ^7.0.47` and `@ai-sdk/react: ^4.0.50` — both *ahead* of the supported range, and `^6` excludes `7.x`. Components import `ToolUIPart`, `DynamicToolUIPart` and `ChatStatus` from `ai`, so those types may have moved. Worth a spike before building on it.

Also note the docs' own list is out of date relative to what ships: `Response` → `MessageResponse`, `Actions` → `MessageActions`, `Branch` → `MessageBranch`, and `Loader` is gone in favour of `shimmer`.

## The citation mechanism — this is the key technical move

The docs are candid that inline citations aren't solved:

> "Currently, there is no official support for inline citations with Streamdown or the Response component… There isn't any good markdown syntax for inline citations… The AI SDK doesn't have built-in support for inline citations."

Their documented workaround is `streamObject` with a Zod schema — which costs you token-by-token streaming. **There's a better path that keeps both.** Streamdown v2 (which `MessageResponse` wraps) supports custom tag allowlisting:

```tsx
<Streamdown
  allowedTags={{ fact: ["id"] }}
  components={{ fact: ({ id, children }) => <FactCitation factId={id}>{children}</FactCitation> }}
>
```

So: system-prompt the model to emit `<fact id="...">…</fact>` around every claim, allowlist the tag, and map it onto `InlineCitation` resolved against your `facts` collection. You keep true streaming *and* get per-claim provenance back to a specific fact `_id`. Without `allowedTags` the tags are stripped by sanitisation, so this is opt-in and safe by default.

That directly implements gbrain's "cite every substantive claim, never fabricate slugs" discipline, and it's what makes `t.judge.autoevals.closedQA("cites a source")` a meaningful eval rather than a vibe check.

## Chat SDK — via eve's channel, and it lands on an endpoint you already have

eve ships `chatSdkChannel` bridging any Vercel Chat SDK adapter. The detail that matters: **you can pin an adapter's webhook path exactly.**

```ts
export const { bot, channel, send } = chatSdkChannel({
  adapters: { resend: createResendAdapter({ fromAddress: "brain@…" }) },
  state: createRedisState(),
  routes: { resend: "/webhooks/inbound-email" },   // your existing path
  streaming: false,                                 // email = one message per turn
});
```

That maps onto your existing `apps/api/app/webhooks/inbound-email/route.ts` without changing anything at Resend. And it fixes the bug I found earlier for free — the adapter owns webhook verification and inbound dedup, so the raw `From`-header parsing that's currently dropping every display-name email stops being your code.

HITL prompts render as Chat SDK Cards with buttons, and button clicks resume the parked session automatically. **Your review queue becomes a Slack message with Approve/Discard buttons.**

# 4. What to implement — sequenced

## Phase 0 — the two questions that gate everything

1. **Ask Vercel where Vercel Workflow stores durable session state, in which region, and how to delete it.** eve's docs have no answer: zero hits across 79 files for `region|residenc|GDPR`, and no session-delete route anywhere. A session transcript containing a voice memo about a named person *is* personal data.
2. **Decide the eve bet.** v0.29.5, 88 releases, `@workflow/core` vendored at `5.0.0-beta.38`. The durability substrate is a beta and eve is coupled to its protocol version.

## Phase 1 — close the residency gap (independent of eve; do this regardless)

- Add `inferenceRegion: { scope: 'zone', geoRegion: 'eu' }` to `createGatewayGenerate` and **move off DeepSeek** to an EU-capable model. This is a one-file change in `packages/knowledge/gateway.ts` and it closes a live exposure.
- Add an Atlas Resource Policy pinning cluster regions to EU; confirm Native Reranking is disabled at the project level.
- Write down the rule: never `type: "autoEmbed"`, never `$rerank`.

## Phase 2 — the corrections from the earlier review, unchanged

These stand on their own and don't depend on the framework decision:

1. **The consolidation anchor-narrowing leak** — union parent anchors into merged drafts, add a bounded `derivedFrom` fixpoint to `erasePerson`, run `buildRedactor` over `facts.text`, assert post-erasure referential integrity. Still the highest-severity item.
2. **Write `validFrom`/`validUntil`**, split `occurredAt` from `capturedAt`, emit audit rows on supersession.
3. **Scoped NLI contradiction pre-filter** — same anchor *and* same category, since consolidation structurally cannot find contradictions today.
4. **Make `confidence` load-bearing** via `$score`, with the provenance cap `r = min(channel_tier, content_confidence)`.

## Phase 3 — the read path

`$vectorSearch` + `$search` → `$rankFusion` → `$score` (confidence × recency × source tier) → Bedrock `cohere.rerank-v3-5:0` in Frankfurt → dossier assembly. Retrieve facts **and** source chunks — Engram's measured result was that facts-only loses recall.

## Phase 4 — the surface

`withEve(nextConfig)` mounts the agent inside `apps/app`, single Vercel project. AI Elements for the chat UI with the `<fact id>` citation mechanism. Chat SDK channel for Slack review + the existing Resend inbound path. Your `resolveProposalItems` becomes a tool with an `approval` policy; the nightly consolidation becomes a handler-form `defineSchedule` (handler form, because markdown task-mode cannot park for HITL) — remembering Vercel evaluates cron in **UTC**, so your 03:00 CEST job is `0 1 * * *`.

## Phase 5 — evals

`evals/*.eval.ts` with `t.succeeded()`, `t.calledTool()`, `t.check(t.reply, includes(...))`, and `t.judge.autoevals.closedQA("cites a source")`. Dataset fan-out over a YAML fixture gives you the 100-case golden set. `eve eval --strict --junit` in CI.

Note the cost shape: **evals run against a live model** — there's no documented way to mock the model of the agent under test from inside an eval, since `mockModel` lives in `agent.ts` and is a fixture-agent tool.

---

**Three settings to change on day one if you do adopt eve**, all defaults that leak content: `recordInputs: false` and `recordOutputs: false` in `instrumentation.ts` (both default `true` — full message history on every span), and `EVE_TRACES_CONTENT=off`. Note that `$eve.title` still writes a truncated first user message into Vercel Workflow run metadata and is explicitly not configurable.

And one design rule that falls out of everything above: **keep every fact, source and proposal in your EU MongoDB behind authored tools, and treat eve sessions as disposable compute.** Don't put durable knowledge in `defineState` — it's session-scoped, has no tenant dimension, can't be queried from your Next.js app or a Mongo aggregation, and has no deletion API.

# EU-resident embeddings + reranker: provider survey (verified 2026-08-03)

## TL;DR — the shortlist

| Rank | Option | Embeddings | Cross-encoder reranker | Residency strength |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **IONOS AI Model Hub** (Berlin, DE) | `BAAI/bge-m3` 1024d/8k, `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B` 4096d/32k | ✅ **`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B`** 32k, true cross-attention | German DC, stateless, no logging. Best German-native self-serve. |
| **2** | **AWS Bedrock `eu-central-1`** (Frankfurt) | `cohere.embed-multilingual-v3` 1024d/**512tok** In-Region | ✅ **`cohere.rerank-v3-5:0`** In-Region only | Hardest guarantee: Geo & Global routing *not supported* for these models. ZDR+ZOA by default. |
| **3** | **HF Inference Endpoints `eu-west-1`** + TEI | `BAAI/bge-m3` (self-served) | ✅ `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` via TEI `/rerank` | Container pinned to Ireland; control plane/logs undocumented (likely US). ~€390–730/mo. |
| **4** | **Fireworks `EU_FRANKFURT_1`** | `qwen3-embedding-8b` | ✅ `qwen3-reranker-8b` | Explicit region pin, on-demand only. ZDR default. |
| — | **Mistral La Plateforme EU** | `mistral-embed` 1024d | ❌ **no reranker at all** | Good, but no rerank story. |

**Best German embeddings:** `Qwen3-Embedding-8B` (Scaleway/OVH/IONOS/Fireworks/Nebius — Matryoshka 32–4096, 32k ctx) or `BAAI/bge-m3` (1024d, 8k ctx, 100+ langs, cheapest at OVH €0.01/M).
**Best EU reranker:** IONOS `Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B` (self-serve, Berlin, 32k ctx) or Bedrock `cohere.rerank-v3-5:0` (Frankfurt, In-Region-only).

---

## 1. Mistral AI (La Plateforme, Paris)

**(a) Embeddings** — `mistral-embed`: 1024 dims, fixed [V [docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/knowledge-rag/embeddings/text_embeddings)]. `codestral-embed` (v25.05): up to **3072 dims** (default 1536), `output_dimension` + `output_dtype` params, Matryoshka-ordered, **8192 ctx** [V [docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/embeddings/code_embeddings)]. `mistral-embed` max context not stated in docs — INFERRED 8k. Multilingual quality not benchmarked publicly.

**(b) Reranker — NONE.** API reference lists chat, fim, embeddings, classifiers, files, models, batch, ocr, audio, events, workflows, beta agents/RAG. **No `/v1/rerank`** [V [docs.mistral.ai/api](https://docs.mistral.ai/api/)].

**(c) Residency** — Regional endpoint **`api.eu.mistral.ai`** [V [docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/regional-inference)]: *"Multiple data centers in EU/EFTA countries"*, *"Inference occurs within that region, and processed data doesn't leave it."* **+10% price upcharge.** Only Function Calling supported; **Agents, Batch, Files API unavailable** on regional endpoints. `api.us.mistral.ai` "coming soon".
⚠️ Two flags: (1) **"EU/EFTA"** includes Switzerland/Norway/Iceland — not EU-member-states-only. (2) *"Regional endpoints only serve models hosted in that region"* — **you must call `models.list()` against `api.eu.mistral.ai` to confirm `mistral-embed` is actually served there.** Not verifiable without a key.
Data not used for training unless opt-in; ~30 rolling days abuse retention; ZDR option exists [INFERRED, help-center index only].

**(d) Legal** — DPA at [legal.mistral.ai](https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/data-processing-addendum): French law, but **explicitly authorizes transfers to "Restricted Countries" under SCCs Module 4** [V]. SOC 2 Type II + ISO 27001/27701 [V [help.mistral.ai](https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347638-do-you-have-soc-2-or-iso-27001-certification)]. DCs: Bruyères-le-Châtel (FR, live Q2 2026), Borlänge (SE, 2027).

**(e) Pricing** — `mistral-embed` **$0.10/1M**, `codestral-embed` **$0.15/1M** [V [pricing/api](https://mistral.ai/pricing/api)]; +10% on the EU endpoint.

**Mistral on Azure/Bedrock EU: chat models only. `mistral-embed` is NOT available on either** [V — absent from both catalogs].

---

## 2. Aleph Alpha (Heidelberg) — ⚠️ **now part of Cohere**

**Merged with Cohere, announced 2026-04-24.** Cohere shareholders ~90%; dual HQ Toronto + Heidelberg; **Schwarz Group $600M into Series E**; sovereign offering to run on **STACKIT** [V [cohere.com/blog/cohere-alephalpha-join-forces](https://cohere.com/blog/cohere-alephalpha-join-forces), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/24/cohere-aleph-alpha-germany-ai-europe-expansion.html)]. This makes items 2 and 11 the same vendor now.

- **Embeddings:** `Pharia-1-Embedding-4608-control` — **4608 dims**, built on Pharia-1-LLM-7B-control, instruction-tunable, strong cross-lingual DE/EN/FR/ES [V [HF card](https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Pharia-1-Embedding-4608-control)]. Endpoints `/semantic_embed`, `/instructable_embed`; `/embeddings` (OpenAI-compatible) for any HF model on a vLLM worker.
- **Reranker:** ✅ `/rerank` endpoint, **but no native Aleph Alpha cross-encoder** — you deploy an HF model on a vLLM worker with `task="score"`. Documented example: **`bge-reranker-v2-m3`**. Endpoint is **compatible with both Jina and Cohere clients** [V [admin guide](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-admin-guide/latest/pharia-inference/rerank.html)].
- **Residency:** this is a **deployment platform, not a hosted API** — full weights + inference runtime shipped, run on-prem/air-gapped or in your cloud. PhariaAI-as-a-Service on STACKIT (German, Schwarz Group). Maximum sovereignty, maximum ops burden.
- **Pricing:** enterprise/sales-gated. ~$30/M in, $33/M out cited by third parties [INFERRED].

## 3. IONOS AI Model Hub (Berlin, Germany) — **best German self-serve option**

Endpoint: `https://openai.inference.de-txl.ionos.com/v1/{embeddings,rerank}` [V [how-tos](https://docs.ionos.com/cloud/ai/ai-model-hub/how-tos/reranking)].

**(a) Embeddings** [V [models-comparison](https://docs.ionos.com/cloud/ai/ai-model-hub/models/models-comparison), [embedding-models](https://docs.ionos.com/cloud/ai/ai-model-hub/models/embedding-models)]:

| Model ID | Dims | Max input | Languages |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BAAI/bge-m3` | 1024 | **8192** | 100+ |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B` | **4096** | **32768** | 30+, multimodal |
| `BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5` | 1024 | 8192 | English only |
| `sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2` | 768 | **128 tokens** ⚠️ | multilingual |

**(b) Reranker** ✅ **`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B`** — genuine **cross-encoder with cross-attention**, **32,768 ctx**, 30+ languages, multimodal, live since **2026-05-12** [V [model page](https://docs.ionos.com/cloud/ai/ai-model-hub/models/reranking-models/qwen3-vl-reranker-8b)].

**(c) Residency** [V [data-handling](https://docs.ionos.com/cloud/ai/ai-model-hub/governance-and-compliance/data-handling)] — *"Securely stored in a database in our **Berlin data center**"*; *"AI Model Hub operates as a **stateless service, discarding user prompts and outputs at the end of each session**"*; *"Your interactions remain private, **free from logging, recording, or reuse for model training**."*

**(d) Certs** — IONOS Cloud: **BSI C5:2020 Type 1** (33 services / 10 clusters, attested **2026-05-28**, PwC per ISAE 3000), **ISO 27001 on IT-Grundschutz basis** (Frankfurt + Berlin DCs, valid to 2028-09-13), ISO 50001 [V [cloud.ionos.de/zertifikate](https://cloud.ionos.de/zertifikate)]. ⚠️ **Whether AI Model Hub sits inside the C5 scope is not publicly published** — the 2023 attestation covered only Compute Engine / Cloud Cubes / S3. **Ask IONOS for the scope list.**

## 4. Scaleway Generative APIs (Paris) — ⚠️ "rerank" is not a cross-encoder

**(a) Embeddings** [V [supported-models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/reference-content/supported-models/), [pricing](https://www.scaleway.com/en/pricing/model-as-a-service/)]:

Scaleway itself recommends doing the similarity in your vector DB instead [V [query-reranking-models](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/generative-apis/how-to/query-reranking-models/)]. Open feature requests for `Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-8B` and `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-gemma` confirm real cross-encoders haven't shipped [V [feature-request #1256](https://feature-request.scaleway.com/posts/1256/generative-api-for-qwen-qwen3-reranker-8b)].

## 7. Hugging Face — dedicated endpoints OK, routing NOT OK

**Regions: exactly ONE EU region exists — `AWS eu-west-1` (Ireland).** No eu-central-1, no Azure EU, no GCP EU. [V live catalog `api.endpoints.huggingface.cloud/v2/provider` + [FAQ](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-endpoints/en/faq)] — your Frankfurt/Azure-EU hypotheses are false.

**eu-west-1 instances** [V [pricing](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-endpoints/en/pricing)]: CPU x1–x16 **$0.033–$0.536/hr**; `nvidia-t4-x1` **$0.50/hr**; `nvidia-a10g-x1` **$1.00/hr**. **No L4/L40S/A100/H200/Inferentia in Ireland** (7 computes vs 20 in us-east-1). Billed **per minute**; scale-to-zero supported.

content.text:
A late sub-agent from the retrieval research just landed with the full EU provider survey. It refines my Section 2 recommendation in one materially important way.

## Correction: I under-specified the Bedrock embedding option

I recommended `cohere.embed-multilingual-v3` without flagging that it has a **512-token input cap**. For German meeting transcripts and forwarded email threads that forces aggressive chunking — a real cost I should have surfaced. The alternative in Frankfurt, `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`, is documented as *"optimized for English"* with *"sub-optimal"* cross-language performance, which is the wrong trade for a German product.

Also worth checking before you budget: the live AWS Price List API shows `titan-embed-text-v2` at **$0.20/1M in `eu-central-1` versus $0.026 in `eu-west-1`** — a 10× outlier matching the legacy Titan G1 rate. That reads like an unrepriced SKU rather than real pricing.

## IONOS is now the stronger primary recommendation

Single vendor, Berlin data centre, and it beats Bedrock on both model specs:

| | IONOS | Bedrock `eu-central-1` |
|---|---|---|
| Embeddings | `BAAI/bge-m3` — 1024d, **8192 ctx**, 100+ langs | `cohere.embed-multilingual-v3` — 1024d, **512 ctx** |
| Reranker | `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B` — true cross-attention, **32k ctx** | `cohere.rerank-v3-5:0` — 4k ctx |

Their data-handling doc is unusually direct: *"AI Model Hub operates as a **stateless service, discarding user prompts and outputs at the end of each session**"* and *"free from logging, recording, or reuse for model training."* BSI C5:2020 Type 1 and ISO 27001 on IT-Grundschutz basis for the Berlin DC.

**Bedrock remains the stronger *contractual* guarantee**, and it's worth understanding why: both the embed and rerank models are **In-Region only — Geo and Global inference profiles are explicitly "Not supported"**, so there is no routing path out of Frankfurt even by misconfiguration. ZDR and zero-operator-access are on by default with no application process (contrast Azure, where the abuse-monitoring opt-out is gated to "managed customers and partners"), and the Model Deployment Account means Cohere itself never sees your data. CloudTrail's `additionalEventData.inferenceRegion` gives you audit evidence.

So: **IONOS if you optimise for German sovereignty and model quality, Bedrock if you optimise for demonstrable contractual control.** Either works; they're different kinds of strong.

## Four options I'd now rule out explicitly

- **Jina** — despite the Berlin GmbH. The documented EU hostnames (`eu.r.jina.ai`, `eu.s.jina.ai`) **return NXDOMAIN** as of today, `api.jina.ai` resolves to a GCP backend with the region undisclosed, and no sub-processor list is published. It was acquired by Elastic in Oct 2025, and every current model is CC-BY-NC-4.0 — so you can't self-host as a fallback either. (Elastic Inference Service in `eu-central-1` is a legitimate path, but it does *proximity* routing, not a contractual pin.)
- **Scaleway's `/v1/rerank`** — not a cross-encoder. Their own docs say the embedding and reranking APIs are *"functionally equivalent"* because scores are cosine similarity of normalised vectors, and they recommend doing it in your vector DB instead.
- **Mistral** — no reranker endpoint at all. Their regional endpoint is also "EU/EFTA", which includes Switzerland, Norway and Iceland rather than EU member states only.
- **Together** — its only serverless embedding model has a **514-token** context.

One strategic note worth your attention: **Aleph Alpha merged with Cohere in April 2026**, with Schwarz Group investing $600M and **STACKIT** (German, Schwarz-owned) as the sovereign hosting backbone. Not purchasable as a product today, but for a German buyer with your posture that's the most relevant development in this space and probably worth a sales conversation.

## Questions to put to vendors before committing

- **IONOS** — list price per 1M tokens (not published anywhere), and confirmation that AI Model Hub is inside the C5 services-in-scope list. The 2023 attestation covered only Compute Engine, Cloud Cubes and S3.
- **AWS** — is `eu-central-1` inside the Bedrock C5 attestation, and is that $0.20/1M Frankfurt Titan rate real?
- **Vercel** — the Workflow residency and deletion question from the eve section. Still the one that gates the most.

Nothing else in the plan changes. Phase 1 is unaffected and still worth doing first: `inferenceRegion: { scope: 'zone', geoRegion: 'eu' }` plus moving off DeepSeek closes a live exposure regardless of which retrieval vendor you pick.

### vLLM
**VERIFIED** — vLLM exposes `/score`, `/v1/score` and Cohere-compatible `/rerank`, `/v1/rerank`, `/v2/rerank`. Any `*For*Classification` with `num_labels == 1` works as a scoring model, and `--convert classify` converts LM-head models. Score types: cross-encoder (linear classifier), bi-encoder (cosine), late-interaction (MaxSim).

| Model | vLLM |
|---|---|
| `bge-reranker-v2-m3` | ✅ `LLM(model="BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3", task="score")` |
| `Qwen3-Reranker-*` | ✅ vLLM ≥0.8.5, yes/no logit extraction (documented on the model card) |
| `mxbai-rerank-v2` | ✅ Qwen2 causal LM |
| `llama-nemotron-rerank-1b-v2` | ✅ **vLLM ≥ v0.14.0**, requires a score template via `--chat-template` |
| `ctxl-rerank-v2` | ✅ vLLM ≥0.8.5 (but NC license) |
| `LAMAR-600m` / `gte-multilingual-reranker-base` | ✅ INFERRED (seq-cls, num_labels=1) |

**Practical implication:** if you want the simplest ops story (one small Rust binary, no CUDA graph warmup, trivial autoscaling), TEI + `bge-reranker-v2-m3` or `gte-multilingual-reranker-base` is the path. Every Qwen3-based reranker forces you onto vLLM.

## 7. Latency / throughput

**VERIFIED primary source** — [mxbai-rerank-large-v2 card](https://huggingface.co/mixedbread-ai/mxbai-rerank-large-v2), A100, NFCorpus, per-query:

| Model | Params | Latency |
|---|---|---|
| mxbai-rerank-base-v2 | 0.5B | **0.67 s** |
| mxbai-rerank-large-v2 | 1.5B | **0.89 s** |
| mxbai-rerank-large-v1 | 0.4B (encoder) | 2.24 s |
| `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-gemma` | 2.5B | **7.20 s** (8× slower than mxbai-large-v2) |

**SECONDARY source, treat as INFERRED** — [Spheron TEI guide](https://www.spheron.network/blog/self-host-embedding-reranker-tei-gpu-cloud/), TEI 1.9 + FA2, A100 80GB PCIe, batch=64: bge-reranker-v2-m3 ~800 pairs/s, Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B ~700 pairs/s, jina-reranker-v2 ~600 pairs/s; 15–30 ms per pair; full two-stage pipeline p50 30–80 ms.

**My grounded estimate for your workload (20–50 passages × ~512 tok, single modern GPU) — INFERRED:**

| Class | Example | 50 passages @ 512 tok |
|---|---|---|
| 300M encoder cross-encoder | `gte-multilingual-reranker-base` | **~15–30 ms** on A100/L40S; runs acceptably on **CPU** (~0.5–1.5 s) for low QPS |
| 570M encoder cross-encoder | `bge-reranker-v2-m3`, `LAMAR-600m` | **~30–60 ms** on A100/L40S. One forward pass over 50×512 = 25.6k tokens, no KV cache, fully parallel. |
| 0.6B LLM scorer | `Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B` | **~60–150 ms** — same param count but decoder prefill + chat-template overhead (instruction prompt adds ~50–80 tok/pair) + vLLM scheduling |
| 1–1.5B | `llama-nemotron-rerank-1b-v2`, `mxbai-large-v2` | **~150–400 ms** |
| 4B LLM scorer | `Qwen3-Reranker-4B` | **~0.7–1.5 s** — roughly **20–40× the 300M encoder**. Needs ~8–9 GB VRAM at bf16 just for weights. |
| 4B listwise / generative | LightOn-rerank-2B | **~45 s/query at rerank-100** (VERIFIED from LightOn blog). Not viable interactively. |

Rule of thumb: cross-encoder cost scales ~linearly in params **and** you pay a fixed instruction-prompt tax on every LLM-based reranker. KaLM's paper quantifies this as **6.9× vs 42.4×** relative online compute (KaLM-Small vs Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B).

## 10. Concrete recommendation

1. **Ship `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` on TEI now.** Apache-2.0, zero legal ambiguity, best-documented ops path, +6.0 nDCG@10 German lift over dense retrieval when candidates come from a matched retriever. Chunk to ≤1024 tokens.
2. **Build a German eval set from your own corpus before anything else.** The CheckThat! 2026 result — where bge-v2-m3 pushed German MRR@5 *below* the no-rerank baseline (0.4866 vs 0.5974) — is the strongest signal in this whole report. Public multilingual averages will not predict your domain.
3. **A/B `nlpai-lab/LAMAR-600m` against it.** It is a literal drop-in (same arch, same param count, same tokenizer, same 8194 positions, MIT license), +0.3 MIRACL-de, and **+12 points of language coherence** (96.9 vs 84.7 XQuAD nDCG@1) — which matters a lot for a German company brain with mixed DE/EN documents. Risk: released 2026-07-27, 363 downloads.
4. **Only reach for `Qwen3-Reranker-4B` if your corpus is German-monolingual.** It wins MIRACL-de (59.5) but its 33.03 XQuAD language-coherence score means it will systematically prefer English near-duplicates. Also costs ~20–40× the compute and forces vLLM.
5. **Get legal to look at `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-1b-v2`.** It is the best-balanced model in the whole survey — top MMTEB reranking average (86.82), German explicitly in its 26 eval languages, real bidirectional cross-encoder, 8192 ctx, near-top language coherence. NVIDIA Open Model License + Llama 3.2 Community License permit commercial use, but that's a lawyer call, not an engineering one.
6. **Do not spend time on:** any Jina model, ContextualAI ctxl-rerank-v2, EuroBERT/mmBERT rerankers (they don't exist at production quality), German-specific 2022-era cross-encoders, or a bge-reranker-v3 (BAAI hasn't shipped a reranker since July 2024).

### A4. License landmines (all VERIFIED by reading the actual license files)

- **`tencent/KaLM-Embedding-Gemma3-12B-2511` — the #1 model on MMTEB (72.32) is legally unusable for you.** Its `LICENSE.txt` clause 1 reads verbatim: *"KaLM-Embedding IS NOT INTENDED FOR USE WITHIN THE EUROPEAN UNION."* Hard stop for a German product.
- **Every current Jina text model is CC-BY-NC-4.0** (v3, v4 under Qwen Research, v5 nano/small, all rerankers). Elastic completed the Jina AI acquisition in Oct 2025; commercial waivers now route through Elastic sales. Jina being Berlin-based doesn't help — geography isn't the problem, licensing is. Sole exception: `jinaai/jina-embeddings-v2-base-de` (161M, 768d, 8192 ctx) is **Apache-2.0**.
- **`OpenMDW-1.1`** (Nemotron-3-Embed) is a Linux Foundation permissive model license released 2026-05-28: unrestricted royalty-free use, **no field-of-use restrictions, no separate commercial license**. Cleanest of the "non-Apache" options. Base is Ministral-3 (Apache-2.0). Card says verbatim "ready for commercial use."
- **`google/embeddinggemma-300m`** is under Gemma Terms — commercial OK but not OSI, HF-gated, Google reserves a remote-restriction right, and redistribution obligations flow down. Also only **2048 token context**.
- **`nvidia/llama-embed-nemotron-8b`** (the model some blogs tout as "#1 multilingual, fully open") is **research/non-commercial only**. Don't confuse it with Nemotron-3-Embed.

### B3. The finding that should actually drive your choice — **language coherence**

Same source, XQuAD/BELEBELE parallel-document sets: *does the reranker put the document in the query's language first?* Directly relevant to a German company brain that inevitably mixes German notes with English product docs / Slack / vendor PDFs. nDCG@1:

## C) Serving

- **TEI v1.9.3** (2026-03-23, **Apache-2.0** — the HFOIL scare was TGI, not TEI). Supports XLM-R/BERT/GTE/ModernBERT/JinaBERT/Nomic/Qwen2/**Qwen3**/**Gemma3**, `/embed` + `/rerank` + `/v1/embeddings`, `dimensions` param for MRL, ONNX (`ort`) compiled into the CPU image, Prometheus + OTLP + `--api-key`. Images: `:89-1.9` (L4/L40S/4090), `:86-1.9` (A10G), `:cpu-1.9`. `brew install text-embeddings-inference` gives a Metal build for local dev.
  - **TEI does NOT support Qwen3-Reranker** (`Qwen3ForSequenceClassification`) — 14 open issues, still unresolved. TEI rerankers are limited to CamemBERT/RoBERTa/XLM-R/GTE/ModernBERT seq-cls heads.
  - TEI likely does *not* support Nemotron-3-Embed either (custom `Ministral3Model` arch) — NVIDIA's card recommends sentence-transformers or **vLLM ≥0.25.0**. INFERRED but consistent with the arch list.
- **vLLM v0.26.0** (2026-07-27). `--task` is gone → `--runner pooling` + `--convert {embed,classify}`; the `score` task was removed in v0.21. Endpoints: `/v1/embeddings`, **`/v2/embed`** (Cohere-compatible, has `output_dimension` for MRL), `/score`, `/rerank`, `/v1/rerank`, `/v2/rerank`. Supports bge-m3, EmbeddingGemma, gte-multilingual-base, Qwen3-Embedding, Qwen3-Reranker, mxbai-rerank-v2, bge-reranker-v2-m3/gemma, llama-nemotron-rerank. Several rerankers need a jinja score template (`examples/pooling/score/template/`). vLLM's own docs warn pooling models are supported "for convenience," not speed — treat it as the coverage engine.
- **Infinity** (MIT) is effectively in maintenance mode: last release 0.0.77 (2025-08-22), ~4 commits in 10 months, and its author is now landing perf PRs in TEI. Don't start new work on it.

**VRAM (fp16 weights + slack, INFERRED arithmetic):** 0.3B ≈ 1.5–2.5 GB · 0.6B ≈ 2.5–4 GB · 1B ≈ 4–6 GB · 4B ≈ 10–13 GB · 8B ≈ 18–22 GB. An **L4 (24 GB)** hosts a 1B embedder + a 568M reranker comfortably; **L40S (48 GB)** hosts an 8B embedder + reranker co-resident. Long context is the killer: Qwen3-8B KV cache is ~144 KiB/token → 1.13 GiB per 8k sequence, so batching 8k inputs on a 24 GB card OOMs. TEI's `--max-batch-tokens` (default 16384) is the real dial.

**Latency for your critical path (rerank 20–50 passages @ ~512 tok, single L4/A10G):**
- 306M encoder (`gte-multilingual-reranker-base`): **~15–60 ms**
- 568M encoder (`bge-reranker-v2-m3`, `LAMAR-600m`): **~30–100 ms** ← plan around this
- 1–1.5B: ~150–400 ms
- 4B LLM scorer (Qwen3-Reranker-4B): **~0.7–1.5 s** — not viable interactively
- Full two-stage budget: query embed 5–15 ms + Atlas ANN 5–30 ms + rerank 40–100 ms ≈ **60–150 ms** pre-LLM
- **CPU cross-encoding 50×512 tokens is 5–20 s. Never put a cross-encoder on CPU in the request path.** CPU int8 ONNX embedding is fine for batch indexing (~3–10 docs/s at 512 tok for a 560M model on 8 VNNI vCPUs).

**EU-hosted managed options** (if you don't want GPUs): **IONOS AI Model Hub** (Berlin, `openai.inference.de-txl.ionos.com`) is the only EU-native provider with both embeddings *and* a genuine cross-encoder rerank endpoint — bge-m3 at $0.02/M tokens, `REDACTED` at $0.045/M. **Scaleway's `/v1/rerank` is not a cross-encoder** — their docs admit it returns cosine similarity from a bi-encoder, i.e. zero lift over doing the dot product yourself. **OVHcloud has no reranker at all** (roadmap issue #1140, open since 2026-04-22, no response). STACKIT (Schwarz Group, `eu01`, German DCs only) and T-Systems LLMHub (hosts `jina-embeddings-v2-base-de` on T-Cloud DE) are embeddings-only. Note: **Aleph Alpha was acquired by Cohere (Canada) on 2026-04-24** — recheck the controller chain before using them as your "German sovereign" story.

---

## D) MongoDB Atlas Vector Search — your 4096 assumption is stale

**The max is 8192 dimensions, not 4096.** VERIFIED: *"You must specify a value less than or equal to `8192`"* — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/index/vector-search-type.md. Raised in the 30 March 2025 release. (Note the docs moved: `/docs/atlas/atlas-vector-search/*` now 404s; canonical is `/docs/vector-search/*`, with clean markdown at `<url>.md`.)

- **Every model above fits**, including harrier-27b at 5376 and Qwen3-8B/Nemotron-8B at 4096. The 8192 ceiling applies identically to `none`, `scalar`, and `binary` quantization.
- **Quantization:** `"quantization": "none" | "scalar" | "binary"`. RAM reduction **3.75x scalar / 24x binary** (vectors shrink 4x/32x; the HNSW graph doesn't). Binary requires `numDimensions` be a **multiple of 8** and uses rescoring against full-fidelity floats kept on disk. Storage:RAM ≈ 4:1 scalar, 24:1 binary.
- **Dimension guidance:** *"We recommend over 1024 dimensions when running larger workloads with quantization."* At 5.5M docs, 256d never exceeds 70% recall and 512d never exceeds 80%. So **don't MRL-truncate below 1024** — which rules out truncating Nemotron-1B to 512, and makes 2048d (Nemotron-1B native) or 2560d (Qwen3-4B) the sweet spot.
- **Data types:** BSON `double`, or `binData` subtype `float32`/`int8`/`int1`. Pre-converting to `binData float32` cuts `mongod` disk ~66%. `int1` is euclidean-only.
- **Other limits:** `numCandidates` ≤ 10000 (recommend ≥20x `limit`); 2500 search indexes/cluster hard cap; 2.1B index objects per shard; `$vectorSearch` must be the first pipeline stage; `indexingMethod: "flat"` added in preview 2026-04-07.
- **Hybrid search:** **`$rankFusion`** (RRF) requires MongoDB **8.0+**; **`$scoreFusion`** requires **8.3+**; a native **`$rerank`** stage landed in Preview 2026-06-30 but only wraps **Voyage AI** rerankers, requires 8.3+, caps at `numDocsToRerank ≤ 1000`, runs off-cluster and bills separately — so it does not fit a self-hosted German model. Use `$rankFusion` + your own reranker.
- **EU:** Search Nodes are supported on AWS `eu-central-1` (Frankfurt), `eu-west-1`, `eu-north-1`, `eu-central-2`, `eu-west-2`, `eu-south-2` (**not** Paris or Milan), and on Azure `germanywestcentral` (**not** `germanynorth`). GCP: all regions. **There is no EU-sovereign Atlas offering** — only data residency + Atlas Resource Policies. MongoDB Inc. is US-incorporated with a US control plane, so Frankfurt residency ≠ CLOUD Act immunity (INFERRED from third-party analysis, not a MongoDB statement).

---

## Recommendation

**Embedding: `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16`** (1.14B, **2048d**, 32k ctx, OpenMDW-1.1, `query: ` / `passage: ` prefixes) served on vLLM. It scores 83.16 on RTEB(deu) — above Qwen3-Embedding-4B's 83.93 within noise, above every Apache model under 4B, above jina-v4, and it *tops* both GermanDPR (85.50) and GermanQuAD-Retrieval (97.12) outright. 2048d is right in Atlas's quantization sweet spot. Upgrade path to `Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16` (4096d, 88.04) if quality matters more than the GPU bill.

**If you need Apache-2.0 with no license conversation at all: `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B`** (2560d, 83.93) — or `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` (1024d, 76.16) if you're CPU/edge-constrained, though that's a real 8-point drop.

**Reranker: `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` on TEI**, chunked to ≤1024 tokens. It's the only strong multilingual cross-encoder with first-class TEI support, Apache-2.0, 19M downloads. **A/B `nlpai-lab/LAMAR-600m` against it immediately** — identical XLM-R arch and param count (567,755,777 both), MIT, +12 points language coherence. Risk: released 2026-07-21, only 363 downloads.

**Do not use Qwen3-Reranker-4B** unless your corpus is German-monolingual — the 33.03 XQuAD coherence score is a product bug waiting to happen, plus it forces vLLM and costs 20–40x the compute.

**Two things to do before committing:**
1. **Build a German eval set from your own corpus.** The CheckThat! 2026 result — bge-reranker-v2-m3 pushing German MRR@5 *below* the no-rerank baseline — is the single strongest signal in this report. Public averages will not predict your domain.
2. **Go hybrid.** BM25 beats every dense model by 40% on GerDaLIR. German compound nouns, internal jargon, and product identifiers are exactly what dense embeddings lose. `$rankFusion` (MongoDB 8.0+) over `$search` + `$vectorSearch`, then your cross-encoder on the fused top-30.</result>

## C) Serving

- **TEI v1.9.3** (2026-03-23, **Apache-2.0** — the HFOIL scare was TGI, not TEI). Supports XLM-R/BERT/GTE/ModernBERT/JinaBERT/Nomic/Qwen2/**Qwen3**/**Gemma3**, `/embed` + `/rerank` + `/v1/embeddings`, `dimensions` param for MRL, ONNX (`ort`) compiled into the CPU image, Prometheus + OTLP + `--api-key`. Images: `:89-1.9` (L4/L40S/4090), `:86-1.9` (A10G), `:cpu-1.9`. `brew install text-embeddings-inference` gives a Metal build for local dev.
  - **TEI does NOT support Qwen3-Reranker** (`Qwen3ForSequenceClassification`) — 14 open issues, still unresolved. TEI rerankers are limited to CamemBERT/RoBERTa/XLM-R/GTE/ModernBERT seq-cls heads.
  - TEI likely does *not* support Nemotron-3-Embed either (custom `Ministral3Model` arch) — NVIDIA's card recommends sentence-transformers or **vLLM ≥0.25.0**. INFERRED but consistent with the arch list.
- **vLLM v0.26.0** (2026-07-27). `--task` is gone → `--runner pooling` + `--convert {embed,classify}`; the `score` task was removed in v0.21. Endpoints: `/v1/embeddings`, **`/v2/embed`** (Cohere-compatible, has `output_dimension` for MRL), `/score`, `/rerank`, `/v1/rerank`, `/v2/rerank`. Supports bge-m3, EmbeddingGemma, gte-multilingual-base, Qwen3-Embedding, Qwen3-Reranker, mxbai-rerank-v2, bge-reranker-v2-m3/gemma, llama-nemotron-rerank. On **GerDaLIR** (German legal retrieval), BM25 scores **41.80 and beats every dense model** — the best dense result is 29.52. That's lexical search winning by 40%.
